21.name: Fonds 21
21.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht set up in 1998 by SNS REAAL, independent since that group's nationalisation in 2013.
21.money: Stichting Beheer SNS REAAL supplies its budget, €12 million in donations for 2026.
21.arts: It funds art, culture and education projects for young people aged 12 to 30.

aatoserkko.name: Jane and Aatos Erkko Foundation
aatoserkko.what: A private Finnish foundation set up in Helsinki in 2002 by the newspaper publisher Aatos Erkko and his wife Jane, mainly to fund research in technology, economics and medicine.
aatoserkko.money: Returns on Sanoma shares Aatos Erkko left it in 2012, worth about 700 million euros, which made it Sanoma's largest shareholder.
aatoserkko.arts: It also supports arts and culture, and gave grants of 45.2 million euros across all its fields in 2020.

aatoserkkopayingforballetsyouthcompany.name: Jane and Aatos Erkko Foundation
aatoserkkopayingforballetsyouthcompany.what: A private Finnish foundation set up in Helsinki in 2002 by the Sanoma owner and Helsingin Sanomat editor Aatos Erkko and his wife Jane to fund research, art and culture.
aatoserkkopayingforballetsyouthcompany.money: Aatos Erkko's fortune: on his death in 2012 he left it his Sanoma shares, which made it Sanoma's largest shareholder with 23%.
aatoserkkopayingforballetsyouthcompany.arts: It awarded €45.2 million in grants in 2020; on 1 October 2026 it announced over €7 million for medicine and the arts.

acenpo.name: Arts Council England
acenpo.what: A non-departmental public body and registered charity set up by Royal Charter in 1994, based in Manchester.
acenpo.money: Grant-in-aid from the UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport (£578.1 million) and National Lottery proceeds (£250.3 million) in 2024-25.
acenpo.arts: Its 2023-26 National Portfolio gives £446 million a year to 990 museums, libraries and arts organisations.
acenpo.address: The Hive, 49 Lever Street, Manchester M1 1FN

adjarastamba.name: Adjara Group
adjarastamba.what: A Georgian hospitality holding founded in Tbilisi in 2010 by the entrepreneur Temur Ugulava, who died in 2026; its brands include Rooms Hotels, Stamba and Fabrika.
adjarastamba.money: Revenue from its hotels, restaurants, bars, co-working offices and event spaces in Georgia; the group employs about 1,700 people.

aerok.name: Aero K
aerok.what: A South Korean low-cost airline founded on 18 May 2016, flying since April 2021 from Cheongju International Airport; its parent is Aero K Holdings (Daemyung Chemical).
aerok.money: Passenger fares on its scheduled routes from Cheongju, flown with a fleet of nine aircraft.

aesop.name: Aesop
aesop.what: An Australian cosmetics brand founded in 1987 by the hairdresser Dennis Paphitis in Armadale, Melbourne; headquartered in Collingwood, Victoria, and owned by L'Oréal since 2023.
aesop.money: Sales of its skincare, haircare and fragrance products, as a subsidiary of L'Oréal.

afac.name: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture
afac.what: An independent non-profit founded in 2007 by Arab cultural activists that gives grants to artists, writers, researchers and cultural groups across the Arab region; based in Beirut.
afac.money: Donations, mainly from businesspeople and organisations in the Arab region, plus individual Friends and partner foundations and companies.
afac.arts: From 2007 to 2021 it raised slightly more than US$47 million and gave almost US$36 million in grants.

afd.name: Agence française de développement
afd.what: A French public financial institution, founded by Charles de Gaulle in 1941 as the Caisse Centrale de la France Libre, that finances development projects for the French state.
afd.money: Bonds it issues on the capital markets fund its loans; six of its board members represent French ministries.

ag2rlamondiale.name: AG2R La Mondiale
ag2rlamondiale.what: A French social protection and insurance group run jointly by employers and unions and as a mutual; La Mondiale was founded in 1905 by seven northern industrialists.
ag2rlamondiale.money: Supplementary pensions, provident and health insurance, life insurance and savings: revenue of €13.1 billion in 2025.

agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.name: Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.what: A special body of Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, set up in 1968 to promote arts and culture, with its main offices in Kyoto since 2023.
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.money: Japan's national budget through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology; its budget was 107 billion yen in 2026.
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.arts: Its divisions protect the nation's cultural properties and oversee the Japan Arts Council.

ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.name: A. Ahlström Kiinteistöt Oy
ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.what: The real estate subsidiary of A. Ahlström Oy, a Finnish family investment company; it owns and maintains Villa Mairea and runs the Ahlström Estate in Noormarkku.
ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.money: Its parent's investments in industry, real estate and forest; the companies A. Ahlström owns had about EUR 5.5 billion of revenue in 2025.

aig.name: American International Group, Inc.
aig.what: An American multinational insurance company founded in Shanghai on 19 December 1919 by Cornelius Vander Starr, now headquartered in New York City.
aig.money: Premiums and investment income from commercial and personal property, casualty, liability and specialty insurance; revenue was US$26.77 billion in 2025.
aig.address: 1271 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10020

ajuntamentdebarcelona.name: Ajuntament de Barcelona
ajuntamentdebarcelona.what: The municipal government of Barcelona, elected every four years since 1979 and led by mayor Jaume Collboni; seated in the Casa de la Ciutat.
ajuntamentdebarcelona.money: The city's municipal budget: 4,180 million euros for 2026.

ako.name: AKO Foundation
ako.what: A London charitable foundation set up in 2013 by Nicolai Tangen, founder of the hedge fund AKO Capital, who left its board in 2020.
ako.money: Gifts from Nicolai Tangen, who in 2020 gave it substantially all of his partnership interest in AKO Capital and other investment assets.

alcaldademedelln.name: Alcaldía de Medellín
alcaldademedelln.what: The executive government of the Special District of Medellín, Colombia, a city of 2,427,129 people led by mayor Federico Gutiérrez; the city owns the utility company EPM.
alcaldademedelln.money: The district budget, funded by local taxes such as property and business tax; budgeted revenue grew to 12.90 trillion pesos for 2026.

alexanders.name: Alexander S. Onassis Public Benefit Foundation
alexanders.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
alexanders.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
alexanders.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

alexandertutsek.name: Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung
alexandertutsek.what: A non-profit foundation for art and engineering science, set up in Munich in 2000 by Alexander Tutsek and his wife Eva-Maria Fahrner-Tutsek, with its seat in Munich-Schwabing.
alexandertutsek.money: The fortune of Alexander Tutsek (1927 to 2011), previous shareholder of the Refratechnik Group, a Munich maker of refractory products for cement and steel plants.
alexandertutsek.arts: It collects glass sculpture and modern photography, holds exhibitions at its Schwabing headquarters and gives the C/O Berlin Talent Award to young photographers.

alexsainsbury.name: The Glass-House Trust
alexsainsbury.what: A grant-making charity incorporated on 30 November 2011, funded by its trustee Alex Sainsbury; one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, which share an administration in London.
alexsainsbury.money: An expendable endowment from its funder Alex Sainsbury, held in an investment portfolio: net assets of £6,671,700 on 5 April 2025.
alexsainsbury.arts: It gives long-term support to a few projects in the built environment, child development, social policy and art, and takes no applications.
alexsainsbury.address: The Peak, 5 Wilton Road, London SW1V 1AP

aliph.name: ALIPH Foundation
aliph.short: International Alliance for the Protection of Heritage (ALIPH)
aliph.what: A Geneva foundation set up in March 2017 at the initiative of France and the United Arab Emirates to protect heritage, with the immunities of an intergovernmental organisation.
aliph.money: Contributions from states including France, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Morocco, Luxembourg, China and Cyprus, plus the Mellon Foundation, the Getty and private donors.

alkenmaes.name: Brouwerij Alken-Maes
alkenmaes.what: A Belgian brewery formed in 1988 by merging the Maes brewery at Kontich-Waarloos with Cristal-Alken at Alken, headquartered in Mechelen and owned by Heineken.
alkenmaes.money: Beer sales, with profits going to its owner, the Dutch brewer Heineken.

allagash.name: Allagash Brewing Company
allagash.what: A craft brewery founded in Portland, Maine, in 1995 by Rob Tod, who owns it; it specialises in Belgian-style beers.
allagash.money: Beer sales: it was the Maine craft brewery with the highest sales volume in 2024 and brewed 94,743 barrels in 2017.

alliances.name: Fondation Alliances
alliances.what: A Moroccan foundation created in 2009 by Alami Lazraq and his wife to house their art collection; their son Othman Lazraq directs it.
alliances.money: Groupe Alliances, the real estate company Alami Lazraq founded in 1994.
alliances.arts: Besides MACAAL it runs the Al Maaden Sculpture Park (opened 2013), the La Chambre Claire photography award and the Passerelles programme.

allies.name: Allies and Morrison LLP
allies.what: A London architecture and urban planning practice founded in 1984 by Bob Allies and Graham Morrison, with studios in Cambridge, Manchester, Dublin, Jeddah and Toronto.
allies.money: Fees from architecture, urban planning and consultancy commissions, much of it repeat work for long-term clients.

almanaseer.name: Manaseer Group
almanaseer.what: A Jordanian business group started in 1999 by Ziad Al Manaseer, a Jordanian-born Russian billionaire, with more than 20 companies and over 10,000 staff in Jordan.
almanaseer.money: Its companies in mining, cement and concrete, steel, fertilizers and chemicals, oil and gas through Manaseer Oil & Gas, trading and transport.

almineetbernardruizpicassopourlart.name: Fundación Almine y Bernard Ruiz-Picasso para el Arte
almineetbernardruizpicassopourlart.what: A private Spanish foundation set up in Madrid on 21 June 2002 by Bernard Ruiz-Picasso, Pablo Picasso's grandson, and his wife, the gallerist Almine Rech.
almineetbernardruizpicassopourlart.money: The private means of its two founders; its assets include their collection of works by Pablo Picasso and contemporary artists.
almineetbernardruizpicassopourlart.arts: It opened the Château de Boisgeloup, Picasso's former studio, which Bernard Ruiz-Picasso inherited in 1975, to the public in 2012.

altum.name: JSC Development Finance Institution Altum
altum.what: A Latvian state-owned development finance company set up on 27 December 2013 by merging three state institutions; the finance, economics and agriculture ministries hold its shares.
altum.money: Latvian state and EU funds for the support programmes it runs, plus money it raises from international institutions and capital markets.

americaforbulgaria.name: America for Bulgaria Foundation
americaforbulgaria.what: An independent American philanthropic foundation working in Bulgaria, founded in 2008 as successor to the Bulgarian-American Enterprise Fund, a USAID investment fund set up under the 1989 SEED Act.
americaforbulgaria.money: A $400 million endowment descended from the Bulgarian-American Enterprise Fund, which US tax money financed; it gives about $20 million a year.

americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.name: American Friends of the Israel Museum
americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.what: A New York non-profit, tax-exempt since May 1972, that raises money in the United States for the Israel Museum in Jerusalem.
americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.money: Donations: in 2024 contributions were $11.8 million of its $15.9 million revenue, with $3.4 million in investment income.

ammodo.name: Stichting Ammodo
ammodo.what: A Dutch foundation set up in Amsterdam in 2011 that funds visual and performing arts, science and architecture.
ammodo.money: Mainly donations from the Inphykem Foundation, former sole owner of the pension insurer Optas, which it sold to Aegon in 2007.
ammodo.arts: Ammodo Art supports new visual and performing arts productions and development programmes with partner institutions.

amosanderson.name: Amos Andersons fond rf
amosanderson.what: A Finnish association founded in 1940 by the businessman and newspaper publisher Amos Anderson, renamed from Föreningen Konstsamfundet in 2025, based in Helsinki.
amosanderson.money: The fortune Amos Anderson bequeathed to it as sole legatee, held in investments and in Hufvudstadsbladet, the Swedish-language newspaper it wholly owns.
amosanderson.arts: It funds fine arts, publications, music and theatre for Swedish-speaking Finns and runs the Söderlångvik museum in Anderson's former summer home in Dragsfjärd.

ampersand.name: The Ampersand Foundation
ampersand.what: A UK grant-making charity for the visual arts founded in 2011 by the collector Jack Kirkland, a director and shareholder of the Bowmer + Kirkland group.
ampersand.money: Donations from founder Jack Kirkland, including £319,744 in 2024-25 from his 2003 family settlement, plus investment income.
ampersand.arts: Its biennial Ampersand Foundation Award gives a Plus Tate member institution the funds for its director's or curator's chosen project.
ampersand.address: Third Floor, 21 Conduit Street, London W1S 2XP

amsterdamforarts.name: Stichting Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst
amsterdamforarts.what: A private-law foundation that distributes Amsterdam's arts subsidies, listed in the Dutch register of organisations with government involvement, based at Pakhuis de Zwijger in Amsterdam.
amsterdamforarts.money: The City of Amsterdam's arts budget: the mayor and aldermen adopt its grant schemes within the city's Kunstenplan 2025-2028.
amsterdamforarts.arts: It gives four-year and project subsidies to Amsterdam arts organisations and makers, and awards the Amsterdamprijs voor de Kunst.

amsterdamsvoordekunst.name: Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst
amsterdamsvoordekunst.what: Amsterdam's arts fund, set up in 1972 to award the city's arts commissions and prizes, managing part of the municipal arts subsidy independently.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.money: The Municipality of Amsterdam, which funds it to carry out the city's Kunstenplan arts policy.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.arts: It runs multi-year subsidies under the Kunstenplan 2025-2028, one-off project grants and the Amsterdam Prize for the Arts.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.address: Pakhuis de Zwijger, Piet Heinkade 179, 1019 HC Amsterdam

andywarholforvisualarts.name: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts
andywarholforvisualarts.what: A New York foundation set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which acts as the artist's estate and makes grants to the visual arts.
andywarholforvisualarts.money: An endowment built from Warhol's estate, sales of his works through Christie's and fees for licensing his images.
andywarholforvisualarts.arts: It has given over $300 million in cash grants to more than 1,000 arts organisations and donated 52,786 works to 322 institutions.
andywarholforvisualarts.address: 65 Bleecker Street, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10012

annemarion.name: Burnett Foundation
annemarion.what: A private foundation in Fort Worth, Texas, formerly the Anne Burnett and Charles D. Tandy Foundation, whose president was the ranch heiress Anne Windfohr Marion, who died in 2020.
annemarion.address: 640 Taylor St, Suite 2200, Fort Worth, TX

annenbergtrustatsunnylands.name: The Annenberg Foundation Trust at Sunnylands
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.what: A not-for-profit trust that owns and runs Sunnylands, the 200-acre Rancho Mirage winter estate of Walter and Leonore Annenberg, as a retreat for world leaders and a public site.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.money: Returns on the Annenberg fortune, made publishing TV Guide, The Philadelphia Inquirer and Seventeen; revenue was $40.5 million in the year to June 2025.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.arts: It holds the Sunnylands Collection of modern sculpture by Rodin, Giacometti, Arp and Agam, and runs public programmes on culture, music and film.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.address: 37977 Bob Hope Drive, Rancho Mirage, California

anschutz.name: Anschutz Foundation
anschutz.what: A private foundation in Denver, tax-exempt since 1984, through which the billionaire Philip Anschutz makes grants.
anschutz.money: Dividends and asset sales on net assets of US$1.65 billion (fiscal 2024); Anschutz's fortune comes from oil, railroads and entertainment.

aon.name: Aon plc
aon.what: A professional services firm created in 1982 when Patrick Ryan's Ryan Insurance Group merged with Combined Insurance Company of America; corporate seat in Dublin, operations run from London.
aon.money: Fees and commissions from insurance and reinsurance brokerage and from risk, health and retirement consulting; revenue was US$15.70 billion in 2024.

appliedmaterialstaiwan.name: Applied Materials Taiwan
appliedmaterialstaiwan.what: The Taiwan subsidiary of Applied Materials, Inc., the US semiconductor and display equipment maker founded in 1967 in Santa Clara, California; it has sites in Hsinchu, Tainan and elsewhere.
appliedmaterialstaiwan.money: Sales and servicing of chip and display manufacturing equipment; the parent's revenue was US$34.446 billion in 2026.

aqualand.name: Aqualand
aqualand.what: An Australian luxury property, hospitality and investment group established in Sydney in 2014 and started by its managing director Jin Lin.
aqualand.money: Sales and leasing of its Sydney residential, commercial and mixed-use developments, such as Central Barangaroo, plus its AL Capital funds and Etymon Projects hospitality arm.

arabforarts.name: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture
arabforarts.what: An independent non-profit foundation set up in 2007 by Arab cultural activists and based in Beirut, supporting artists, writers and organisations across the Arab region.
arabforarts.money: Gifts from individual donors through its Friends of AFAC circle, and grants and sponsorship from foundations, companies and cultural institutions.
arabforarts.arts: It awards about 250 grants a year across seven programmes, including performing arts, visual arts, documentary film, music and writing.

arabpotash.name: Arab Potash Company
arabpotash.what: A Jordanian mining company founded in 1956 as a pan-Arab venture, based in Amman and the Arab world's sole potash producer; China's SDIC Mining bought 28% in 2018.
arabpotash.money: Sales of potash and derivatives harvested from the Dead Sea; net profit after tax and mining royalties was about JOD 173 million in 2025.

aramark.name: Aramark
aramark.what: An American food service and facilities company founded as Davidson Brothers in 1936 by Davre and Henry Davidson, headquartered in Philadelphia and listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
aramark.money: Contracts to run catering and facilities for schools, hospitals, prisons, businesses and leisure venues, with revenue of US$18.5 billion in 2025.

aramex.name: Aramex PJSC
aramex.what: A logistics and courier company founded in Amman in 1982 by Fadi Ghandour and Bill Kingson, now based in Dubai and listed on the Dubai Financial Market.
aramex.money: Courier, freight and logistics fees, with revenue of US$1.732 billion in 2025, for a company 40.47% owned by the Abu Dhabi holding company ADQ.

arnoldblochleibler.name: Arnold Bloch Leibler
arnoldblochleibler.what: An Australian commercial law firm founded in 1953 with offices in Melbourne and Sydney, led by senior partner Mark Leibler and managing partner Henry Lanzer.
arnoldblochleibler.money: Legal fees from tax, commercial, mergers, disputes and property work for businesses, private groups and wealthy individuals.

arpels.name: Van Cleef & Arpels
arpels.what: A Paris jewellery house founded in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, now part of the Swiss luxury group Richemont.
arpels.money: Jewellery and watch sales for its owner Richemont, the luxury holding company Johann Rupert founded in 1988.
arpels.arts: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, launched in 2020, supports the creation and promotion of dance works and dance education.

art.name: National Art Collections Fund
art.what: An independent UK membership charity organised in 1903 by the activist Christiana Herringham to help public museums acquire art; based in London.
art.money: Subscriptions from its 142,000 members, who buy the National Art Pass, plus trusts, foundations and donors; it takes no government or National Lottery money.
art.arts: Since 1903 it has helped bring over 860,000 works of art into UK public collections.
art.address: 2 Granary Square, King's Cross, London N1C 4BH

artbridges.name: Art Bridges Foundation
artbridges.what: A US nonprofit founded in 2017 by Alice Walton that funds exhibitions, collection loans and programmes of American art with more than 400 partner museums.
artbridges.money: Alice Walton's philanthropy: she founded it and leads its board, and she is heiress to the Walmart fortune of her father Sam Walton.

artek.name: Artek Oy
artek.what: A Finnish furniture company founded in Helsinki in December 1935 by Alvar and Aino Aalto, Maire Gullichsen and Nils-Gustav Hahl, now owned by Vitra.
artek.money: Sales of furniture and design objects by Alvar and Aino Aalto and other designers, through its own stores and retailers.

artexplora.name: Fondation Art Explora
artexplora.what: A French foundation set up in 2019 by the entrepreneur Frédéric Jousset, recognised as a foundation of public interest by decree of 23 May 2023, based in Paris.
artexplora.money: A first non-expendable endowment of €4 million from its founder, topped up each year, plus sponsorship and private donations.

arthurerickson.name: Arthur Erickson Foundation
arthurerickson.what: A BC-incorporated society and federally registered charity founded to promote appreciation of the architect Arthur Erickson (1924-2009), and sole owner of his house and garden in Vancouver.
arthurerickson.money: Donations, memberships and garden tour fees (C$35 for non-members), raised to restore the house and garden and build an endowment for their care.

artjameel.name: Art Jameel
artjameel.what: An independent arts organisation set up in 2003 as part of Community Jameel, the philanthropy of the Saudi Jameel family, with centres in Jeddah and Dubai.
artjameel.money: The Jameel family, owners of Abdul Latif Jameel, a Jeddah group founded in 1945 that has distributed Toyota cars in Saudi Arabia since 1955.
artjameel.arts: It partnered with the Victoria and Albert Museum in London in 2003.

artotelspaviliunradensaleh.name: ARTOTEL Group
artotelspaviliunradensaleh.what: An Indonesian hotel operator and management company started in Surabaya in July 2012 by Erastus Radjimin and his sister Christine.
artotelspaviliunradensaleh.money: Hotel operation and management, food and drink, events and merchandise, with investment from Intudo Ventures and a Series B round led by Indies Capital Partners.
artotelspaviliunradensaleh.arts: Its hotels display work by 50 Indonesian artists and have hosted exhibitions by nearly 1,000 more.

artscouncilengland|UK.name: Arts Council England
artscouncilengland|UK.what: England's national development agency for the arts, museums and libraries, set up by Royal Charter in 1994 as an arm's length body of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport.
artscouncilengland|UK.money: UK government grant-in-aid through the culture department and National Lottery proceeds: £578,077,000 and £250,259,000 respectively in 2024-25.
artscouncilengland|UK.arts: It took over the Museums, Libraries and Archives Council in 2011 and has distributed lottery money to the arts since 1994.
artscouncilengland|UK.address: 2nd Floor, The Hive, 47 Lever Street, Manchester M1 1FN

artscouncilni|UK.name: Arts Council of Northern Ireland
artscouncilni|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilni|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.
artscouncilni|UK.address: The MAC, 10 Exchange Street West, Belfast BT1 2NJ

artscouncilnpo|UK.name: Arts Council England
artscouncilnpo|UK.what: A non-departmental public body and registered charity set up by Royal Charter in 1994, based in Manchester.
artscouncilnpo|UK.money: Grant-in-aid from the UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport (£578.1 million) and National Lottery proceeds (£250.3 million) in 2024-25.
artscouncilnpo|UK.arts: Its 2023-26 National Portfolio gives £446 million a year to 990 museums, libraries and arts organisations.
artscouncilnpo|UK.address: The Hive, 49 Lever Street, Manchester M1 1FN

artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.name: Arts Council of Northern Ireland
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.address: The MAC, 10 Exchange Street West, Belfast BT1 2NJ

artscouncil|Ireland.name: The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon
artscouncil|Ireland.what: Ireland's national government agency for funding, developing and promoting the arts, established in 1951.
artscouncil|Ireland.money: The Irish state, which channels its arts funding to artists and arts organisations through the council.

artsqueensland.name: Arts Queensland
artsqueensland.what: The arts agency of the Queensland Government, a service area of the state Department of Education, based in Brisbane.
artsqueensland.money: The Queensland state budget: the arts portfolio received A$420.7 million for the first year of the Time to Shine strategy (2025).

arup.name: Arup Group Limited
arup.what: A British engineering and design firm founded in London in 1946 by Sir Ove Arup, owned through a trust for its present and past employees.
arup.money: Fees for design, engineering, planning and advisory work on buildings and infrastructure, with revenue of £2,202.2 million in 2024.

asahishimbun.name: 公益財団法人朝日新聞文化財団
asahishimbun.what: A Tokyo foundation set up on 18 May 1992 with the approval of the education minister, a public interest incorporated foundation since 2011.
asahishimbun.money: An endowment of ¥5.68 billion built from Asahi Shimbun Company donations, including gifts of TV Asahi and Asahi Shimbun shares.
asahishimbun.arts: It funds music and art exhibitions and the protection of cultural property, awards the Asahi Prize and runs the Osaka International Festival.

asiaeurope.name: Asia-Europe Foundation
asiaeurope.what: An intergovernmental not-for-profit foundation set up on 15 February 1997 by the countries of the Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM), based in Singapore.
asiaeurope.money: Voluntary contributions from ASEM member governments, such as the Czech Republic's US$75,000 a year up to 2010.

assicurazionigenerali.name: Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A.
assicurazionigenerali.what: An Italian insurance group founded in Trieste in 1831, listed on the Borsa Italiana and the largest insurer in Italy as of 2022.
assicurazionigenerali.money: Insurance premiums and asset management, with operating income of €8.0 billion and net income of €4.3 billion in 2025.

associationvillalelac.name: Association Villa « Le Lac » Le Corbusier
associationvillalelac.what: The association that has run the Villa Le Lac museum in Corseaux, owned by the Fondation Le Corbusier, since 1 January 2013.
associationvillalelac.money: Admission fees (CHF 16 full price) and support from the Commune de Corseaux, with restoration and upkeep paid by the villa's owner.

astanamotors.name: Astana Motors
astanamotors.what: A Kazakh car retail, service and assembly company founded in 1992 by Nurlan Smagulov, its chair, based in Almaty.
astanamotors.money: Sales and servicing of the car brands it represents in Kazakhstan (11 in 2019) and output of its Hyundai Trans plant in Almaty.
astanamotors.arts: Smagulov set up the Almaty Museum of Arts, which shows the more than 700 works he collected over thirty years.

attwellssolicitors.name: Attwells Solicitors LLP
attwellssolicitors.what: A law firm registered in England and Wales as a limited liability partnership, with offices in Ipswich, Colchester, Woodbridge and London.
attwellssolicitors.money: Fees for conveyancing, property, employment, probate and business law work for private and business clients.
attwellssolicitors.address: St. Vincent House, 1 Cutler Street, Ipswich IP1 1UQ

atuge.name: Association des Tunisiens des Grandes Écoles
atuge.what: A non-profit, independent and non-political association of Tunisian graduates of the French grandes écoles, created in 1990, with branches in Tunis, Paris, the United Kingdom and Shanghai.
atuge.money: Membership dues from its more than 8,000 members worldwide.

aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.name: Auckland Council
aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.what: The unitary local and regional government of the Auckland Region, formed in 2010 by merging seven territorial authorities and one regional council.
aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.money: The council group reported NZ$8.7 billion in revenue in 2025/26, which also funds its council-controlled organisations.

audainforvisualarts.name: Audain Foundation
audainforvisualarts.what: A private foundation set up in 1997 by Michael Audain to support the visual arts in British Columbia.
audainforvisualarts.money: Gifts from Audain, chairman and major shareholder of the British Columbia home builder Polygon Homes.
audainforvisualarts.arts: It funds capital projects and exhibitions at public galleries and schools and created the C$100,000 Audain Prize for senior British Columbia artists.

audi.name: Audi AG
audi.what: A German maker of luxury cars headquartered in Ingolstadt and wholly owned by the Volkswagen Group.

costopoulos.name: The J. F. Costopoulos Foundation
costopoulos.what: A private foundation set up in 1979, at the centenary of Credit Bank (now Alpha Bank), by its chairman Spyros Costopoulos and his wife Eurydice.
costopoulos.money: A donation from Spyros and Eurydice Costopoulos at its founding; its accounts are audited yearly and submitted to Greece's Ministry of Finance.
costopoulos.arts: It supports visual arts, theatre, music, cinema and dance, cultural heritage and research, and keeps a library and an art collection.

cottonon.name: Cotton On Foundation
cottonon.what: The charity of the Australian retailer Cotton On Group, started in Geelong in 2007 after a donation request for a healthcare centre in Mannya, Uganda.
cottonon.money: Proceeds from Foundation products sold in Cotton On Group stores and online, all of which go to its projects.

cova.name: Fondation d'entreprise Covéa
cova.what: The corporate foundation of Covéa, the French mutual insurance group behind MAAF, MMA and GMF; it was set up at the end of 2022 and launched in May 2023.
cova.money: Covéa's insurance business funds it, with a budget of about €4 million a year for social and human inclusion.

cragg.name: Cragg Foundation
cragg.what: A non-profit foundation set up in Wuppertal in 2005 by the family of the Anglo-German sculptor Tony Cragg; it runs the Waldfrieden Sculpture Park, opened in 2008.
cragg.money: The Cragg family, who set it up; Tony Cragg owns the Waldfrieden estate that it runs.

crditdunord.name: Crédit du Nord
crditdunord.what: A French retail bank seated in Lille, bought by Société Générale from Paribas in 1997 and merged with the Société Générale branch network into SG on 1 January 2023.
crditdunord.money: Banking income from retail and business customers of its regional banks; since 2023 that business belongs to SG, the French retail bank of Société Générale.

creatensw.name: Create NSW
creatensw.what: The NSW Government's arts and culture agency, formed on 1 April 2017 from Arts NSW and Screen NSW.
creatensw.money: The New South Wales state budget, through the Minister for the Arts, who answers to the NSW Parliament.
creatensw.arts: Its Arts and Cultural Funding Program includes Creative Steps grants of up to $75,000 for new work by NSW artists.

creativeaustralia.name: Creative Australia
creativeaustralia.what: The Australian Government's principal arts investment and advisory body, founded as the Australia Council for the Arts in 1968 and renamed in 2023; based in Sydney.
creativeaustralia.money: The Australian Government, with funding decisions made at arm's length from the federal arts minister.

creativeeurope|Netherlands.name: Creative Europe
creativeeurope|Netherlands.what: The European Commission's programme for the cultural, creative and audiovisual sectors, run by its Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture with grants handled by EACEA.
creativeeurope|Netherlands.money: The European Union budget: EUR 2.44 billion for 2021-2027, up from EUR 1.47 billion in 2014-2020.

creativeindustriesnl.name: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie
creativeindustriesnl.what: The Dutch national culture fund for design, architecture and digital culture, a private-law foundation and independent administrative body active since 1 January 2013, based in Rotterdam.
creativeindustriesnl.money: State money from the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, the parent ministry of the national culture funds (rijkscultuurfondsen).

creativenewzealand.name: Arts Council of New Zealand Toi Aotearoa
creativenewzealand.what: The national arts development agency of the New Zealand government, a Crown entity governed by the Arts Council, set up in 1994 to replace the Queen Elizabeth II Arts Council.
creativenewzealand.money: The New Zealand Lottery Grants Board Te Puna Tahua and the government through Vote: Arts, Culture and Heritage.
creativenewzealand.arts: It invested NZ$61 million in the arts in 2024/25.

creativescotland.name: Creative Scotland
creativescotland.what: The Scottish Government's public body for the arts, screen and creative industries, created in 2010 from the Scottish Arts Council and Scottish Screen; based in Edinburgh.
creativescotland.money: Funding from the Scottish Government and the National Lottery.
creativescotland.address: Waverley Court, 4 East Market Street, Edinburgh EH8 8BG

creativescotlandregularfunding.name: Creative Scotland
creativescotlandregularfunding.what: An executive non-departmental public body of the Scottish Government for the arts, screen and creative industries, created in 2010 from Scottish Screen and the Scottish Arts Council.
creativescotlandregularfunding.money: Funding from the Scottish Government and from the UK National Lottery, which it distributes to artists and cultural organisations in Scotland.
creativescotlandregularfunding.arts: Its Multi-Year Funding programme, which replaced Regular Funding, covers the core costs of cultural organisations from April 2025 to March 2028.
creativescotlandregularfunding.address: Waverley Court, 4 East Market Street, Edinburgh EH8 8BG

creativevictoria.name: Creative Victoria
creativevictoria.what: The Victorian state government's agency for the arts and creative industries, reporting to the Minister for Creative Industries; based in Melbourne.
creativevictoria.money: The budget of the State of Victoria.

ctdecd.name: Connecticut Department of Economic and Community Development
ctdecd.what: The State of Connecticut's economic development department; the Connecticut Office of the Arts, the state arts agency, sits within it.
ctdecd.money: Connecticut's state budget, plus National Endowment for the Arts funds that the Office of the Arts regrants.
ctdecd.arts: Its Office of the Arts made 232 Supporting Arts grants totalling US$1,050,005 in fiscal 2024.

cultureliverpool.name: Culture Liverpool
cultureliverpool.what: The culture and events service of Liverpool City Council, which stages major cultural and sporting events in the city.
cultureliverpool.money: Liverpool City Council's £817.6m net budget for 2026/27, made up of business rates £295.1m, council tax £277.0m and government grants £245.5m.
cultureliverpool.arts: The council's Culture and Arts Investment Programme funds 29 arts organisations; in September 2025 its cabinet proposed extending it to March 2027 with £2.245m.

cultureministry|Denmark.name: Kulturministeriet
cultureministry|Denmark.what: Denmark's ministry for culture, sport and media, founded in 1961 with Julius Bomholt as its first minister, based on Nybrogade in Copenhagen.
cultureministry|Denmark.money: The Danish state budget: section 21 of the Finance Act for 2026 sets the ministry's net spending at DKK 14,015.8 million.
cultureministry|Denmark.arts: Its agencies include the Danish Arts Foundation (Statens Kunstfond) and the Agency for Culture and Palaces.

cultuurfonds.name: Cultuurfonds
cultuurfonds.what: A Dutch private foundation set up by Prince Bernhard in London in 1940, renamed in 2023 to drop his name, with its office in Amsterdam.
cultuurfonds.money: Proceeds from the VriendenLoterij and the Nederlandse Loterij, plus gifts and bequests from donors.
cultuurfonds.arts: It puts more than EUR 50 million a year into culture and nature.

cultuurfondsnoordholland.name: het Cultuurfonds Noord-Holland
cultuurfondsnoordholland.what: The Noord-Holland branch of the Cultuurfonds, the Dutch cultural fund Prince Bernhard set up in London in 1940; each province has a branch with its own board.
cultuurfondsnoordholland.money: The national Cultuurfonds, funded by the VriendenLoterij and Nederlandse Loterij, donors and bequests; the branch also manages named funds set up by private donors.
cultuurfondsnoordholland.arts: The Cultuurfonds gives more than 50 million euros a year to culture and nature; the branch judges applications for projects of regional importance.

danireissctoexpansion.name: Dani Reiss
danireissctoexpansion.what: Toronto businessman, chairman and chief executive of the parka maker Canada Goose; he took over as chief executive from his father, David Reiss, in 2001.
danireissctoexpansion.money: His wealth from Canada Goose, listed in Toronto and New York since 2017 and part owned by Bain Capital; revenue CA$1.35 billion in fiscal 2025.
danireissctoexpansion.renamed: The AGO gift came from Dani Reiss personally, not from the company Canada Goose.

danisharts.name: Statens Kunstfond
danisharts.what: Denmark's state arts fund, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, with 16 expert committees that award its grants.
danisharts.money: The Danish state budget, through funds provided by the Ministry of Culture.
danisharts.arts: It awards about 640 million Danish kroner a year to some 6,000 projects through about 65 grant schemes.

danone.name: Danone
danone.what: A French food and beverage group, listed on Euronext Paris and based in Paris, whose Danone brand Isaac Carasso founded in Barcelona in 1919.
danone.money: Sales of dairy and plant-based products, bottled waters and specialised nutrition: 27.3 billion euros in 2025.

darlingtonbuildingsociety.name: Darlington Building Society
darlingtonbuildingsociety.what: A mutual building society owned by its members, formed in 1856 as the Darlington Working Men's Equitable Permanent Building Society, with its head office in Darlington.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.money: Mortgage lending funded by members' savings: retail deposits of 939 million pounds and total assets of 1,025 million pounds in 2025.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.arts: It gives 5 percent of its profits each year to local good causes.
darlingtonbuildingsociety.address: Sentinel House, Morton Road, Darlington DL1 4PT

davidzwirner.name: David Zwirner
davidzwirner.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in New York in 1993 by the German-born dealer David Zwirner, with galleries in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris and Hong Kong.
davidzwirner.money: Sales of works by the more than seventy artists and estates it represents, in the primary and secondary art markets.

dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.name: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.what: The UK government ministerial department for culture, media, sport and digital services, named the Department for Culture, Media and Sport from 2023 until its renaming in 2026.
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.money: UK central government money, as a ministerial department of the UK government.
dcmsstatutorygrantinaid|UK.arts: Its public bodies include Arts Council England, the British Museum, the National Gallery, Tate and the Victoria and Albert Museum.

debethune.name: De Bethune
debethune.what: An independent Swiss watch manufacturer founded in 2002 by Denis Flageollet and David Zanetta, with its workshops in L'Auberson near Sainte-Croix, in the canton of Vaud.
debethune.money: Sales of a few hundred mechanical watches a year; since Zanetta sold his majority share in 2017 it has four shareholders.

deborahloebbrice.name: Deborah L Brice Foundation
deborahloebbrice.what: A private foundation in New York, tax-exempt since 1971, with Deborah Loeb Brice, a granddaughter of Arthur Lehman and sister of Ambassador John L. Loeb Jr., as trustee.
deborahloebbrice.money: Investment income on its endowment: 1,026,742 dollars in dividends in 2024, with net assets of 25,486,275 dollars at the end of that year.

degroofpetercam.name: Degroof Petercam
degroofpetercam.what: A Brussels private bank founded as Banque Philippson in 1871, merged with the broker Petercam in 2015 and owned since 2024 by Crédit Agricole's Indosuez Wealth Management.
degroofpetercam.money: Fees and income from private banking, asset management, investment banking and asset services for private and institutional clients.

delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.name: De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde, Inc.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.what: A private Catholic non-stock, non-profit college in Malate, Manila, founded in 1988 by the De La Salle Brothers and a member of De La Salle Philippines.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.money: Tuition from its students; in 2019 the Supreme Court ruled its 2002 gross receipts of 643 million pesos exempt from tax.
delasallecollegeofsaintbenilde.arts: It was the first school in the Philippines to offer degrees in animation, photography, film, multimedia arts and production design.

delenprivatebank.name: Delen Private Bank
delenprivatebank.what: An Antwerp private bank grown from the brokerage Delen & C°, founded by André Delen in 1936; Ackermans & van Haaren owns 78.75 percent, the Delen family 21.25 percent.
delenprivatebank.money: Fees for managing and planning the wealth of private clients and their companies.

delmontephilippines.name: Del Monte Philippines, Inc.
delmontephilippines.what: A Philippine food company 87 percent owned by Del Monte Pacific Limited, which is 72 percent owned by the Campos family's NutriAsia Pacific Group.
delmontephilippines.money: Sales of packaged fruit, juices, sauces and fresh pineapples grown on its 30,000-hectare leased plantation in Bukidnon and Misamis Oriental.
delmontephilippines.address: JY Campos Centre, 9th Avenue corner 30th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City 1634

denederlandschebank.name: De Nederlandsche Bank N.V.
denederlandschebank.what: The central bank of the Netherlands, founded by King William I in 1814, now a state-owned public limited company within the Eurosystem and the Dutch financial supervisor.
denederlandschebank.money: Income on its monetary assets; in 2025 interest costs exceeded it, for a loss of 967 million euros, so the Dutch state receives no dividend.

denza.name: Shenzhen Denza New Energy Automotive Co., Ltd.
denza.what: A Chinese electric car brand founded in February 2011 as a 50-50 joint venture of BYD and Daimler; BYD became its sole shareholder in September 2024.
denza.money: Car sales; it is wholly owned by BYD, the Shenzhen electric vehicle maker.

deroytestamentary.name: DeRoy Testamentary Foundation
deroytestamentary.what: A private foundation in Michigan created under the will of Helen L. DeRoy (1882 to 1977), who ran her husband's car business, and tax-exempt since 1978.
deroytestamentary.money: Helen DeRoy's estate, built on Aaron DeRoy's Studebaker dealerships; in 2025 it spent 25.3 million dollars, leaving net assets of 272,970 dollars.

deutschebrsephotography.name: Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation gGmbH
deutschebrsephotography.what: A non-profit corporate foundation of Deutsche Börse, the Frankfurt stock exchange group, set up in Frankfurt am Main in 2015.
deutschebrsephotography.money: Deutsche Börse, which began collecting contemporary photography in 1999 and in 2015 handed the foundation its collection and cultural sponsorship.
deutschebrsephotography.arts: It holds the Art Collection Deutsche Börse of more than 2,400 works by about 170 artists and awards an annual photography prize with the Photographers' Gallery, London.

deutschedenkmalschutz.name: Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz
deutschedenkmalschutz.what: A privately funded foundation set up on 17 April 1985, the largest private initiative for monument preservation in Germany, with its seat in Bonn.
deutschedenkmalschutz.money: Gifts from about 200,000 private donors and money from the GlücksSpirale lottery.
deutschedenkmalschutz.arts: It has helped preserve more than 7,400 monuments with almost 800 million euros in funding.

didrichsenart.name: Didrichsens konstmuseum sr
didrichsenart.what: A foundation set up on 11 November 1963 by Marie-Louise and Gunnar Didrichsen to preserve their art collections and museum building on Kuusisaari island in Helsinki.
didrichsenart.money: The founders' fortune; Gunnar Didrichsen, a Danish businessman, founded the import company Transmeri in Finland in 1927.

digitalrealty.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
digitalrealty.what: A US real estate investment trust that owns and operates data centres worldwide, formed in 2004 by GI Partners and headquartered in Austin, Texas.
digitalrealty.money: Rent and fees for data centre space, colocation and interconnection: revenue of 6.11 billion dollars in 2025.

dior.name: Christian Dior Couture
dior.what: A Paris fashion house founded in 1946 by the designer Christian Dior with the textile industrialist Marcel Boussac, now a subsidiary of LVMH.
dior.money: Sales of its fashion and leather goods; its parent group is controlled by Bernard Arnault's family, which holds 97.5% of Christian Dior SE.

dlgsc.name: Department of Creative Industries, Tourism and Sport
dlgsc.what: A Western Australian government department formed on 1 July 2025, when it took over the creative industries and sport work of the Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries.
dlgsc.arts: Its arts funding includes Arts Projects for Organisations, the Contemporary Music Fund and the Regional Aboriginal Arts Development programme.

dmgmori.name: DMG MORI AKTIENGESELLSCHAFT
dmgmori.what: A Bielefeld maker of CNC lathes, milling machines and other machine tools, formerly Gildemeister AG, controlled since 2016 by a holding company of the Japanese DMG MORI group.
dmgmori.money: Sales of machine tools, automation and services to manufacturers: 2,228.3 million euros in 2024, 59 percent of it outside Germany.

dnv.name: DNV
dnv.what: A Norwegian classification society and assurance company for shipping, energy and other industries, headquartered in Høvik and owned by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation.
dnv.money: Fees for ship classification, certification, testing and advisory work: operating revenue of 34,966 million Norwegian kroner in 2024.

do.name: DO & CO Aktiengesellschaft
do.what: A Vienna catering group founded by Attila Dogudan and listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange since 1998, serving airlines, rail operators and international events.
do.money: Catering revenue of about 2.46 billion euros in the 2025/26 financial year, of which airline catering brought 1.95 billion euros.

doen.name: Stichting DOEN
doen.what: A Dutch foundation set up in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij that funds pioneers in the Netherlands and abroad.
doen.money: Lottery proceeds: 24,303,520 euros from the Postcode Loterij and 7,200,000 euros from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
doen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and culture projects in 2025.

dorotheum.name: Dorotheum
dorotheum.what: An auction house founded in Vienna in 1707 by Emperor Joseph I; a state enterprise until its 2001 sale to Erwin and Hanno Soravia and Christoph Dichand.
dorotheum.money: Its auctions, retail sales and pawn lending; about 600 auctions a year bring some 60 percent of its turnover.

dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.name: Département des Bouches-du-Rhône
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.what: The departmental government of Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France, run by an elected departmental council presided over by Martine Vassal, seated in Marseille.
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.money: The departmental budget its councillors adopted on 14 April 2026, with more than 1.6 billion euros, over 62 percent of spending, for social welfare.

dracgrandest.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles Grand Est
dracgrandest.what: The regional office of the French Ministry of Culture for Grand Est, under the regional prefect, seated in the Palais du Rhin in Strasbourg with sites in Metz and Châlons-en-Champagne.
dracgrandest.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

dracledefrance.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles d'Île-de-France
dracledefrance.what: The Paris office of the French Ministry of Culture for the Île-de-France region.
dracledefrance.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

dracnouvelleaquitaine.name: Direction régionale des affaires culturelles Nouvelle-Aquitaine
dracnouvelleaquitaine.what: A regional service of the French Ministry of Culture under the prefect of Nouvelle-Aquitaine, with its seat in Bordeaux and sites in Limoges and Poitiers.
dracnouvelleaquitaine.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry of Culture.

droomendaad.name: Stichting Droom en Daad
droomendaad.what: A family foundation set up in Rotterdam on 13 December 2016 by Martijn van der Vorm, former chief executive of the investment company HAL; Van der Vorms chair its board.
droomendaad.money: The Van der Vorm family fortune, invested in HAL since the family sold its Holland America cruise business in 1988.
droomendaad.arts: It takes no applications and develops its own Rotterdam projects through foundations it sets up, among them the Fenix museum.

drosos.name: Drosos Stiftung
drosos.what: A private foundation set up in Zurich in 2003 by Christa Gelpke-Engelhorn, who stayed anonymous until the board disclosed her name in 2020; it funds projects for young people.
drosos.money: An endowment from Christa Gelpke-Engelhorn's inheritance in the pharmaceutical firm Boehringer Mannheim, including proceeds from the 1998 sale of the family holding company.

dtactelecomfounderboonchaibencharongkul.name: Boonchai Bencharongkul
dtactelecomfounderboonchaibencharongkul.what: A Thai businessman and art collector, born in 1954, who founded the mobile operator DTAC and served as its chairman.
dtactelecomfounderboonchaibencharongkul.money: His family's telecommunications business, inherited from his father Suchin in 1981 and later run with Telenor; the siblings sold most DTAC shares in 2005.
dtactelecomfounderboonchaibencharongkul.arts: He owns one of the largest private art collections in Thailand.
dtactelecomfounderboonchaibencharongkul.renamed: The atlas name puts DTAC first, but the museum is Boonchai Bencharongkul's own project, not the company's.

dtcbotswana.name: Diamond Trading Company Botswana
dtcbotswana.what: A 50/50 joint venture of the Government of Botswana and De Beers, set up under a 2006 agreement, that sorts and values rough diamonds in Gaborone.
dtcbotswana.money: Sorting and valuing rough diamonds, up to 45 million carats a year, for sale through De Beers Sightholder Sales and the Okavango Diamond Company.

dubaiculture.name: Dubai Culture & Arts Authority
dubaiculture.what: A public authority of the Government of Dubai created by Law No. 6 of 2008, chaired since 5 September 2019 by Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.
dubaiculture.money: The general budget of the Emirate of Dubai, plus its own fees and grants or gifts approved by the Executive Council.

dublincitycouncil|Ireland.name: Dublin City Council
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.what: The local authority for the city of Dublin, called Dublin Corporation until 2001, with 63 elected members and a Lord Mayor.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.money: The council's own budget, from which its Arts Office pays annual arts grants and bursary awards.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.arts: It added €50,000 to its 2026 project grants and bursary awards.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.address: Civic Offices, Wood Quay, Dublin 8, D08 RF3F

dublinport.name: Dublin Port Company
dublinport.what: The State-owned commercial company that operates and develops Dublin Port; private companies carry out all cargo handling in the port.
dublinport.money: Port charges and services such as towage and pilotage: revenue of 106.26 million euros in 2024 and post-tax profit of 30.04 million euros.
dublinport.arts: It runs the Pumphouse and Substation venues for Irish and international artists and a distributed museum across the city.

durhamcountycouncil|UK.name: Durham County Council
durhamcountycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for County Durham in England, with its seat in Durham.
durhamcountycouncil|UK.money: Council tax, local business rates and government grants; for 2025/26 it expected 48.825 million pounds in additional government funding.

dutchministryofeducation|Netherlands.name: Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap
dutchministryofeducation|Netherlands.short: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW)
dutchministryofeducation|Netherlands.what: The Dutch government ministry for education, culture and science, formed on 9 September 1918 and based in The Hague; Rianne Letschert is minister.

duvel.name: Duvel Moortgat
duvel.what: A Belgian family-owned brewer founded in 1871 by Jan-Leonard Moortgat, now in its fourth generation, based in Breendonk, Puurs-Sint-Amands.
duvel.money: Beer sales from brands including Duvel, Vedett, Chouffe and Liefmans: consolidated turnover of 608 million euros in 2024.

ebsco.name: EBSCO Industries, Inc.
ebsco.what: A privately held American company of over 40 businesses, founded in 1944 by Elton B. Stephens and his wife Alys and headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama.
ebsco.money: Its businesses in information services, consumer products, industrial goods, real estate and renewable energy; revenue above US$3 billion.

edostategovernment|Nigeria.name: Edo State Government
edostategovernment|Nigeria.what: The government of Edo State, Nigeria, seated in Benin City; Monday Okpebholo has been governor since 12 November 2024.
edostategovernment|Nigeria.money: The state budget: the 939.85 billion naira 2026 budget relies on 480 billion naira of federal FAAC allocations and 160 billion naira of own revenue.
edostategovernment|Nigeria.arts: In August 2026 a committee set up by the state government reported that the Obaseki administration spent 3.8 billion naira on the Museum of West African Art.

eduardolenjimenes.name: Fundación Eduardo León Jimenes, Inc.
eduardolenjimenes.what: A Dominican family foundation of the León family, named after Eduardo León Jimenes, who founded the La Aurora cigar factory in 1903; it marked 30 years in January 2026.
eduardolenjimenes.money: The León family's Grupo León Jimenes, an investment company built on La Aurora tobacco and Cervecería Nacional Dominicana, where it keeps a 15% stake.
eduardolenjimenes.arts: It runs the Centro León in Santiago de los Caballeros, opened in 2003, with collections of Dominican art and pre-Columbian archaeology.
eduardolenjimenes.address: Calle José María Cabral Bermúdez 10, Bella Vista, Santo Domingo

egdholding.name: EGD Holding AS
egdholding.what: A Bergen family investment company founded in 1907 by Einar Galtung Døsvig. Its chairman, Espen Galtung Døsvig, represents the fourth generation.
egdholding.money: The family's holdings in shipping (eight ships through EGD Shipholding), property (EGD Property) and financial investments (EGD Capital).
egdholding.arts: Its registered purpose includes buying and selling art and building and lending out an art collection.

egdholdingas.name: EGD Holding AS
egdholdingas.what: A Bergen family holding company founded in 1907 by Einar Galtung Døsvig as a textile trader; the fourth-generation chair, Espen Galtung Døsvig, owns 100% of the shares.
egdholdingas.money: Investments in international shipping, property and capital through EGD Shipholding, EGD Property and EGD Capital, after the textile business closed around 2000.
egdholdingas.arts: Its registered purpose includes buying and selling art and setting up and renting out an art collection.

elephanttrust.name: The Elephant Trust
elephanttrust.what: A UK charity (no. 269615) created in 1975 by the artist Roland Penrose and the photographer Lee Miller; it gives visual artists grants of up to £5,000.
elephanttrust.money: An endowment from Penrose's 1975 sale of Max Ernst's painting The Elephant Celebes to the Tate, plus bequests from Shelagh Wakely and George Melhuish.
elephanttrust.arts: The Shelagh Wakely Bequest funds London residencies for Latin American artists with Gasworks; the trust also awards the Joanna Drew Travel Bursary.

embru.name: Embru-Werke AG
embru.what: A Swiss furniture maker entered in the commercial register in Rüti, canton Zurich, on 1 January 1904 as Eisen- und Metallbettenfabrik Rueti AG; it calls itself a family company.
embru.money: Sales of the school, office, home and care furniture it makes at its factory in Rüti.

emmanuelcollege.name: Emmanuel College, Cambridge
emmanuelcollege.what: A constituent college of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1584 by Sir Walter Mildmay, Chancellor of the Exchequer to Elizabeth I.
emmanuelcollege.money: Its own endowment, valued at £154 million in 2024 in the college's financial statement.

enabel.name: Enabel
enabel.what: The Belgian federal government's agency for international cooperation, formerly the Belgian Technical Cooperation (CTB), with over 2,500 staff running over 200 projects.
enabel.money: Project work worth 500 million euros a year, at least half paid by the Belgian state, the rest by clients such as the European Union.

enbwwindpower.name: Borusan EnBW Enerji A.Ş.
enbwwindpower.what: A Turkish renewable power company founded in Istanbul in 2009 as a joint venture in which the German utility EnBW and Borusan Holding each hold 50%.
enbwwindpower.money: Electricity sales from 720 megawatts of plants in Turkey (2022): nine wind farms, two solar plants and one hydro plant.
enbwwindpower.renamed: The atlas name points at the German utility EnBW AG, but the museum line lists Borusan group units, which means the joint venture Borusan EnBW Enerji.

engiehaspartnered.name: ENGIE SA
engiehaspartnered.what: A French energy group formed in 2008 by the merger of Gaz de France and Suez, listed in Paris and based at La Défense, Courbevoie; the French state holds 23.64%.
engiehaspartnered.money: Sales of electricity, natural gas, renewable power and energy services in 30 countries; revenue €82.56 billion in 2023.

eonenergiamegoldsok.name: E.ON Energiamegoldások Kft.
eonenergiamegoldsok.what: The energy supply company of the E.ON Hungária group, part of Germany's E.ON, selling electricity and natural gas to companies and municipalities across Hungary.
eonenergiamegoldsok.money: Sales of electricity and gas to small, medium and large businesses and municipalities, plus solar plant installation and energy efficiency services.

eonpolska.name: E.ON Polska S.A.
eonpolska.what: An electricity seller in Warsaw owned by Germany's E.ON group, formerly RWE Polska and then innogy Polska, renamed E.ON Polska in December 2021.
eonpolska.money: Electricity sales, mainly to customers in Warsaw, where the group's Stoen Operator runs the distribution network.

ernstvonsiemenskunststiftung.name: Ernst von Siemens Kunststiftung
ernstvonsiemenskunststiftung.what: A foundation under German civil law set up in 1983 through the gifts of the industrialist Ernst von Siemens, grandson of Siemens founder Werner von Siemens; seat in Munich.
ernstvonsiemenskunststiftung.money: An endowment built from gifts by Ernst von Siemens and Siemens AG.
ernstvonsiemenskunststiftung.arts: It pays out 8 to 12 million euros a year (2026) and has funded acquisitions worth €112.8 million and over 1,100 exhibitions or catalogues for German museums.

erste.name: DIE ERSTE österreichische Spar-Casse Privatstiftung
erste.what: Austria's largest savings bank foundation, formed in 2003 from Erste österreichische Spar-Casse, the first Austrian savings bank (1819), seated in Vienna.
erste.money: Dividends from its stake as core shareholder of Erste Group Bank AG, part of which it spends on Central and South Eastern Europe.

eskerasmcneofficiel.name: Esker
eskerasmcneofficiel.what: A French software company founded in 1985 by Jean-Michel Bérard and Benoît Borrits and based in Villeurbanne; the fund Bridgepoint, with General Atlantic, bought it through a 2024 takeover offer.
eskerasmcneofficiel.money: Sales of its cloud platform that automates purchasing, invoicing and customer order processes; revenue €205.3 million in 2024.

esmefairbairn.name: Esmée Fairbairn Foundation
esmefairbairn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity founded in 1961 by unit-trust pioneer Ian Fairbairn and named after his late second wife; based in London.
esmefairbairn.money: Investment returns on an endowment that began as a 33% stake in fund manager M&G, sold to Prudential in 1999.
esmefairbairn.arts: In 2025 it gave £52.9m across its three aims, one of which is Creative, Confident Communities.

essexcommunityfdn.name: Essex Community Foundation
essexcommunityfdn.what: A community foundation launched in 1996 by Ian and Angela Marks, who sold their family sweet maker Trebor to Cadbury in 1989; it funds Essex charities.
essexcommunityfdn.money: Donations and funds from individuals, families, businesses and trusts, which it invests; it gives about £4 million in grants a year.

estrelladamm.name: Sociedad Anónima Damm
estrelladamm.what: A Barcelona brewery founded in 1876 by the Alsatians August Kuentzmann Damm and Joseph Damm, maker of Estrella Damm beer.
estrelladamm.money: Beer and drinks sales, EUR 2,061 million in 2023; in 2018 the Carceller family held the largest stake through Disa, a Canarian oil company.

eucalyptus.name: Eucalyptus Foundation
eucalyptus.what: A private grantmaking foundation in San Francisco, tax-exempt since June 1992, whose board includes members of the Geballe family, with Gordon T. Geballe as president.
eucalyptus.money: Investment returns on net assets of $267.8 million (2025), mostly dividends and asset sales, plus $18.6 million in gifts in 2024.

eudelegation|Peru.name: Delegación de la Unión Europea en Perú
eudelegation|Peru.what: The European Union's diplomatic mission in Peru, in San Isidro, Lima, part of the European External Action Service; the European Commission has had a presence in Peru since March 1991.
eudelegation|Peru.money: The European Union budget, through the European External Action Service and EU development cooperation with Peru.

eugenekaspersky.name: Eugene Kaspersky
eugenekaspersky.what: A Russian cybersecurity expert born in 1965 who co-founded Kaspersky Lab in Moscow in 1997 and is its chief executive.
eugenekaspersky.money: His fortune from Kaspersky Lab, whose revenue was US$836 million in 2025; Forbes put his net worth at US$1.3 billion in 2017.
eugenekaspersky.renamed: The atlas name is the company Kaspersky Lab, but the biennale sentence names Eugene Kaspersky himself as the main payer.

eugenemcdermott.name: Eugene McDermott Foundation
eugenemcdermott.what: A private foundation in Dallas set up in 1955 by Eugene McDermott, co-founder of Texas Instruments; his daughter Mary McDermott Cook is president.
eugenemcdermott.money: An endowment from Eugene McDermott's Texas Instruments fortune; net assets were $131.0 million in August 2025.

europeancultural.name: European Cultural Foundation
europeancultural.what: An independent foundation set up in Geneva in 1954 by the Swiss philosopher Denis de Rougemont and based in Amsterdam since 1960.
europeancultural.money: A yearly contribution from the Dutch lotteries VriendenLoterij and Nederlandse Loterij, paid through Het Cultuurfonds, plus partners for single programmes.
europeancultural.arts: It runs grant programmes such as the Culture of Solidarity Fund and works on libraries, digital citizenship and cross-border solidarity in Europe.

europeanregionaldevelopment.name: European Regional Development Fund
europeanregionaldevelopment.what: An EU fund set up in 1975 and one of the European Structural and Investment Funds, run by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy.
europeanregionaldevelopment.money: The EU budget, spent through programmes shared between the Commission and national and regional authorities, which choose the projects.

europeanunion|Poland.name: European Commission
europeanunion|Poland.what: The politically independent executive arm of the European Union, established in 1958 and based in Brussels, led by President Ursula von der Leyen.
europeanunion|Poland.money: The EU budget, funded by own resources: customs duties, a VAT-based share, member states' gross national income contributions and a plastics own resource.
europeanunion|Poland.arts: Its Creative Europe programme has a 2021-2027 budget of €2.44 billion for the cultural and creative sectors.

europeanuniversitycyprus.name: European University Cyprus
europeanuniversitycyprus.what: A private university in Nicosia founded in 1961, part of the private higher education group Galileo Global Education, with a second campus in Frankfurt.

evabesen.name: Besen Family Foundation
evabesen.what: A Melbourne family foundation set up in 1978 by Marc and Eva Besen; Marc Besen co-founded the fashion retailer Sussan and ran it from 1951 to 1980.
evabesen.money: The Besen family's fortune from Sussan, the Australian women's fashion chain Marc Besen co-founded.
evabesen.arts: Its grant programmes cover arts and culture, the Jewish community, and health and welfare in Australia and Israel.

evraz.name: EVRAZ plc
evraz.what: A steel and mining company incorporated in London in 2011 and operating mainly in Russia; Roman Abramovich held 28.64% in 2021, and the UK sanctioned it in May 2022.
evraz.money: Sales of steel, steel products, vanadium and iron ore; revenue US$13.224 billion in 2021.
evraz.address: Portman House, 2 Portman Street, London W1H 6DU

exhibitioncreditsnamemillerknoll.name: MillerKnoll, Inc.
exhibitioncreditsnamemillerknoll.what: A US furniture group based in Zeeland, Michigan, formed when Herman Miller bought Knoll in 2021; its brands include Herman Miller, Knoll, HAY and Design Within Reach.
exhibitioncreditsnamemillerknoll.money: Sales of office and home furniture; net sales were US$3.84 billion in fiscal 2026.

expertisefrance.name: Expertise France
expertisefrance.what: France's public agency for international technical cooperation, created at the end of 2014 from six public operators and placed under the foreign affairs and economy ministries.
expertisefrance.money: Revenue from the cooperation projects it carries out, put at €120 million a year by the economy ministry at its 2015 launch.

fairfieldcountybank|USA.name: Fairfield County Bank
fairfieldcountybank|USA.what: A community bank founded in 1871 in Ridgefield, Connecticut, where Ridgefield Savings Bank opened in the Old Hundred building, now the Aldrich Museum.
fairfieldcountybank|USA.money: Deposits, loans and wealth services for Fairfield County clients; the bank gives its size as $1.9 billion.

farrow.name: Farrow & Ball Ltd
farrow.what: A British paint and wallpaper maker started in 1946 by the chemists John Farrow and Richard Ball in Wimborne Minster, Dorset; the Danish coatings group Hempel bought it in 2021.
farrow.money: Sales of its paints and wallpapers through its own showrooms and stockists; net income £16.03 million in 2019/2020.
farrow.address: 33 Uddens Trading Estate, Wimborne, Dorset BH21 7NL

fcccommunities.name: FCC Communities Foundation
fcccommunities.what: A not-for-profit company set up in 1997 as Waste Recycling Environmental and renamed in 2019; it hands out Landfill Communities Fund grants across the UK.
fcccommunities.money: Money from the landfill activities of the waste company FCC Environment and its Severn Waste Services, paid under the Landfill Communities Fund.
fcccommunities.arts: It has granted over £295.5 million to more than 8,680 projects since 1997, including landscaping at the Stourbridge Glass Museum.

fdrationwalloniebruxelles.name: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
fdrationwalloniebruxelles.what: The government of the French Community of Belgium, one of the country's three language communities, established in 1980 and using the name Wallonia-Brussels Federation since 2011.
fdrationwalloniebruxelles.money: Federal transfers: shares of VAT (€9.21 billion) and personal income tax (€3.46 billion), together 94% of its 2025 revenue.

federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.name: Der Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.short: Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM)
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.what: The German federal government's office for culture and media policy, headed by a Minister of State, currently Wolfram Weimer, with staff in Bonn and Berlin.
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.money: The federal budget: the cabinet set about €2.5 billion for culture and media in 2026.

federalinbal|Mexico.name: Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes y Literatura
federalinbal|Mexico.what: A Mexican federal agency for the arts and arts education, created in 1946 and part of the Secretaría de Cultura since 2015; it sits in the Palacio de Bellas Artes.
federalinbal|Mexico.money: The Mexican federal government, as a deconcentrated body of the Secretaría de Cultura.
federalinbal|Mexico.arts: It runs 29 art schools and, with INAH, protects buildings declared artistic heritage.

federalministryforarts|Austria.name: Bundesministerium für Wohnen, Kunst, Kultur, Medien und Sport
federalministryforarts|Austria.short: Austrian Ministry for Arts and Culture (BMWKMS)
federalministryforarts|Austria.what: The Austrian federal ministry for housing, arts, culture, media and sport in Vienna, led by Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler; it holds the federal arts and culture brief.
federalministryforarts|Austria.arts: Its culture spending was €623.193 million in 2025, 1.47 percent less than in 2024, according to the Kunst- und Kulturbericht 2025.

ferroviedellostato.name: Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane S.p.A.
ferroviedellostato.what: Italy's state-owned railway holding company, based in Rome, whose units include Trenitalia, the network manager Rete Ferroviaria Italiana and the road operator ANAS.
ferroviedellostato.money: Its transport, infrastructure and logistics businesses; operating revenue €17.3 billion in 2025, including €9.2 billion from transport services.

finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.name: Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö
finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.short: Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture
finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.what: One of Finland's twelve ministries, in charge of education, science, culture, sport and youth; it began as the Ecclesiastical Department in 1809.
finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.money: The Finnish state budget; appropriations for its administrative branch are about €9 billion in 2026.

finnishministryofeducation|Finland.name: Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö
finnishministryofeducation|Finland.short: Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture
finnishministryofeducation|Finland.what: One of Finland's twelve ministries, in charge of education, science, culture, sport and youth; it began as the Ecclesiastical Department in 1809.
finnishministryofeducation|Finland.money: The Finnish state budget; appropriations for its administrative branch are about €9 billion in 2026.

finnmarkcounty|Norway.name: Finnmark fylkeskommune
finnmarkcounty|Norway.what: The regional government of Finnmark county in northern Norway, re-established on 1 January 2024 after four years merged into Troms og Finnmark, with its administration in Vadsø.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.money: The county budget set by its elected county council.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.arts: It runs a culture and cultural heritage service and gives grants to festivals in the county.

firsthorizonbank.name: First Horizon Bank
firsthorizonbank.what: A regional bank chartered in Memphis in 1864 as First National Bank of Memphis, now the banking unit of NYSE-listed First Horizon Corporation; it merged with IberiaBank in 2020.
firsthorizonbank.money: Banking across 12 southeastern US states; the group reported assets of US$88.7 billion in 2022.

flagart.name: The FLAG Art Foundation
flagart.what: A nonprofit exhibition space in New York, set up as a private operating foundation by the collector Glenn Fuhrman and open to the public since 2008.
flagart.money: Returns on net assets of $24.5 million (2024), mostly asset sales and dividends; Glenn Fuhrman is president and treasurer.
flagart.arts: It runs the Serpentine x FLAG Art Foundation Prize and lends contemporary works from the Fuhrman Family Foundation collection to museums.

flemishcommunity.name: Vlaamse Gemeenschap
flemishcommunity.what: One of Belgium's three language communities, responsible for culture and education in the Dutch-language area and Brussels; the Flemish Government under Matthias Diependaele is its executive.
flemishcommunity.money: The budget of the Flemish Government; its Department of Culture, Youth and Media pays arts subsidies under the Arts Decree.

flemishgovernment|Belgium.name: Vlaamse Regering
flemishgovernment|Belgium.what: The executive of the Flemish Community and Flemish Region of Belgium, led by a Minister-President and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
flemishgovernment|Belgium.money: The Flemish public budget, which its Department of Culture, Youth and Media spends on arts subsidies under the Arts Decree (Kunstendecreet).

florahewlett.name: William and Flora Hewlett Foundation
florahewlett.what: A US private foundation in Menlo Park, California, set up in 1966 by Hewlett-Packard co-founder Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora.
florahewlett.money: An endowment of about US$13.9 billion at the end of 2024, from the Hewletts' personal gifts; it is independent of HP.
florahewlett.arts: Its Performing Arts programme awarded US$40.5 million in 94 grants in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2024.

fondazionecariplo.name: Fondazione Cariplo
fondazionecariplo.what: A foundation of banking origin created in Milan in December 1991, when the Amato law split the Cariplo savings bank into this foundation and a commercial bank.
fondazionecariplo.money: Returns on an endowment of 8,207,623,005 euros (2023) built on its stake in the Cariplo bank, which later merged into Intesa Sanpaolo.

fondazionecrfirenze.name: Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze
fondazionecrfirenze.what: A Florence foundation of banking origin, created in April 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, a savings bank founded by 100 citizens in 1829, became a company.
fondazionecrfirenze.money: Returns on an endowment of about 2 billion euros inherited from the savings bank, including a holding in Intesa Sanpaolo.
fondazionecrfirenze.arts: Culture is one of its four missions, and its endowment includes an art collection.

fondazionecrt.name: Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino
fondazionecrt.what: A banking foundation formed in Turin in 1991, when the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino moved its banking business into a separate company; Italy's third-largest by assets.
fondazionecrt.money: Returns on its endowment, inherited from the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino and long including a large UniCredit shareholding.
fondazionecrt.arts: It has given more than 2 billion euros to over 50,000 projects in art, research, training, welfare, environment and innovation.

fondazionedivenezia.name: Fondazione di Venezia
fondazionedivenezia.what: An Italian banking foundation formed in 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Venezia, founded in 1822, was split into a bank and a foundation.
fondazionedivenezia.money: An endowment from its former ownership of the Cassa di Risparmio di Venezia, now part of Intesa Sanpaolo, in which it held 0.33% in 2013.
fondazionedivenezia.address: Palazzo Flangini, Calle Flangini 252, Cannaregio, 30121 Venice

fondazionedonnaregina.name: Fondazione Donnaregina per le arti contemporanee
fondazionedonnaregina.what: The foundation that runs Madre, the museum of contemporary art in Naples; Angela Tecce is president and Eugenio Viola became director in August 2026.
fondazionedonnaregina.money: Contributions mainly from the Campania Region: €3.4 million in 2021, with €4.7 million expected for 2022, according to Il Sole 24 Ore.
fondazionedonnaregina.renamed: This is the museum's own operating foundation, not an outside donor.

fondazionepasquinelli.name: Fondazione Francesco Pasquinelli
fondazionepasquinelli.what: A private foundation set up in Milan at the end of 2011 by Giuseppina Antognini, its president, in memory of her partner, the Milanese entrepreneur Francesco Pasquinelli.
fondazionepasquinelli.money: The private means of Giuseppina Antognini and the late Francesco Pasquinelli, whose art collection its exhibitions show.
fondazionepasquinelli.arts: It runs the exhibition series L'arte in una stanza at its Milan seat and launched a national network of youth orchestras and choirs.

forartsiniciative.name: Foundation for Arts Initiatives
forartsiniciative.what: A New York private foundation that grew out of the American Center in Paris, founded in 1931; it became a grantmaking foundation and began making grants in 1999.
forartsiniciative.money: An endowment from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture; net assets $32.9 million in 2025.
forartsiniciative.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and visual art institutions.

forartsinitiatives.name: Foundation for Arts Initiatives
forartsinitiatives.what: A New York grant-making foundation that began in 1931 as the American Center for Students and Artists in Paris and took its present name in 2008.
