forartsinitiatives.money: An endowment created from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture, now about $30 million.
forartsinitiatives.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and independent art spaces in many countries.

fordgrantstomuseum.name: Ford Foundation
fordgrantstomuseum.what: A private foundation set up in Michigan on 15 January 1936 by Edsel Ford and Henry Ford of the Ford Motor Company; based in New York since 1953.
fordgrantstomuseum.money: An endowment built on Ford Motor Company shares, sold between 1955 and 1974; about $16 billion in 2025.
fordgrantstomuseum.arts: Its Ford Foundation Symphony Program gave $80.2 million to 61 American orchestras from 1966 to 1976.

foster.name: Foster + Partners
foster.what: A British architecture and engineering firm founded in London in 1967 by Norman Foster, who keeps a controlling interest; Hennick & Company became its largest shareholder in 2021.
foster.money: Fees for architecture, engineering and design commissions worldwide; revenue £571.2 million in 2024/25.
foster.address: Riverside Three, Albert Wharf, 22 Hester Road, London SW11 4AN

foundingsponsoreczacba.name: Eczacıbaşı Holding A.Ş.
foundingsponsoreczacba.what: A Turkish industrial group founded in 1942 by Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı, with headquarters in Levent, Istanbul, and over 9,000 employees.
foundingsponsoreczacba.money: Sales of building products, healthcare products and natural resources in more than 90 markets, plus technology, finance, real estate and investment businesses.
foundingsponsoreczacba.arts: Its arts commitments include the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts, the İzmir Foundation for Culture, Arts and Education and the Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Foundation (1978).
foundingsponsoreczacba.address: Kanyon Ofis, Büyükdere Street 185, Levent 34394, Istanbul

fourpillarsgin.name: Four Pillars Gin
fourpillarsgin.what: A gin distillery founded in Healesville, Victoria, in 2013 by Cameron Mackenzie, Stuart Gregor and Matt Jones; wholly owned by the drinks group Lion since July 2023.
fourpillarsgin.money: Sales of its gin; Lion bought half in 2019 and the rest in 2023, placing it in its Four Corners Global Spirits division.

foyle.name: The Foyle Foundation
foyle.what: A UK grant-making charity formed in 2000 to carry out the will of bookseller Christina Foyle; it closed in December 2025 and entered voluntary liquidation in June 2026.
foyle.money: The estate of Christina Foyle, daughter of a founder of Foyles bookshop on Charing Cross Road, London.
foyle.arts: From 2000 to 2025 it gave over £185M to almost 7,500 charities and state schools, mainly for arts and learning.

frankenthaler.name: Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Inc.
frankenthaler.what: A New York non-profit formed by the painter Helen Frankenthaler in 1984; it became active in 2013, when her estate closed.
frankenthaler.money: Endowed by the artist; net assets were $173,182,625 in 2024, when sales of assets brought 86.3% of revenue.
frankenthaler.arts: Its Frankenthaler Climate Initiative made its first grants, totalling $5.1 million, in July 2021.

frderstiftungderhamburgerkunsthalle.name: Förderstiftung Hamburger Kunsthalle
frderstiftungderhamburgerkunsthalle.what: A private-law foundation in Hamburg, set up on private initiative to support the Hamburger Kunsthalle; the Hans Brökel Stiftung provided its founding capital.
frderstiftungderhamburgerkunsthalle.money: Donations, endowment gifts and bequests that build its capital; it spends the interest on the museum.

freelands.name: Freelands Foundation
freelands.what: A London art education charity set up in 2015 by the media executive Elisabeth Murdoch, who chairs its board.
freelands.money: Investment income on a large 2019 donation, plus services donated by Freelands Group, owned by a trust of which Elisabeth Murdoch is a beneficiary.
freelands.arts: In 2025 it paid grants totalling £1,475,492 to 28 organisations.

frenchembassy|Paraguay.name: Ambassade de France au Paraguay
frenchembassy|Paraguay.what: France's diplomatic mission in Asunción, sharing a building with the European Union delegation; Jean-Philippe Gavois is ambassador.
frenchembassy|Paraguay.money: The French state; the embassy calls the budget for its cultural cooperation in Paraguay modest.
frenchembassy|Paraguay.arts: With the artists' association Gente de Arte it has run Paraguay's main visual arts prize, the Prix Matisse, for 25 years, and added photography and documentary prizes in 2018.
frenchembassy|Paraguay.address: Avda. General Santos 465 c/ España, Asunción

frenchministryofculturesubventions|Franc.name: Ministère de la Culture
frenchministryofculturesubventions|Franc.what: The French government ministry for national museums, historic monuments and the arts; the post of culture minister was created on 8 January 1959 for André Malraux.

frenchstate|France.name: Ministère de la Culture
frenchstate|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchstate|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.
frenchstate|France.renamed: Same body as the atlas entry ministredelaculture; the DRAC named in two sentences are the ministry's regional offices.

friendsofcentrepompidou.name: Les Amis du Centre Pompidou
friendsofcentrepompidou.what: A French association recognised as of public utility, founded in 1903 as the Société des Amis du Musée du Luxembourg and renamed Amis du Centre Pompidou in 2017.
friendsofcentrepompidou.money: Members' subscriptions, donations, bequests and dedicated funds, plus its annual Dîner des Amis.
friendsofcentrepompidou.arts: Its twelve acquisition committees take part, with the curators, in choosing new works for the Musée national d'art moderne.

friendsofweissenhofestate.name: Freunde der Weissenhofsiedlung e.V.
friendsofweissenhofestate.what: A nonprofit association registered in Stuttgart on 17 November 1979 to restore the 1927 Weissenhof Estate; Bodo Rasch, Mia Seeger and Frei Otto formed its first board.
friendsofweissenhofestate.money: Members' dues of €50 a year; since 2006 it runs the Weissenhof Museum in the Le Corbusier House for the City of Stuttgart.

frittordprojects.name: Stiftelsen Fritt Ord
frittordprojects.what: A Norwegian private foundation for free expression, set up in Oslo on 7 June 1974 by Narvesen kiosk executives Jens Henrik Nordlie and Finn Skedsmo and lawyer Jens Christian Hauge.
frittordprojects.money: An endowment that began as the shares of the Narvesen kiosk company, which it sold in stages until November 2001.

fukutake.name: Fukutake Foundation
fukutake.what: A Japanese foundation that runs Benesse Art Site Naoshima with Benesse Corporation, grown from a foundation Soichiro Fukutake set up in 2004.
fukutake.money: A personal endowment from Soichiro Fukutake, former head of Benesse, the Okayama correspondence education and publishing company.
fukutake.arts: It has been a founding patron of CIMAM, the international committee for modern art museums, since 2000.

fultoncounty|USA.name: Fulton County, Georgia
fultoncounty|USA.what: The county government of Fulton County, Georgia, led by a seven-member Board of Commissioners and based at the Fulton County Government Center in Atlanta.
fultoncounty|USA.money: The county budget, funded in part by property tax, which the FY2026 budget kept at 8.87 mills.
fultoncounty|USA.arts: Its Department of Arts & Culture runs the Contracts for Services programme: $2,857,643 in initial FY2026 awards to 200 organisations.

fundacicatalunyalapedrera.name: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera
fundacicatalunyalapedrera.what: A private Catalan special foundation founded in 2013 from the transformation of the savings bank Caixa d'Estalvis de Catalunya, Tarragona i Manresa; it runs La Pedrera in Barcelona.
fundacicatalunyalapedrera.money: Visitor income from La Pedrera above all, plus its nature sites, programmes and group companies; group income was €66.6 million in 2025.

fundacilacaixa.name: Fundación "la Caixa"
fundacilacaixa.what: A Spanish banking foundation that grew out of the la Caixa savings bank, headquartered in Barcelona since March 2025.
fundacilacaixa.money: Dividends from its holding company CriteriaCaixa, which holds 31 per cent of CaixaBank and 9.99 per cent of Telefónica.
fundacilacaixa.arts: Its social work budget, which covers cultural as well as social and scientific projects, is €710 million for 2026.

fundacinamador.name: Fundación Amador
fundacinamador.what: A Panamanian non-profit foundation established in 2000 that operates and cares for the Biomuseo, Frank Gehry's museum of biodiversity in Panama City.
fundacinamador.money: Tickets, school and tourist visits, events, service contracts and donations; in 2016 Panama's state agreed $18 million for the museum's second phase.

fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.name: Fundación Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat
fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.what: A private Argentine foundation set up by Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat, owner of the cement maker Loma Negra; it was first named Fundación Alfredo Fortabat y Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat.
fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.money: The fortune of Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat from Loma Negra, Argentina's largest cement maker, whose 80% stake she sold to Camargo Correa in 2005.
fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.arts: It has given more than $40 million to Argentine charities since 1976.

fundacinamparo.name: Fundación Amparo
fundacinamparo.what: A Mexican private foundation set up in 1979 by the banker Manuel Espinosa Yglesias in honour of his wife; it sponsors the Museo Amparo in Puebla, opened in 1991.
fundacinamparo.money: The fortune of Manuel Espinosa Yglesias, general director and major shareholder of the bank Bancomer from 1959 until the 1982 bank expropriation.

fundacinbancariabbk.name: Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa Fundación Bancaria
fundacinbancariabbk.what: A Basque banking foundation formed in 2014 when the Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa savings bank converted into a foundation; it is the majority shareholder of Kutxabank.
fundacinbancariabbk.money: Its Kutxabank stake: 1,140,000 shares, 57% of the bank's capital, which made up its €2,774 million net worth at the 2014 conversion.

fundacinbancosantander.name: Fundación Banco Santander
fundacinbancosantander.what: The corporate foundation of the Santander banking group, based in Madrid; it shows the bank's art collection at the Sala de Arte Santander in Boadilla del Monte.
fundacinbancosantander.money: Mostly dividends on its Banco Santander shares, held since April 1992; its income was €31,328,998 in 2025.

fundacinbbva.name: Fundación BBVA
fundacinbbva.what: The foundation of the Spanish banking group BBVA, with headquarters in Bilbao and an office in Madrid.
fundacinbbva.money: The BBVA Group, whose corporate social responsibility the foundation carries out.

fundacinbotn.name: Fundación Botín
fundacinbotn.what: A family foundation set up in Santander on 18 April 1964 by Marcelino Botín Sanz de Sautuola, vice-chairman of Banco de Santander, and his wife Carmen Yllera.
fundacinbotn.money: An endowment that began with Marcelino Botín's bequest of 500 million pesetas, which his widow then increased.
fundacinbotn.arts: In 2024 Jaime Botín gave it portraits from his collection for a room at Centro Botín, with an annual financial endowment.

fundacincarlosslim.name: Fundación Carlos Slim, A.C.
fundacincarlosslim.what: The philanthropic body of Carlos Slim Helú and his family, created in Mexico City in 1986 as Asociación Carso A.C. by Slim and his wife Soumaya Domit.
fundacincarlosslim.money: The fortune of Carlos Slim Helú, drawn from his holdings in Mexican companies through his conglomerate Grupo Carso.

fundacinmutuamadrilea.name: Fundación Mutua Madrileña
fundacinmutuamadrilea.what: The foundation of the Spanish insurer Mutua Madrileña, set up in 2003 for medical research and widened to social, road safety and cultural work in 2009.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.money: Funds from Mutua Madrileña, the Madrid insurer founded in 1930 that sells car, health and life insurance.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.arts: Cultural work takes about a quarter of the foundation's resources (2024).

fundacinpaiz.name: Fundación Paiz para la Educación y la Cultura
fundacinpaiz.what: A Guatemalan family foundation that grew from scholarships Graciela Andrade de Paiz began giving in the early 1970s; it has held the Bienal de Arte Paiz since 1978.
fundacinpaiz.money: The Paiz family and public donations; its marimba festival began in 1980 in the family's Paiz stores.
fundacinpaiz.arts: It runs the Bienal de Arte Paiz, the Festival de Marimba, the Premio Monteforte Toledo literary prize and a collection of about 300 Guatemalan works.

fundacinprosegur.name: Fundación Prosegur
fundacinprosegur.what: The corporate foundation of Prosegur, the Madrid security company Herberto Gut founded in 1976; it turned its focus to social action and education in 2005.
fundacinprosegur.money: Support from Prosegur, whose guarding, cash-in-transit and security technology businesses had €4,291 million revenue in 2017.
fundacinprosegur.arts: It has worked with the Fundación Amigos del Museo del Prado since 2006 and runs a programme called El Arte como Motor de Cambio.

fundaomanuelantniodamota.name: Fundação Manuel António da Mota
fundaomanuelantniodamota.what: A corporate foundation of the Portuguese construction group Mota-Engil, set up by public deed in Porto on 18 December 2009 and declared of public utility in 2014.
fundaomanuelantniodamota.money: Funds from the Mota-Engil construction and engineering group, which calls the foundation an instrument of its social responsibility policy.

fundaomillenniumbcp.name: Fundação Millennium bcp
fundaomillenniumbcp.what: The foundation of the Portuguese bank Banco Comercial Português, set up by the bank in 1991, working in culture, education and social development.
fundaomillenniumbcp.money: Funds from the bank, Portugal's largest private bank, which made €856.0 million net income in 2023.

fundos.name: Fundación Obra Social de Castilla y León
fundos.what: A private foundation created in 2015 from the social fund of the Caja España-Duero savings bank; based at Casa Botines in León, it works across Castilla y León.
fundos.money: The buildings, art and archives of the former Caja España-Duero social fund, plus revenue from the Casa Botines museum and its MonteCredit pawn loans.
fundos.arts: Its collection and historical archive came from the savings bank, whose social fund held more than 10,500 artworks in 2014.
fundos.address: Casa Botines, Plaza de San Marcelo 5, 24002 León

gador.name: Gador S.A.
gador.what: An Argentine pharmaceutical company founded in 1940 by Dr. Nicolás Gador, joined in 1948 by Américo and Jorge Balla, whose descendants still sit on its board.
gador.money: Sales of its medicines; it makes more than 2 billion tablets a year and holds over 800 product registrations worldwide.

galeriemaxhetzler.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galeriemaxhetzler.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded by Max Hetzler in Stuttgart in September 1974; it has spaces in Berlin, Paris and London and a venue in Marfa, Texas.
galeriemaxhetzler.money: Sales of work by the more than sixty artists it represents.

galleriessuchasgagosian.name: Gagosian
galleriessuchasgagosian.what: A commercial art gallery owned and directed by the dealer Larry Gagosian, who opened his first gallery in Los Angeles in 1980; it had 19 exhibition spaces in 2024.
galleriessuchasgagosian.money: Sales of artworks; a 2011 Wall Street Journal survey estimated its annual sales at about $1 billion.

garantibbvainternational.name: Garanti BBVA International N.V.
garantibbvainternational.what: A Dutch bank set up in Amsterdam in 1990 as a subsidiary of Istanbul's Türkiye Garanti Bankası, now Garanti BBVA, of which Spain's BBVA owns 85.97%.
garantibbvainternational.money: Its banking business within the Garanti BBVA group, which had US$15.53 billion revenue in 2024.

gasterra.name: GasTerra B.V.
gasterra.what: A Dutch natural gas wholesaler created in Groningen in 2005 from the split of Gasunie, owned by Shell (25%), ExxonMobil (25%) and the Dutch state (50%).
gasterra.money: Sales of natural gas, revenue €9.6 billion in 2017; after the end of Groningen field production it is winding down by 31 December 2026.

gazpromfinancedparks.name: PJSC Gazprom
gazpromfinancedparks.what: Russia's state-owned energy company, founded on 8 August 1989; the Russian government holds 50.23% and it is headquartered in the Lakhta Center, Saint Petersburg.
gazpromfinancedparks.money: Sales of natural gas, oil and petrochemicals and gas pipeline transport; revenue US$115 billion in 2025.

gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.name: Gemeente Leiden
gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Leiden in South Holland, with 127,046 inhabitants in January 2023, run by a council and a college of mayor and aldermen.
gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.arts: It has owned Museum De Lakenhal, its municipal museum of fine art and history, since the museum opened in 1874.

genelec.name: Genelec Oy
genelec.what: A Finnish maker of active loudspeakers for studios, broadcasting and film, founded in 1978 by Ilpo Martikainen and Topi Partanen, with its factory and headquarters in Iisalmi.
genelec.money: Sales of its loudspeakers and studio monitors: revenue of €43,614,000 in 2025, with 203 employees.

generalpartnerkomernbanka.name: Komerční banka, a.s.
generalpartnerkomernbanka.what: A Czech bank founded in 1990 from the commercial arm of the State Bank of Czechoslovakia, based in Prague; Société Générale bought the state's 60% stake in 2001.
generalpartnerkomernbanka.money: Banking for individuals, businesses and municipalities in Czechia; net income was CZK 17.4 billion in 2024.

georgiapower.name: Georgia Power
georgiapower.what: An investor-owned electric utility in Atlanta, the largest of the four utilities owned by Southern Company; it began in 1902 as the Georgia Railway and Power Company.
georgiapower.money: Electricity sales to more than 2.8 million customers in Georgia, generated at coal, gas and nuclear plants including Plant Scherer and Plant Vogtle.

germanfederalforeignoffice|Germany.name: Auswärtiges Amt
germanfederalforeignoffice|Germany.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, first set up in 1870 and re-established in 1951, seated at Werderscher Markt in Berlin and led by Minister Johann Wadephul.
germanfederalforeignoffice|Germany.money: The German federal budget, which gave the ministry €6.302 billion in 2021.

germanfederalforeignoffice|Poland.name: Auswärtiges Amt
germanfederalforeignoffice|Poland.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, first set up in 1870 and re-established in 1951, seated at Werderscher Markt in Berlin and led by Minister Johann Wadephul.
germanfederalforeignoffice|Poland.money: The German federal budget, which gave the ministry €6.302 billion in 2021.

germanykfw.name: KfW
germanykfw.what: Germany's state-owned development bank, a public-law institution formed in 1948 under the Marshall Plan and based in Frankfurt; the federal government owns 80% and the states 20%.
germanykfw.money: It raises over 90% of its funds on capital markets, mainly through bonds guaranteed by the federal government.

germanysforeignoffice.name: Auswärtiges Amt
germanysforeignoffice.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanysforeignoffice.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.name: Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst am Museum Ludwig Köln e.V.
gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.what: A registered non-profit association in Cologne, founded in 1985 by collectors from the Rhineland to support the Museum Ludwig through acquisitions, exhibitions and projects.
gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.money: Dues from more than 650 members: €660 a year for an individual and €2,500 for a company.
gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.arts: Its annual Wolfgang Hahn Prize puts up to €100,000 toward buying the winner's work for the Museum Ludwig; Lee Ufan won in 2026.

ghanatourismauthority.name: Ghana Tourism Authority
ghanatourismauthority.what: Ghana's state tourism agency under the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts; founded in 1960 as the Ghana Tourist Board and renamed by Act 817 of 2011.
ghanatourismauthority.money: The Tourism Development Fund, fed by a 1% levy patrons pay at tourism businesses since October 2012, plus government money.

gijncity|Spain.name: Ayuntamiento de Gijón/Xixón
gijncity|Spain.what: The city council of Gijón in Asturias, seated on the Plaza Mayor and led since 2023 by mayor Carmen Moriyón of Foro Asturias.
gijncity|Spain.money: The municipal budget, voted by the council plenary, the 2025 budget taking effect after publication in the BOPA on 20 December 2024.

gilbertfamily.name: Gilbert Family Foundation
gilbertfamily.what: The family foundation of Dan Gilbert, co-founder, majority owner and chairman of Rocket Mortgage, and his wife Jennifer Gilbert; based in Detroit and US tax-exempt since October 2021.
gilbertfamily.money: Contributions of $130,606,908 in 2024, 99.1% of its revenue; the Gilberts' fortune comes from Rocket Mortgage.

gilberts.name: Gilbert Family Foundation
gilberts.what: The family foundation of Dan Gilbert, co-founder, majority owner and chairman of Rocket Mortgage, and his wife Jennifer Gilbert; based in Detroit and US tax-exempt since October 2021.
gilberts.money: Contributions of $130,606,908 in 2024, 99.1% of its revenue; the Gilberts' fortune comes from Rocket Mortgage.

globalradio.name: Global Media & Entertainment Limited
globalradio.what: A British media company founded in 2007 by Ashley Tabor-King with backing from his father Michael Tabor; it owns Heart, Capital, Classic FM, LBC and other radio stations.
globalradio.money: Advertising sold on its radio stations and on its outdoor billboards, a business it built by buying Primesight and Outdoor Plus in 2018.

goethe.name: Goethe-Institut e.V.
goethe.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association founded in 1951 and based in Munich, with institutes in 100 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goethe.money: Mainly the German federal budget through annual grants from the Federal Foreign Office, plus its own course fees and money from sponsors and patrons.
goethe.arts: A framework agreement signed with the Foreign Office in 1976 sets its tasks; it began its cultural programme work in 1968.

goetheinstitut.name: Goethe-Institut e.V.
goetheinstitut.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goetheinstitut.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.name: Golden Harvest Group
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.what: A Bangladeshi conglomerate based in Dhaka that started as a commodity brokerage and now runs food, dairy, IT, logistics, property and insurance companies; Rajeeb Samdani is managing director.
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.money: Its companies, among them frozen food, Bloop ice cream, a Domino's Pizza joint venture, Nippon Express Bangladesh and Sonali Life Insurance.
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.arts: It lists the Samdani Art Foundation, set up in 2011 by Nadia and Rajeeb Samdani and producer of the Dhaka Art Summit, as its CSR work.
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.address: Shanta Western Tower, Level 5, 186 Gulshan-Tejgaon Link Road, Tejgaon I/A, Dhaka 1208

goldshoman.name: Abdul Hameed Shoman Foundation
goldshoman.what: A non-profit foundation that Arab Bank set up in Amman in 1978 to support science, the humanities and culture in the Arab world.
goldshoman.money: Arab Bank's profits: in 2011 the bank gave it over 8 million Jordanian dinars, about 87% of its community investment budget.
goldshoman.arts: It runs a cultural forum, film screenings and musical evenings in Amman, and gives cultural grants and an award for creativity.

goldsmith.name: Horace W. Goldsmith Foundation
goldsmith.what: A New York private foundation created in 1955 by Horace Ward Goldsmith, who bought a New York Stock Exchange seat in 1927.
goldsmith.money: Investment returns, chiefly gains on asset sales and dividends, on assets of $826 million in 2024.

grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.name: Grand Casino de Lyon Le Pharaon
grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.what: A casino with slot machines and gaming tables at the Cité Internationale in Lyon's 6th arrondissement, run by Groupe Partouche, the casino group Isidore Partouche founded in 1973.
grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.money: Gaming revenue; its parent Groupe Partouche reported €460.2 million of revenue for the year to 31 October 2025, €415 million from casinos.
grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.address: 70 quai Charles de Gaulle, Cité Internationale, 69006 Lyon

greekministryofculture|Greece.name: Hellenic Ministry of Culture
greekministryofculture|Greece.what: The Greek government ministry for cultural heritage and the arts, set up on 26 August 1971 as the Ministry of Culture and Sciences; Lina Mendoni is minister.
greekministryofculture|Greece.money: The Greek state budget, which allotted it €189,293,000 for 2025.
greekministryofculture|Greece.arts: Its agencies include the Acropolis Museum, the National Gallery in Athens, the National Theatre of Greece and the Athens Epidaurus Festival.

greenbergfamily.name: Minto Group
greenbergfamily.what: The Ottawa family behind the Minto Group, a real estate company founded in Ottawa in 1955 by four Greenberg brothers; Roger Greenberg is its executive chairman.
greenbergfamily.money: Profits of the Minto Group, a privately held real estate company active across North America.
greenbergfamily.arts: The family gives to health, sports, arts and education causes.

grnlandsbanken.name: GrønlandsBANKEN A/S
grnlandsbanken.what: One of Greenland's two commercial banks, founded by Danish banks on 26 May 1967, listed on the Copenhagen stock exchange and headquartered in Nuuk.
grnlandsbanken.money: Lending, deposits and services for about 50,000 customers in Greenland: profit before tax of DKK 181.4 million in 2025.

groupedassault.name: Groupe Industriel Marcel Dassault
groupedassault.what: The Dassault family's holding company, which traces its start to the aircraft maker Marcel Dassault set up in 1929; Éric Trappier has led it since 2025.
groupedassault.money: Its holdings: 62% of Dassault Aviation, which owns 26% of the defence group Thales, 45.1% of Dassault Systèmes, Groupe Figaro and Immobilière Dassault.
groupedassault.arts: It owns the Paris auction house Artcurial and runs a group patronage programme.

groupegalerieslafayette.name: Groupe Galeries Lafayette
groupegalerieslafayette.what: A French retail group owned by the Moulin family, grown from a Paris shop Théophile Bader and Alphonse Kahn opened in 1894; it runs Galeries Lafayette stores and La Redoute.
groupegalerieslafayette.money: Retail sales in its stores and brands, €4.5 billion a year, and property held through its real estate arm Citynove.

grupograda.name: Grupo Grada
grupograda.what: A Panamanian communications and technology group in Panama City that owns the IT supplier Data Serve and radio stations including Estereo Azul, Antena 8 and Crush 89.7.
grupograda.money: Sales of IT equipment, audio and video systems and services through Data Serve, in business since 1989, and advertising on its radio stations.
grupograda.address: Av. Ricardo Miró, Urb. El Carmen, Panama City

grupopromerica.name: Grupo Promerica
grupopromerica.what: A regional banking group that grew from Banpro, the Nicaraguan bank Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga founded in Managua in November 1991 with 133 partners; it now operates in nine countries.
grupopromerica.money: Interest and fees from its banks: Banpro in Nicaragua, Banco Promerica in five countries, Produbanco in Ecuador and St. Georges Bank.

gstaserlachiusfinearts.name: Gösta Serlachius Fine Arts Foundation
gstaserlachiusfinearts.what: A private fine arts foundation in Mänttä, Finland, set up in 1933 by the industrialist Gösta Serlachius to keep his art collection and build a museum.
gstaserlachiusfinearts.money: An endowment from Gösta Serlachius: nearly 3,000 shares in G.A. Serlachius, his family's paper company, plus property.
gstaserlachiusfinearts.arts: Its collections hold more than 10,000 works, known for Finnish Golden Age art and old European masters.

gucci.name: Guccio Gucci S.p.A.
gucci.what: An Italian luxury fashion house founded in Florence in 1921 by Guccio Gucci and owned since 1999 by the French luxury group Kering.
gucci.money: Sales of clothing, leather goods, shoes and accessories: 7.65 billion euros in 2024.

gulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
gulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
gulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

gulfstream.name: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation
gulfstream.what: An American maker of business jets, a subsidiary of the defence contractor General Dynamics since 1999, headquartered in Savannah, Georgia, where it set up in 1967.
gulfstream.money: Sales and servicing of its business jets, such as the G650, G700 and G800; General Dynamics' aerospace division brought 23% of group revenue in 2024.

gyeongnam.name: Gyeongsangnam-do Provincial Government
gyeongnam.what: The government of South Gyeongsang Province in southeastern South Korea, seated in Changwon since 1983; Park Wan-su is governor.
gyeongnam.money: Provincial taxes and national government money: a 2026 budget of KRW 14.2845 trillion, as proposed in November 2025.

habasit.name: Habasit International AG
habasit.what: A Swiss maker of conveyor and power transmission belts, founded in 1946 by Fernand and Alice Habegger, with its head office and a main plant in Reinach, Basel-Landschaft.
habasit.money: Sales of its belts and conveyor components to food, packaging, printing and other industries in more than 70 countries.

hamber.name: The Hamber Foundation
hamber.what: A private foundation in Vancouver set up in 1964 by Aldyen Irene Hamber in memory of her husband Eric Hamber, Lieutenant-Governor of British Columbia from 1937 to 1941.
hamber.money: An endowment from Aldyen Hamber: a C$1 million gift in 1964 and the residue of her estate after her death in 1988.
hamber.arts: It makes grants for cultural, educational and charitable projects in British Columbia.

hanafinancial.name: Hana Financial Group Inc.
hanafinancial.what: A South Korean financial holding company in Seoul, formed in 2005 around Hana Bank; it bought control of Korea Exchange Bank in 2012.
hanafinancial.money: Interest and fees from its bank, card, securities, insurance and capital companies: net profit of 4.0 trillion won (KRW) in 2025.

hannoverrck.name: Hannover Rück SE
hannoverrck.what: A German reinsurance company founded on 6 June 1966 and based in Hannover, one of the world's three largest reinsurers; Talanx holds 50.2% of its voting rights.
hannoverrck.money: Reinsurance premiums paid by insurers worldwide for property, casualty, life and health risks, about €33 billion gross a year.

hansu.name: Laurenz-Stiftung
hansu.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
hansu.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
hansu.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

hanswerner.name: H.W. & J. Hector Stiftung zu Weinheim
hanswerner.what: A private foundation in Weinheim set up in 1995 by Josephine Hector and Hans-Werner Hector, a co-founder of SAP; the couple added Hector Stiftung II in 2008.
hanswerner.money: The fortune of Hans-Werner Hector, who sold most of his SAP shares in 1996.
hanswerner.arts: It funds the Hector Kunstpreis, awarded yearly by the Kunsthalle Mannheim, and supports the Sammlung Prinzhorn in Heidelberg.

harbourviewequity.name: HarbourView Equity Partners
harbourviewequity.what: An investment firm in Newark, New Jersey, that buys music catalogues and other entertainment rights, founded in October 2021 by Sherrese Clarke Soares.
harbourviewequity.money: Investors' capital, starting with up to $1 billion from Apollo Global Management, and royalties from its catalogues; regulatory assets were $3.88 billion at end 2025.

hartwig.name: Hartwig Art Foundation
hartwig.what: A private art foundation in Amsterdam, set up in 2020 by Rob Defares, a Dutch electronic trading billionaire, to buy art for Dutch state collections.
hartwig.money: The fortune Rob Defares made in electronic trading.
hartwig.arts: It is turning Amsterdam's former courthouse into the Hartwig Museum, due to open in 2028.

hassoplattner.name: Hasso Plattner Foundation
hassoplattner.what: A charitable civil-law foundation in Potsdam, set up in 2015 by SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, that runs its own projects in science, education, conservation and culture.
hassoplattner.money: An endowment of a double-digit billion euros gifted by Hasso Plattner, invested by its own investment office in Potsdam.
hassoplattner.arts: It also runs the DAS MINSK Kunsthaus in Potsdam and backs the Wildenstein Plattner Institute.

hauser.name: Hauser & Wirth
hauser.what: A commercial art gallery founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.
hauser.money: Its gallery business: it represents over 80 artists and estates, including those of Philip Guston and Louise Bourgeois.

hawaiisuchaskamehamehaschools.name: Kamehameha Schools
hawaiisuchaskamehamehaschools.what: A private school system in Hawaiʻi created under the will of Princess Bernice Pauahi Bishop, whose trust opened its first school in Honolulu in 1887.
hawaiisuchaskamehamehaschools.money: An endowment of $15.1 billion (2022) built on Bishop's bequest of 375,000 acres; her estate is Hawaiʻi's largest private landowner.

helenfrankenthaler.name: Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Inc.
helenfrankenthaler.what: A New York non-profit formed by the painter Helen Frankenthaler in 1984; it became active in 2013, when her estate closed.
helenfrankenthaler.money: The artist's estate: net assets of $173,182,625 at the end of 2024, when sales of assets brought 86.3% of revenue.
helenfrankenthaler.arts: It runs the Frankenthaler Climate Initiative and, since 2018, the Frankenthaler Prints Initiative for university-affiliated museums.
helenfrankenthaler.address: 134 West 26th Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10001

helis.name: The Helis Foundation
helis.what: A Louisiana private foundation established and funded in 1955 by the family of William Helis, a Greek emigrant to New Orleans who made a fortune in oil.
helis.money: The Helis family's oil fortune, plus art funds bequeathed by Diana Helis Henry and Adrienne Helis Malvin. Total assets were US$82,984,093 in 2024.
helis.arts: Its Art Funds paid for Prospect.3's Basquiat and the Bayou and for installing Lynda Benglis's The Wave of the World in New Orleans City Park.
helis.address: 201 St. Charles Avenue, Suite 2600, New Orleans, LA

henrymoore.name: The Henry Moore Foundation
henrymoore.what: A charity founded in 1977 by sculptor Henry Moore and his family, with headquarters at his former home in Perry Green, Hertfordshire, and the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds.
henrymoore.money: A founding gift from Henry Moore and his family; it also administers the sale and exhibition of Moore's work.
henrymoore.arts: Henry Moore Grants fund sculpture exhibitions, commissions, acquisitions and research, with grants of up to £20,000 in the main categories.
henrymoore.address: Dane Tree House, Perry Green, Much Hadham SG10 6EE

heritavzw.name: Herita vzw
heritavzw.what: A non-profit association in Antwerp that manages, restores and opens historic sites in Flanders as the region's National Trust; it has about forty permanent staff.
heritavzw.money: An annual operating subsidy from the Flemish government, €3,250,000 in 2023, plus membership and donations.
heritavzw.arts: Its sites include Paleis op de Meir in Antwerp, Kasteel van Beersel and Abdij van Herkenrode; the Flemish government approved its 2026 to 2030 agreement in December 2025.

hermannreemtsma.name: Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung
hermannreemtsma.what: A private foundation set up in Hamburg in 1988 by Hermann-Hinrich Reemtsma in memory of his father, the cigarette manufacturer Hermann F. Reemtsma.
hermannreemtsma.money: The fortune of its founder Hermann-Hinrich Reemtsma, a shareholder in his family's Reemtsma cigarette company, put at about €800 million in 2005.
hermannreemtsma.arts: In 2025 it granted €5,942,369 to 55 culture projects, mainly the care of listed buildings and works of art in northern and eastern Germany.

hermannreemtsmaforresearch.name: Hermann Reemtsma Stiftung
hermannreemtsmaforresearch.what: A private foundation set up in Hamburg in 1988 by Hermann-Hinrich Reemtsma in memory of his father, the cigarette manufacturer Hermann F. Reemtsma.
hermannreemtsmaforresearch.money: The fortune of its founder Hermann-Hinrich Reemtsma, a shareholder in his family's Reemtsma cigarette company, put at about €800 million in 2005.
hermannreemtsmaforresearch.arts: In 2025 it granted €5,942,369 to 55 culture projects, mainly the care of listed buildings and works of art in northern and eastern Germany.

heydaraliyev.name: Heydar Aliyev Foundation
heydaraliyev.what: A foundation in Baku created in 2004 by President Ilham Aliyev and named after his father; First Lady and Vice President Mehriban Aliyeva is its president.
heydaraliyev.money: It does not declare its funding sources, which the press has criticised; it banks with the state-controlled International Bank of Azerbaijan.
heydaraliyev.arts: It funded renovation work at the Louvre and the Palace of Versailles, stained glass at Strasbourg Cathedral and, under a 2012 agreement, the Vatican catacombs.

hikma.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
hikma.what: A British multinational drug company founded in Amman, Jordan, in 1978 by Samih Darwazah, headquartered in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange.
hikma.money: Sales of generic, branded and injectable medicines: core revenue of US$3,349 million in 2025.

himalayanbank.name: Himalayan Bank Limited
himalayanbank.what: A private commercial bank in Nepal, incorporated in 1992 by Nepali individuals with the Employees Provident Fund and Pakistan's Habib Bank; its head office is in Kamaladi, Kathmandu.
himalayanbank.money: Banking in Nepal through 190 branches; it merged with Civil Bank in February 2023, and its promoter group holds 70% of its shares.

hiscox.name: Hiscox Ltd
hiscox.what: An insurance group listed on the London Stock Exchange and based in Hamilton, Bermuda, grown from a Lloyd's of London underwriting agency that began in 1901.
hiscox.money: Specialist insurance, including property, casualty, kidnap and ransom and hacking cover: revenue of £4,883.7 million in 2025.

historicenvironmentscotland.name: Historic Environment Scotland
historicenvironmentscotland.what: A Scottish non-departmental public body with charitable status, formed on 1 October 2015 from Historic Scotland and RCAHMS, that cares for Scotland's historic environment; based in Edinburgh.
historicenvironmentscotland.money: Mostly Scottish Government grant-in-aid and admissions to its properties; grant-in-aid is £69.3 million in its 2025-26 plan.
historicenvironmentscotland.address: Longmore House, Salisbury Place, Edinburgh EH9 1SH

hivos.name: Hivos
hivos.what: A Dutch human rights and development organisation founded in 1968 by the Dutch Humanist Association and others, with its global office in The Hague.
hivos.money: Grants from donors including the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sida, the European Union, the Global Fund and the Dutch Postcode Lottery.

holtrenfrew.name: Holt, Renfrew & Co., Limited
holtrenfrew.what: A Canadian luxury department store chain founded in Quebec City in 1837, owned since 1986 by the Weston family's Wittington Investments and based in Toronto.
holtrenfrew.money: Sales at its six luxury department stores in four Canadian provinces.

honeywell.name: Honeywell International Inc.
honeywell.what: An American industrial technology company formed in 1999 by the merger of Honeywell Inc. and AlliedSignal, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina; it spun off its aerospace business in June 2026.
honeywell.money: Sales of building automation, industrial automation and energy and sustainability technology.

honolulubeerworks.name: Honolulu Beerworks
honolulubeerworks.what: A craft brewery opened in 2014 in Kaka'ako, Honolulu, by Geoff Seideman and his wife Charmayne; its taproom is now on Hart Street in Kalihi.
honolulubeerworks.money: Beer sales at its taproom and to wholesale accounts, plus event bookings and online merchandise.

horgenglarus.name: AG Möbelfabrik Horgenglarus
horgenglarus.what: A Swiss maker of chairs and tables, founded by Emil Baumann in Horgen in 1880 and producing in Glarus since 1902; owned by the von Nordeck family since 2011.
horgenglarus.money: Sales of its chairs, tables and church furniture to homes, offices, museums, restaurants and hotels; its parent is v. Nordeck International Holding AG.

hospitalalemn.name: Hospital Alemán
hospitalalemn.what: A non-profit civil association that runs a private hospital in Buenos Aires, founded on 26 August 1867 and governed by members of Argentina's German-speaking communities.
hospitalalemn.money: Patient care and its own health plan, which has more than 50,000 members.

hrmann.name: Hörmann KG Verkaufsgesellschaft
hrmann.what: The sales company of the Hörmann Group, a family-owned door maker founded by August Hörmann in Bielefeld in 1935 and now based in Steinhagen.
hrmann.money: Sales of garage and industrial doors, doors, frames and operators from over 40 plants: annual turnover of more than €1 billion.

hrt.name: Hrvatska radiotelevizija
hrt.what: Croatia's public broadcaster, founded by the Republic of Croatia and based in Zagreb; it dates its start to Radio Zagreb, first on air on 15 May 1926.
hrt.money: A monthly licence fee of €10.62 per household under Croatian law, over 85% of revenue in 2014, plus limited advertising.

hugoboss.name: HUGO BOSS AG
hugoboss.what: A German fashion company founded in 1924 by Hugo Ferdinand Boss in Metzingen, majority-owned since October 2026 by the British retailer Frasers Group.
hugoboss.money: Sales of BOSS and HUGO clothing, shoes and accessories: 4.27 billion euros in 2025.
hugoboss.arts: It has funded the HUGO BOSS PRIZE with the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation since 1996 and gave the HUGO BOSS ASIA ART Award from 2013.

humanitarianprojects.name: Fond gumanitarnykh proektov
humanitarianprojects.what: A Moscow foundation set up to expand the Russia, My History exhibitions; in 2019 its managing director was the former Gazprom lawyer Ivan Yesin.
humanitarianprojects.money: Mostly the state-controlled Gazprom, plus government grants, according to RFE/RL in 2019.

humanus.name: Humanus-Stiftung
humanus.what: A foundation registered in Basel on 3 June 1969 to serve a comprehensive science of the human being and help shape a social order fit for human life.
humanus.address: c/o Wirtschafts-Treuhand AG, Arnold Böcklin-Strasse 25, 4051 Basel

humtv.name: Hum Network Limited
humtv.what: A Pakistani media company in Karachi, founded by Sultana Siddiqui in February 2004 as Eye TV and listed since 2005; it runs Hum TV, Hum News and other channels.
humtv.money: Its television and media business: sales of PKR 6,831,724,000 in the financial year to June 2026.
humtv.address: Plot No. 10/11, Hassan Ali Street, off I.I. Chundrigar Road, Karachi

huntingtonbank.name: Huntington Bancshares Incorporated
huntingtonbank.what: An American bank holding company headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, which traces its roots to P. W. Huntington & Company, formed in 1866; its bank is The Huntington National Bank.
huntingtonbank.money: Banking through 1,372 offices, mainly in the Midwest and South: revenue of US$12.485 billion and net income of US$2.087 billion in 2025.

huttcitycouncil|New Zealand.name: Hutt City Council
huttcitycouncil|New Zealand.what: The territorial authority for Lower Hutt, New Zealand, formed in the 1989 local government reforms from four councils and chaired by Mayor Ken Laban since October 2025.
huttcitycouncil|New Zealand.money: Rates paid by Lower Hutt ratepayers; its draft 2025-26 annual plan proposed a 12.8% rates rise after growth.

hyundai.name: Hyundai Motor Company
hyundai.what: A South Korean carmaker established in 1967 and based in Seoul, which owns the Genesis brand and 33.88 per cent of Kia.
hyundai.money: Car sales: revenue of KRW 186.3 trillion and net profit of KRW 10.36 trillion in 2025.
hyundai.arts: Its Hyundai Artlab team runs long-term partnerships with Tate, LACMA, the Whitney Museum and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

hyundaidepartmentstore|South Korea.name: Hyundai Department Store Co., Ltd.
hyundaidepartmentstore|South Korea.what: A South Korean department store operator in the Hyundai Department Store Group, which spun off from Hyundai Group in 1999; it began as Keumgang Development Industries in 1971.
hyundaidepartmentstore|South Korea.money: Sales at its department stores, including the Apgujeong flagship in Seoul opened in 1985, and at the group's duty-free shops.

hyundaipresentedfirstshow.name: Hyundai Motor Company
hyundaipresentedfirstshow.what: A South Korean carmaker established in 1967 and based in Seoul, which owns the Genesis brand and 33.88 per cent of Kia.
hyundaipresentedfirstshow.money: Car sales: revenue of KRW 186.3 trillion and net profit of KRW 10.36 trillion in 2025.
hyundaipresentedfirstshow.arts: It has partnerships with MMCA, Tate, LACMA, the Whitney Museum and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale, and runs its own art programme, Hyundai Artlab.

idahocommissiononarts|USA.name: Idaho Commission on the Arts
idahocommissiononarts|USA.what: Idaho's state arts agency in Boise, created by legislation Governor Don Samuelson signed in 1967 as the Idaho Commission on the Arts and Humanities.
idahocommissiononarts|USA.money: Appropriations from the Idaho Legislature and grants from the National Endowment for the Arts.
idahocommissiononarts|USA.address: 2537 West State St., Suite 130, Boise, ID 83702

ikahocountryclub.name: 伊香保カントリークラブ (Ikaho Country Club)
ikahocountryclub.what: A members' golf club in Ikaho, Shibukawa, Gunma Prefecture, opened in 1959 as the first golf course in Gunma.
ikahocountryclub.money: Membership and green fees from golfers, plus its restaurant.

imls.name: Institute of Museum and Library Services
imls.what: An independent US federal agency established in 1996 by the Museum and Library Services Act; the main source of federal support for US libraries and museums.
imls.arts: In 2024 it awarded $266.7 million through grantmaking, research and policy work.

inarimunicipality|Finland.name: Inarin kunta
inarimunicipality|Finland.what: The municipality of Inari in Finnish Lapland, established in 1876, Finland's largest by area and a centre of Sámi culture, with its offices in Ivalo.
inarimunicipality|Finland.money: Local taxes and Finnish state transfers: its 2025 budget plan expected about €18 million in tax revenue and €12.1 million in state transfers.

inditex.name: Industria de Diseño Textil, S.A.
inditex.what: A Spanish clothing group created in 1985 as the holding company for Zara, the chain Amancio Ortega started; it is based in Arteixo, Galicia, and owns Massimo Dutti and Bershka.
inditex.money: Clothing sales through more than 7,200 stores and online: €39.86 billion in its 2025 financial year.

industriellenvereinigungsteiermark.name: Vereinigung der Österreichischen Industrie, Landesgruppe Steiermark
industriellenvereinigungsteiermark.what: The Styrian regional group of the Industriellenvereinigung, the voluntary and independent association that represents Austrian industry; it sits in Graz.
industriellenvereinigungsteiermark.money: Its member companies; the national Industriellenvereinigung is a voluntary association with more than 5,000 members.

institutfranais.name: Institut français
institutfranais.what: France's public agency for cultural diplomacy, a state industrial and commercial body set up in 2011 under the foreign and culture ministries; seated in Paris.
institutfranais.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Culture.
institutfranais.arts: It supports French artists and creative industries abroad and coordinates France's cultural network of more than 150 branches.

institutionofmigroskulturprozent.name: Migros-Genossenschafts-Bund
institutionofmigroskulturprozent.what: The Zurich federation of Switzerland's ten regional Migros cooperatives; Gottlieb Duttweiler founded Migros in 1925.
institutionofmigroskulturprozent.money: Retail and trade; the Migros group had sales of CHF 31.9 billion in 2025.
institutionofmigroskulturprozent.arts: The Migros-Kulturprozent spends CHF 121 million a year on culture, society, education, leisure and business, and has spent CHF 5.5 billion since 1957.

intach.name: Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage
intach.what: A non-profit membership society founded in New Delhi in 1984 to protect India's natural and cultural heritage; Rajiv Gandhi sat on its first governing council.
intach.money: Grants from funders it lists, including India's Ministry of Culture, the Archaeological Survey of India, the World Monuments Fund and the Helen Hamlyn Trust.
intach.arts: It has chapters in 215 Indian cities and restores monuments; it has held special consultative status with the UN Economic and Social Council since 2007.

internationalrenaissance.name: International Renaissance Foundation
internationalrenaissance.what: A Ukrainian charitable foundation founded on 8 April 1990 by George Soros with the Prosvita Society and others; it is part of the Open Society Foundations network.
internationalrenaissance.money: As a member of George Soros's Open Society Foundations network, it gave total funding of nearly UAH 900 million (US$21.6 million) in 2025.
internationalrenaissance.arts: In 1993 it founded the Soros Center for Contemporary Art at Kyiv-Mohyla Academy, and it set up the Publishers' Forum in Lviv.

interparking.name: Interparking SA
interparking.what: A Brussels car park operator founded in 1958 by Claude De Clercq, owned by AG Insurance (61%) and the Dutch pension fund APG (39%); it absorbed Saba in October 2025.
interparking.money: Parking fees from more than 2,000 car parks in 15 countries: revenue of €719.9 million in 2025.

interpipe.name: Interpipe
interpipe.what: A Ukrainian maker of seamless steel pipes and railway wheels, founded in 1990 by Victor Pinchuk, whose family is its ultimate owner; it is headquartered in Nikopol.
interpipe.money: Sales of steel pipes, railway wheels and steel: revenue of US$1.05 billion and net profit of US$280.48 million in 2024.

intuit.name: Intuit Inc.
intuit.what: An American financial software company founded in 1983 and headquartered in Mountain View, California; it makes TurboTax and QuickBooks and owns Credit Karma and Mailchimp.
intuit.money: Sales of its tax, accounting and marketing software and services: revenue of US$18.8 billion in its 2025 fiscal year.

ireneludwig.name: Peter und Irene Ludwig Stiftung
ireneludwig.what: A charitable foundation under German civil law, set up in Aachen in 1997 by Irene Ludwig from the foundation she and Peter Ludwig had founded in 1982.
ireneludwig.money: The art collection and fortune of Peter and Irene Ludwig; Peter Ludwig built up the chocolate maker Leonard Monheim, later Ludwig Schokolade.
ireneludwig.arts: It buys, manages and lends works for the Ludwig museums and supports exhibitions; a 2017 contract with the City of Cologne covers its work with Museum Ludwig.
ireneludwig.renamed: The Cologne, Beijing and Havana sentences describe gifts by Peter and Irene Ludwig themselves; the 1976 Museum Ludwig gift came before the foundation existed.

italysmondotv.name: Mondo TV S.p.A.
italysmondotv.what: An Italian animation producer and distributor headquartered in Rome and listed on the Milan stock exchange, founded in 1985 by Orlando Corradi.
italysmondotv.money: Producing, co-producing, distributing and licensing animated series.
italysmondotv.wrong_match: A client of SEK Studio, not a funder: it paid for animation work it subcontracted there (OFAC, June 2024).

itaunibanco.name: Banco Itaú Unibanco S.A.
itaunibanco.what: Brazil's largest bank, formed in 2008 by the merger of Banco Itaú and Unibanco, headquartered in São Paulo and controlled by the Itaúsa conglomerate.
itaunibanco.money: Banking and financial services across Latin America, Europe and Asia: revenue of US$33.2 billion and net income of US$8.8 billion in 2025.
itaunibanco.arts: It owns Itaú Cultural, a cultural institute on Avenida Paulista in São Paulo founded in 1987, which has run the Rumos grant programme since 1997.

jaapharten.name: Stichting Jaap Harten Fonds
jaapharten.what: A Dutch foundation set up on 27 December 1988 as the Harten Fonds by the poet and writer Jaap Harten, who died in 2017.
jaapharten.money: The assets Jaap Harten placed in it, and most of his estate, which passed to the fund after his death.
jaapharten.arts: It spends more than €1,000,000 a year on about 100 projects, mainly monographs and biographies on Dutch art, literature, architecture, music and theatre.

jacquelinesommer.name: Fondation François Sommer
jacquelinesommer.what: A French foundation created in 1964 by François and Jacqueline Sommer, industrialists from the Ardennes, working on nature protection, wildlife, art and hunting; Henri de Castries is president.
jacquelinesommer.money: The fortune of its founders; the foundation says it has been financially independent since its creation.
jacquelinesommer.arts: It awards the Prix littéraire François Sommer and the Prix du Patrimoine François Sommer, won in 2026 by the château de Raray.

jaegerlecoultre.name: Manufacture Jaeger-LeCoultre SA
jaegerlecoultre.what: A Swiss watchmaker founded by Antoine LeCoultre in 1833 in Le Sentier, Vallée de Joux, and fully owned by the Swiss luxury group Richemont since 2000.
jaegerlecoultre.money: Sales of its watches and clocks, earned for its parent, the Richemont group.

jameelfamily.name: Abdul Latif Jameel Company Ltd
jameelfamily.what: A family-owned diversified business founded in Jeddah in 1945 by Sheikh Abdul Latif Jameel, active in more than 30 countries.
jameelfamily.money: Its businesses in vehicle distribution, as a Toyota distributor in Saudi Arabia since 1955, and in finance, machinery, real estate, energy and consumer products.
jameelfamily.arts: Through Art Jameel, which the family founded in 2003 and funds privately, it supports the Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai, a free contemporary art institution.

jandenul.name: Jan De Nul Group
jandenul.what: A family-owned Belgian dredging and marine construction company founded in 1938 by Jan De Nul in Hofstade near Aalst, with a financial headquarters in Luxembourg.
jandenul.money: Offshore energy, dredging, construction and environmental remediation contracts worldwide; turnover was €4.24 billion in 2025.

janetbuxton.name: Michael and Janet Buxton Foundation
janetbuxton.what: The philanthropic foundation of the Melbourne art collectors Michael and Janet Buxton, through which they founded Buxton Contemporary at the University of Melbourne.
janetbuxton.money: The Buxtons' own wealth. Michael Buxton co-founded the Melbourne property developer MAB Corporation with Andrew Buxton in 1995.
janetbuxton.arts: In 2014 it gave the university their collection of contemporary Australian art and funds to build the gallery, which opened in 2018.
janetbuxton.renamed: The museum sentences mean Michael and Janet Buxton and their foundation, not MAB Corporation, the property company Michael Buxton co-founded.

japan.name: The Japan Foundation
japan.what: A Japanese public body for international cultural exchange, set up in 1972 by an Act of the Diet, an Independent Administrative Institution since 2003.
japan.money: The Japanese state, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which oversees it.

japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.name: Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.what: A special body of Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, set up in 1968 to promote arts and culture, with its main offices in Kyoto since 2023.
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.money: Japan's national budget through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology; its budget was 107 billion yen in 2026.
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.arts: Its divisions protect the nation's cultural properties and oversee the Japan Arts Council.

japantobacco.name: Japan Tobacco Inc.
japantobacco.what: A Japanese tobacco company set up in 1985 to take over the state tobacco monopoly and parent of Japan Tobacco International. By law the government owns at least one third.
japantobacco.money: Tobacco sales, which drove most of its growth: revenue of 3.47 trillion yen in 2025, up 13.4 percent.

jcdecaux.name: JCDecaux SE
jcdecaux.what: A French outdoor advertising company founded in Lyon in 1964 by Jean-Claude Decaux, majority-owned by the Decaux family and headquartered in Neuilly-sur-Seine.
jcdecaux.money: Advertising on street furniture, in transport and on billboards: revenue of €3.96 billion in 2025.

johnellerman.name: John Ellerman Foundation
johnellerman.what: A grantmaking charity set up in 1971 by Sir John Ellerman, 2nd Baronet, a shipowner who inherited his father's fortune, based in London.
johnellerman.money: An endowment from the Ellerman family fortune in shipping, brewing, coal mining and real estate; its investments stood at £154.9 million on 31 March 2026.
johnellerman.arts: The Charity Commission register lists arts, environment and welfare as the areas of its grants of over £4 million a year.
johnellerman.address: Aria House, 23 Craven Street, London WC2N 5NS

johnkeells.name: John Keells Foundation
johnkeells.what: The corporate social responsibility entity of Sri Lanka's John Keells Group, established in Colombo on 28 March 2005.
johnkeells.money: The John Keells Group, a listed Sri Lankan conglomerate in hotels, supermarkets, ports, food and finance with revenue of LKR 260.7 billion in 2023.
johnkeells.arts: Its arts projects include Kala Pola, the Gratiaen Trust, the Sunera Foundation and the Chitrasena Vajira Dance Foundation.

jordanbromine.name: Jordan Bromine Company
jordanbromine.what: A producer of bromine and bromine derivatives founded in 1999 as a joint venture of the Arab Potash Company and Albemarle, with its plant in Jordan's Safi Valley.
jordanbromine.money: Sales of bromine and derivatives such as the flame retardant TBBPA, made from Dead Sea resources and sold in more than 30 countries.

jordankuwaitbank.name: Jordan Kuwait Bank
jordankuwaitbank.what: A Jordanian public shareholding bank founded in 1976 and based in Amman, set up to bring capital into Jordan from other Arab countries, especially Kuwait.
jordankuwaitbank.money: Banking in Jordan and Cyprus and through subsidiaries such as Bank of Baghdad; KIPCO of Kuwait owns about 51% through Al Rawabi United Holding.

jordanpetroleumrefinery.name: Jordan Petroleum Refinery Company
jordanpetroleumrefinery.what: A Jordanian public shareholding company incorporated on 8 July 1956 that runs the country's only oil refinery, in Zarqa, and the Jopetrol fuel marketing branch.
jordanpetroleumrefinery.money: Refining, storing and selling petroleum products in Jordan; it had 40,159 shareholders and JD 100 million of paid capital at the end of 2025.

josephinehector.name: H.W. & J. Hector Stiftung zu Weinheim
josephinehector.what: A private foundation in Weinheim set up in 1995 by Josephine Hector and Hans-Werner Hector, a co-founder of SAP; the couple added Hector Stiftung II in 2008.
josephinehector.money: The fortune of Hans-Werner Hector, who sold most of his SAP shares in 1996.
josephinehector.arts: It funds the Hector Kunstpreis, awarded yearly by the Kunsthalle Mannheim, and supports the Sammlung Prinzhorn in Heidelberg.

joyobank.name: The Joyo Bank, Ltd.
joyobank.what: A regional bank headquartered in Mito, Ibaraki Prefecture, formed in 1935 from the Goju Bank and the Tokiwa Bank; since 2016 part of Mebuki Financial Group.
joyobank.money: Lending and deposits in Ibaraki Prefecture, where it holds a 38% share of deposits and 42% of loans, with branches across the Kantō region.

jpmorgan.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
jpmorgan.what: The largest US bank, formed in 2000 by the merger of J.P. Morgan & Co. and Chase Manhattan, headquartered at 270 Park Avenue, New York.
jpmorgan.money: Interest and fees from consumer, commercial and investment banking: net income was $57.0 billion in 2025.

jtbanka.name: J&T BANKA, a.s.
jtbanka.what: A Czech private and investment bank in Prague, formed in 1998 when J&T bought Podnikatelská banka; it belongs to J&T Finance Group, owned mainly by Jozef Tkáč and Ivan Jakabovič.
jtbanka.money: Private, investment, corporate and retail banking in Czechia, Slovakia, Croatia and Germany; it manages CZK 338 billion of client assets.

kaimanabeachhotel.name: Kaimana Beach Hotel
kaimanabeachhotel.what: A 125-room hotel on Sans Souci Beach in Waikīkī, opened in 1963 and run by Japan's New Otani until 2020, when it took its present name.
kaimanabeachhotel.money: Room, restaurant and event sales; the Honolulu private equity firm BlackSand Capital bought the land in 2016 and the hotel in 2018.

kaiserfriedrichmuseumsverein.name: Kaiser Friedrich Museumsverein
kaiserfriedrichmuseumsverein.what: A registered association founded in Berlin in 1897 to support the Gemäldegalerie and the sculpture collection in the Bode-Museum.
kaiserfriedrichmuseumsverein.money: Members' dues and tax-deductible donations; it has about 600 members.
kaiserfriedrichmuseumsverein.arts: It owns about 122 paintings and 164 sculptures, lent to the two collections, and helps pay for exhibitions such as the 2024 Frans Hals show.

kantensprung.name: Kantensprung Stiftung
kantensprung.what: A foundation entered in the Basel-Stadt commercial register, with its seat at Dornacherstrasse 192 in Basel.

kauflandromania.name: Kaufland Romania S.C.S.
kauflandromania.what: The Romanian arm of the German Kaufland hypermarket chain, part of the Schwarz Group, which opened its first Romanian store in Bucharest on 13 October 2005.
kauflandromania.money: Grocery sales in more than 195 stores: turnover was €4.2 billion from March 2025 to February 2026.

kawasakiheavyindustries.name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Ltd.
kawasakiheavyindustries.what: A Japanese heavy industry manufacturer founded in 1896 by Shōzō Kawasaki, with head offices in Kobe and Tokyo.
kawasakiheavyindustries.money: Sales of aircraft, defence equipment, rolling stock, ships, energy plants, robots and motorcycles; revenue was ¥1.500 trillion in the year to March 2022.

kbcbank.name: KBC Group NV
kbcbank.what: A Belgian bank and insurance group formed in 1998 by merging Kredietbank, CERA Bank and ABB Insurance, headquartered in Brussels.
kbcbank.money: Banking and insurance for about 13 million clients in Belgium, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Bulgaria; core shareholders include KBC Ancora, Cera and MRBB.

keptbyprivateuniversityfaap.name: Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado
keptbyprivateuniversityfaap.what: A private São Paulo foundation set up in 1947 to fulfil Count Armando Alvares Penteado and his wife Annie's plan for an art school; it runs a private university.
keptbyprivateuniversityfaap.money: Tuition from the faculties it maintains, with about 12,500 students on campuses in São Paulo, Ribeirão Preto and São José dos Campos.
keptbyprivateuniversityfaap.arts: It runs the Museu de Arte Brasileira and the Teatro FAAP; its exhibitions drew 312,104 visitors in 2025.

kfw.name: KfW Stiftung
kfw.what: A foundation in Frankfurt set up by KfW in 2012 to keep the bank's social commitment independent of its yearly earnings.
kfw.money: Money from its founder KfW, Germany's state-owned development bank.
kfw.arts: Art and culture is one of its three fields of action, with the Vila Sul residency, Untold Literatures and exhibitions at Villa 102.

khalidshoman.name: The Khalid Shoman Foundation
khalidshoman.what: A Jordanian foundation that has overseen Darat al Funun in Amman since 2002; the banker Khalid Shoman and his wife Suha opened the arts centre in 1993.
khalidshoman.arts: Darat al Funun shows the Khalid Shoman Collection, and in 2011 the foundation began a fellowship for the study of modern and contemporary Arab art.

kier.name: Kier Group plc
kier.what: A British construction, services and property group founded in 1928 in Stoke-on-Trent, listed in London, with its registered office in Salford.
kier.money: Building and infrastructure contracts, mostly for central government departments and local authorities; revenue was £4,393.0 million in the year to June 2026.
kier.address: 2nd Floor, Optimum House, Clippers Quay, Salford M50 3XP

kimbellart.name: Kimbell Art Foundation
kimbellart.what: A private foundation set up in Fort Worth in 1935 by Kay and Velma Kimbell; it owns and runs the Kimbell Art Museum, opened in 1972.
kimbellart.money: Kay Kimbell's fortune from flour mills, grocery chains and oil mills, left to it in 1964; total assets were $759.3 million in 2024.

kindermorgan.name: Kinder Morgan, Inc.
kindermorgan.what: An American energy infrastructure company founded in 1997 by Richard Kinder and William Morgan, headquartered in Houston and listed in New York.
kindermorgan.money: Moving and storing natural gas, oil and refined products through about 79,000 miles of pipelines and terminals; revenue was US$15.1 billion in 2024.

kingbaudouin.name: King Baudouin Foundation
kingbaudouin.what: Belgium's largest public utility foundation, set up in 1976 for the 25th anniversary of King Baudouin's accession, based in Brussels.
kingbaudouin.money: Returns on its €1.7 billion capital and support from the Belgian National Lottery; its 2026 budget is €273 million.
kingbaudouin.arts: Its heritage and culture division has about €5 million a year, including up to €1 million for art it buys and lends to museums.

kipco.name: Kuwait Projects Company (Holding) K.S.C.P.
kipco.what: A Kuwaiti holding company incorporated on 2 August 1975 and listed on Boursa Kuwait, majority owned by family offices of members of the ruling Al Sabah family.
kipco.money: Its companies in banking, petrochemicals and oil services, food, media, real estate, healthcare and education; total assets were US$45.2 billion at the end of 2025.
kipco.address: KIPCO Tower, Khalid Bin Al Waleed Street, Sharq, Kuwait City

knight.name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
knight.what: A private foundation set up in 1950 by the newspaper publishers John S. and James L. Knight, based in Miami.
knight.money: Knight Newspapers stock left by their mother Clara Knight in 1965 and by John S. Knight's estate; total assets were $2.53 billion in 2024.
knight.arts: It funds arts and culture, journalism and community development in the 26 cities where the Knight brothers published newspapers.

kolmont.name: Kolmont
kolmont.what: A Belgian property developer started as a family business in 2000, with offices in Hasselt and Brussels.
kolmont.money: Sales and lettings of the houses, apartments, building plots, shops and offices it develops.

kommuneqarfiksermersooq.name: Kommuneqarfik Sermersooq
kommuneqarfiksermersooq.what: The Greenland municipality with its seat in the capital Nuuk, formed on 1 January 2009 from five smaller municipalities; by area it is the largest municipality in the world.
kommuneqarfiksermersooq.money: Income tax: residents pay a 26% municipal rate and a 6% joint municipal tax, according to Greenland's Tax Agency.

koret.name: Koret Foundation
koret.what: A private foundation in San Francisco set up in 1979 by Joseph Koret, who built the Koret of California apparel brand with his late wife Stephanie.
koret.money: Returns on its endowment: dividends, interest and asset sales; total assets were $287.4 million at the end of 2025, per its Form 990-PF.
koret.arts: Arts and culture is one of its grant areas; it has given more than $1 billion in grants since 1980.

kpbs.name: KPBS Public Media
kpbs.what: San Diego's public radio and television broadcaster, a department of San Diego State University, founded on the campus in 1960 as KEBS.
kpbs.money: Member donations and underwriting; federal grants of about $4.3 million a year, 12% of its $38.5 million budget, ended in 2025.

kpmg.name: KPMG Argentina
kpmg.what: The Argentine member firm of KPMG, the London-based Big Four network of audit, tax and advisory firms, with its Buenos Aires office at Bouchard 710.
kpmg.money: Fees for audit, tax and advisory work paid by its clients.
kpmg.wrong_match: The Kunstmuseum Basel and Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen sentences mean KPMG's Swiss and German member firms, which are separate firms in the same network.

krber.name: Körber-Stiftung
krber.what: A private foundation set up in Hamburg in 1959 by the businessman Kurt A. Körber; it is the sole shareholder of Körber AG, the holding of the Körber Group.
krber.money: An annual dividend from Körber AG; the foundation's assets are about €580 million.
krber.arts: Culture is one of its seven subject areas.

kuka.name: KUKA SE & Co. KGaA
kuka.what: A German robotics and automation company founded in Augsburg in 1898 by Johann Josef Keller and Jakob Knappich, wholly owned by China's Midea group since 2022.
kuka.money: Sales of industrial robots, automated production systems, intralogistics and healthcare automation; revenue was €3.9 billion in 2025.

kulturstiftungdesbundes.name: Kulturstiftung des Bundes
kulturstiftungdesbundes.what: An independent foundation set up in 2002 with seat in Halle an der Saale that funds contemporary art and culture across Germany and abroad.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.money: German federal funds: an annual budget of 35 million euros.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.arts: Since 2002 it has run over 40 funding programmes and backed about 4,000 projects, with multi-year support for documenta and the Berliner Theatertreffen.

kunststiftungnrw.name: Kunststiftung NRW
kunststiftungnrw.what: A public-law foundation set up on 12 September 1989 by the North Rhine-Westphalia state government under Johannes Rau, based in the Haus der Stiftungen in Düsseldorf.
kunststiftungnrw.money: The proceeds of the lottery operator WestLotto.
kunststiftungnrw.arts: It has funded about 12,000 projects in literature, music, performing arts and visual art with a link to North Rhine-Westphalia since 1989.

kurabo.name: Kurabo Industries Ltd.
kurabo.what: A Japanese textile and chemicals group founded on 9 March 1888 as Kurashiki Spinning Works in Kurashiki, now headquartered in Osaka.
kurabo.money: Sales of textiles, chemical products, advanced technology equipment, food services and real estate.

kuraray.name: Kuraray Co., Ltd.
kuraray.what: A Japanese chemicals and fibre maker founded in Kurashiki in 1926 by Magosaburō Ōhara and Torajiro Kojima, with head offices in Tokyo and Osaka.
kuraray.money: Sales of chemicals, resins, synthetic fibres, high performance materials and dental materials; its main plants are in Kurashiki.

kuwaitpetroleum.name: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation
kuwaitpetroleum.what: Kuwait's state-owned oil company, founded on 27 January 1980 as the umbrella for KOC, KNPC, KOTC and PIC, headquartered in Kuwait City.
kuwaitpetroleum.money: Sales of Kuwait's crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals; revenue was KWD 30.06 billion in fiscal 2024/25.
kuwaitpetroleum.address: Oil Sector Complex, Shuwaikh Industrial 1, Block 1, Street 74, Kuwait

kyocera.name: Kyocera Corporation
kyocera.what: A Japanese ceramics and electronics manufacturer founded in Kyoto in 1959 by Kazuo Inamori as Kyoto Ceramic Company, renamed in 1982.
kyocera.money: Sales of industrial ceramics, semiconductor packages, electronic components, solar power systems and office printers; revenue was ¥1.58 trillion in 2018.
kyocera.arts: It runs the Kyocera Museum of Fine Ceramics and the Kyocera Gallery.

lacity|USA.name: City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs
lacity|USA.what: A department of the City of Los Angeles that makes grants to arts and cultural organisations and artists and manages the city's cultural programmes.
lacity|USA.money: By city code, an amount equal to 1% of expected hotel Transient Occupancy Tax revenue, plus Arts Development Fees paid on non-residential building projects.
lacity|USA.address: 201 North Figueroa Street, Suite 1400, Los Angeles, CA 90012

lambent.name: Lambent Foundation
lambent.what: A New York grantmaker for art, culture and social justice founded by the artist Anne Delaney, grown out of her Starry Night Fund of 2002.
lambent.money: Anne Delaney's philanthropy, held as a fiscally sponsored project of the Tides Center, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
lambent.arts: It funds contemporary art and culture tied to social justice in New York City, New Orleans and Nairobi.
lambent.address: 55 Exchange Place, Suite 406, New York, NY 10005

landberlin|Germany.name: Land Berlin
landberlin|Germany.what: The state government of Berlin: the Senate, led by the Governing Mayor (Der Regierende Bürgermeister) through the Senatskanzlei.
landberlin|Germany.money: The Berlin state budget passed by the Abgeordnetenhaus, about EUR 45.5 billion for 2026 and EUR 46.5 billion for 2027.
landberlin|Germany.arts: Its Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion has EUR 957.3 million in non-staff funds for 2026, down from EUR 1.026 billion in 2025.

landcareaustralia.name: Landcare Australia
landcareaustralia.what: An independent national not-for-profit for environmental conservation and sustainable land management, set up in 1989, when landcare became a national movement championed by Prime Minister Bob Hawke.
landcareaustralia.money: Grants from government partners, sponsorship from corporate partners and public donations.

landobersterreich|Austria.name: Land Oberösterreich
landobersterreich|Austria.what: The government of Upper Austria, one of Austria's nine states, run from the Amt der Oö. Landesregierung in Linz.
landobersterreich|Austria.money: The Upper Austrian state budget, about EUR 9.9 billion for 2026, planned with a deficit of about EUR 255 million.

landvorarlberg|Austria.name: Amt der Vorarlberger Landesregierung
landvorarlberg|Austria.what: The administration of the government of the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, population 401,674, led by Landeshauptmann Markus Wallner (ÖVP) and seated in the Landhaus in Bregenz.
landvorarlberg|Austria.money: The state budget of Vorarlberg, which plans €2.8 billion in spending for 2026, including about €200 million in new borrowing.

langlois.name: Daniel Langlois Foundation for Art, Science, and Technology
langlois.what: A private charitable foundation set up in Montreal in 1997 by Daniel Langlois (1957 to 2023), the founder of the 3D animation software company Softimage.
langlois.money: Daniel Langlois's fortune from Softimage, the company he founded in 1986, which Microsoft bought for 130 million dollars in 1994.
langlois.arts: It supports artistic, scientific and technological research and keeps a documentation collection on electronic and media arts from the 1960s onward.

latam.name: LATAM Airlines Group S.A.
latam.what: A Chilean airline holding company formed in 2012 when LAN Airlines took over Brazil's TAM Linhas Aéreas, headquartered in Santiago and listed in Santiago and New York.
latam.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with US$13.034 billion revenue in 2024; Sixth Street Partners, Delta Air Lines and Qatar Airways are its largest shareholders.

latrobeuniversity.name: La Trobe University
latrobeuniversity.what: A public research university in Victoria, Australia, established on 9 December 1964, with its main campus in Bundoora, Melbourne, and regional campuses.
latrobeuniversity.money: Government funding and student fees; its budget was A$863.7 million in 2023.

latvianministryofculture|Latvia.name: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Latvia
latvianministryofculture|Latvia.what: The Latvian state institution that organises and coordinates culture, social integration and media policy, based in Riga.

lazardfreresgestion.name: Fondation Lazard Frères Gestion-Institut de France
lazardfreresgestion.what: A foundation created in 2020 with the Institut de France by Lazard Frères Gestion, which is owned 99.99% by Compagnie Financière Lazard Frères.
lazardfreresgestion.money: Lazard Frères Gestion's asset management business in Paris; the firm has sponsored heritage projects since 2007.
lazardfreresgestion.arts: It paid for restoring Pierre Dulin's painting of the Hôtel Royal des Invalides, finished in March 2021, and supports four Institut National du Patrimoine students each year.

lazraqfamily.name: Alliances Développement Immobilier
lazraqfamily.what: A Moroccan property developer listed in Casablanca, founded by Alami Lazraq, who chairs it and controls 51.7 percent of its shares.
lazraqfamily.money: Sales of residential, commercial and tourism property developments across North Africa.
lazraqfamily.arts: Its cultural patronage covers the Fondation MACAAL, built on the art collection of Alami and Farida Lazraq, and a sculpture park.

lecorbusier.name: Fondation Le Corbusier
lecorbusier.what: A French foundation recognised as of public utility by decree on 24 July 1968, universal legatee of the architect Le Corbusier; its seat is the Maison Jeanneret, Paris.
lecorbusier.money: Le Corbusier left it everything he owned, including his archives and the moral and economic rights to all his works, which ADAGP manages.

leedscitycouncil|UK.name: Leeds City Council
leedscitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the City of Leeds in West Yorkshire, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Leeds Civic Hall.
leedscitycouncil|UK.money: Council tax and UK government funding; for 2026/27 its government resources rose by £71.1m and council tax by 4.99 per cent.
leedscitycouncil|UK.address: Civic Hall, Calverley Street, Leeds LS1 1UR

leica.name: Leica Camera AG
leica.what: A German maker of cameras, lenses and optics in Wetzlar, with roots in Carl Kellner's Optical Institute of 1849; Andreas Kaufmann's ACM holds 55% and Blackstone 45%.
