leica.money: Sales of cameras, lenses and other optical products; turnover was €596 million in 2024/25.
leica.arts: It runs about 30 Leica galleries and gives the Leica Oskar Barnack Award and the Leica Hall of Fame Award to photographers.

lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.name: Les Amis des Musées d'art et d'histoire du Luxembourg a.s.b.l.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.what: A Luxembourg non-profit association of friends of six museums, under the patronage of the Grand Duchess, tracing its history to the Société des Amis des Musées founded in 1926.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.money: Members' subscriptions and donations; gifts and bequests can also go to its public-utility foundation, the Fondation des Amis des Musées.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.arts: It helps the museums acquire works, among them Jacques Monory's La terrasse no. 5 for the Musée national.

leventis.name: A. G. Leventis Foundation
leventis.what: A private foundation set up in May 1979 under provisions made by Anastasios G. Leventis, a Greek Cypriot trader in West Africa, with its executive office in Zurich.
leventis.money: The fortune Anastasios G. Leventis made with A. G. Leventis & Company, his West African trading group founded in 1936.
leventis.arts: Its own initiatives are the A. G. Leventis Gallery and the Leventis Municipal Museum, and it gives grants for heritage conservation, museums and libraries.

leverhulme.name: The Leverhulme Trust
leverhulme.what: A UK grant-making charity in London, established in 1925 under the will of the 1st Viscount Leverhulme to fund scholarships for research and education.
leverhulme.money: Its shareholding in Unilever plc, which began as shares in Lever Brothers; it gives out over £100 million a year.

lexus.name: Lexus
lexus.what: The luxury car division of the Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corporation, launched in 1989 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi.
lexus.money: Sales of Lexus cars within Toyota Motor Corporation, whose revenue was ¥48.04 trillion in 2025.

libbeys.name: Edward Drummond Libbey and Florence Scott Libbey
libbeys.what: Edward Drummond Libbey, owner of the Libbey Glass Company in Toledo, founded the Toledo Museum of Art in 1901 and led it until 1925; Florence Scott Libbey was his wife.
libbeys.money: Edward Libbey's fortune from Libbey Glass, the Owens Bottle Machine Company and Libbey-Owens Sheet Glass, given to the museum as the Libbey Endowment.
libbeys.arts: The Toledo Museum of Art still buys art from the Libbey Endowment, for example a Sasanian silver plate in 2022.
libbeys.renamed: The atlas name points at Libbey Glass, the company; the museum sentence means the funds the Libbeys themselves left to the museum.

lilly.name: Lilly Endowment Inc.
lilly.what: A private foundation in Indianapolis, created in 1937 by J.K. Lilly Sr. and his sons Eli and J.K. Jr. through gifts of Eli Lilly and Company stock.
lilly.money: Its endowment, mostly Eli Lilly and Company stock; total assets were US$106 billion in 2025.

linbury.name: The Linbury Trust
linbury.what: A UK grant-making trust, one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, set up by Lord Sainsbury of Preston Candover and the ballerina Anya Linden, first granting in 1973.
linbury.money: Investment income and donations; it held funds of £135.0 million at 5 April 2025.
linbury.arts: In the year to April 2025 it paid £3.7 million to culture, including £2.25 million to the National Gallery's Sainsbury Wing.
linbury.address: The Peak, 5 Wilton Road, London SW1V 1AP

lincolnfinancial.name: Lincoln National Corporation
lincolnfinancial.what: A US insurance and asset management company trading as Lincoln Financial Group, organised in Indiana in 1968 with roots in 1905, headquartered in Radnor, Pennsylvania.
lincolnfinancial.money: Premiums and fees from insurance and asset management, including group life, disability and dental cover; revenue was US$19.230 billion in 2021.

littlesun.name: Little Sun
littlesun.what: A Berlin nonprofit founded in 2012 by the artist Olafur Eliasson and the engineer Frederik Ottesen to bring solar energy to off-grid communities in Africa.
littlesun.money: Donations, funder grants and sales of its solar products; Bloomberg Philanthropies made a US$5 million impact investment in 2014.

liuna.name: Laborers' International Union of North America
liuna.what: A trade union of construction and energy workers in the United States and Canada, founded in 1903 and headquartered in Washington, DC, with about half a million members.
liuna.money: Its 2024 US tax return reports US$111.0 million in revenue, 89.7% of it program service revenue and 6.4% investment income.

liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.name: Liverpool City Council
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Liverpool, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, under Labour control since 2010, with main offices in the Cunard Building.
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.money: Business rates (£295.1m), council tax (£277.0m) and general government grants (£245.5m) in its 2026-27 budget, £1.8bn gross.

llbean.name: L.L.Bean, Inc.
llbean.what: A privately held American retailer of clothing and outdoor equipment, founded in 1912 by Leon Leonwood Bean in Freeport, Maine, where it is still headquartered.
llbean.money: Sales of clothing, footwear and outdoor recreation equipment; revenue was US$1.7 billion in 2023.

lombardodier.name: Bank Lombard Odier & Co Ltd
lombardodier.what: A Geneva private bank founded on 11 January 1796, organised as a partnership limited by shares under six managing partners, with headquarters at 1Roof in Bellevue, Geneva.
lombardodier.money: Fees from wealth management, asset management and banking IT services; assets under management were CHF 349 billion in 2023.

lonablottery|Burkina Faso.name: Loterie Nationale Burkinabè
lonablottery|Burkina Faso.what: Burkina Faso's national lottery, created on 10 May 1967 by ordinance and a state-owned company (société d'État) since November 1994, based in Ouagadougou.
lonablottery|Burkina Faso.money: Sales of lottery tickets, PMU'B horse-race bets and other games; turnover grew from 30 million FCFA in 1967 to 110 billion FCFA in 2016.

lookgalapresentedbymawer.name: Mawer Investment Management Ltd.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.what: An independent, privately owned investment firm founded in Calgary in 1974 by Charles Mawer as Mawer & Associates.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.money: Fees for managing about C$64.0 billion for individual and institutional investors.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.arts: It pledges at least 1% of pre-tax profits to community causes, which include the arts, and reports more than C$2.5 million donated.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.address: 517 10th Avenue SW, Suite 600, Calgary, Alberta T2R 0A8

loterieromande.name: Société de la loterie de la Suisse romande
loterieromande.what: A public-benefit lottery and sports betting company created in 1937 under an agreement between the governments of the French-speaking Swiss cantons, based in Lausanne; Jura joined in 1979.
loterieromande.money: Lottery and sports betting: gross gaming revenue was CHF 429.8 million in 2025, and its whole profit, CHF 252 million, went to associations.
loterieromande.arts: Its profit goes to associations in culture, social welfare, health, research, education, the environment, tourism, heritage and sport.

lotterywest.name: Lotterywest (Lotteries Commission of Western Australia)
lotterywest.what: Western Australia's state lottery operator, set up in 1932 as the Lotteries Commission of Western Australia and headquartered in Subiaco, Perth.
lotterywest.money: Profits from its lottery games, shared under the Lotteries Commission Act 1990 among health, sport, the arts and direct community grants.
lotterywest.arts: The Act sends 5% of profits to the Arts Lottery Account (as of 2013), and Lotterywest is a major supporter of the Perth Festival.

louisroederer.name: Louis Roederer
louisroederer.what: A champagne house in Reims, founded in 1776 as Dubois Père & Fils, renamed by Louis Roederer in 1833 and still owned by his descendants, the Rouzaud family.
louisroederer.money: Sales of its champagnes, including Cristal, with over 3.5 million bottles shipped a year, and of wines from estates such as Château de Pez.
louisroederer.arts: Its Fondation Louis Roederer gives the Discovery Award at the Rencontres d'Arles photography festival.

louisvuitton.name: Louis Vuitton Malletier SAS
louisvuitton.what: A Paris fashion house founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton, now a subsidiary of the luxury group LVMH.
louisvuitton.money: Sales of leather goods, shoes, watches, jewellery and other luxury products; revenue was €14 billion in 2020.
louisvuitton.arts: In 2006 it opened the Espace Louis Vuitton, an exhibition space on the seventh floor of its Champs-Élysées store in Paris.

loukil.name: Loukil Holding
loukil.what: A Tunisian family business group founded in 1976 by Mohamed Loukil, who died in 2023, and chaired by his son Bassem Loukil; it works through about 30 companies.
loukil.money: Its companies in agriculture, heavy industry and consulting, and its role as Tunisian representative of Mazda, Kubota, Panasonic, Mitsubishi and Samsung.

lucefdn.name: The Henry Luce Foundation
lucefdn.what: A private foundation formed in New York in 1936 by Henry R. Luce, co-founder of Time magazine and founder of Fortune and Life.
lucefdn.money: An endowment built from Henry R. Luce's stock in his publishing company, Time Inc., and his estate; total assets were US$1.09 billion in 2023.
lucefdn.arts: Its American Art Program, begun in 1980 with a US$4 million allocation as the Luce Fund for Scholarship in American Art, funds museum exhibitions and collection projects.

ludwig.name: Peter und Irene Ludwig Stiftung
ludwig.what: A foundation in Aachen set up in 1997 by Irene Ludwig, a year after the death of her husband Peter Ludwig, to place their collection in public museums.
ludwig.money: The fortune of Irene and Peter Ludwig, who ran the Monheim chocolate company until its sale in 1986, then Ludwig Schokolade until 1998.

luma.name: LUMA Foundation
luma.what: A Zurich non-profit set up in 2004 by Maja Hoffmann to support contemporary artists; it created the LUMA Arles arts campus, launched in 2013.
luma.money: Its founder Maja Hoffmann belongs to the shareholder pool of Roche founder descendants, which controls Roche Holding.

maddocks.name: Maddocks
maddocks.what: An Australian law firm that began in Melbourne in 1885 as Maddock & Johnson, founded by Joe Maddocks and Arthur Johnson, with offices in Melbourne, Sydney and Canberra.
maddocks.money: Fees for legal work, from local government clients to construction, employment and commercial law; it has over 95 partners and 700 staff.
maddocks.address: Collins Square, Tower Two, Level 25, 727 Collins Street, Melbourne VIC 3008

madepossiblebylaurenz.name: Laurenz-Stiftung
madepossiblebylaurenz.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
madepossiblebylaurenz.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
madepossiblebylaurenz.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

mainzerstadtwerke.name: Mainzer Stadtwerke AG
mainzerstadtwerke.what: The municipal utility company of the City of Mainz, supplying electricity, gas, water and public transport, with stakes in about 50 companies.
mainzerstadtwerke.money: Sales of electricity, gas, water and public transport in Mainz and nearby towns; revenue was €508 million in 2019.
mainzerstadtwerke.arts: It set up and supports the Stiftung Kunsthalle Mainz and a Mainz foundation for climate protection and energy efficiency.

malberln.name: Publikum.sk
malberln.what: An independent cultural centre in Trnava, Slovakia, opened in March 2018 and run by the civic association Publikum.sk, founded in 2009.
malberln.money: Public and EU project grants, among them the EU-financed Zmina.Rebuilding programme for Ukrainian culture, plus rentals of its spaces.

manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.name: Manchester City Council
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Manchester in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Manchester Town Hall on Albert Square.
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.money: Its revenue budget, which passed £1 billion for the first time in 2026/27 as national government funding improved.
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.address: Town Hall, Albert Square, Manchester M60 2LA

mandel.name: Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel Foundation
mandel.what: A private family foundation in Cleveland, Ohio; the brothers Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel set up their first charitable foundation in 1953.
mandel.money: The fortune the Mandel brothers made in Premier Industrial Corporation, which merged with Farnell Electronics in 1996 in a $3 billion deal.
mandel.arts: In 2026 it committed US$125 million to Case Western Reserve University, including a Mandel Humanities Building; its Boston institute runs a Cultural Leadership Program.

manitobaartscouncil|Canada.name: Manitoba Arts Council
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Province of Manitoba, established in 1965, that makes awards to professional artists and arts organisations through peer assessment.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.money: The Manitoba provincial budget, through the department of Sport, Culture, Heritage and Tourism.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.arts: Its budget was C$12.7 million in 2023.

manitobaliquor.name: Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries Corporation
manitobaliquor.what: A Crown corporation of the Province of Manitoba, established on 1 April 2014 under the Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries Corporation Act, based in Winnipeg.
manitobaliquor.money: Sales of liquor and gambling products, including casinos, VLTs and lottery tickets; it delivered C$724.1 million in profit to the Province of Manitoba in 2025-26.
manitobaliquor.arts: Its sponsorship and donation programmes totalled C$4.0 million in 2025-26.
manitobaliquor.address: Unit A, 1555 Buffalo Place, Winnipeg, Manitoba

mare.name: Fundația MARe
mare.what: A Bucharest foundation set up in February 2015 to run MARe, the Museum of Recent Art, Romania's first private museum of local art from the last five decades.
mare.money: The private money of its founder Roger Akoury, a Lebanese-born pharmaceutical entrepreneur, who funded the building and assembled its collection of around 550 works.

maritimeelectric.name: Maritime Electric
maritimeelectric.what: An electric utility serving Prince Edward Island, founded in 1918, headquartered in Charlottetown and owned by Fortis Inc.
maritimeelectric.money: Electricity sales to about 92,000 customers, at rates regulated by the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission.

marriott.name: Marriott International, Inc.
marriott.what: A US hotel company headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, formed in 1993 as successor to the hospitality arm of the Marriott Corporation founded by J. Willard and Alice Marriott.
marriott.money: Operating, franchising and licensing hotel, residential and timeshare brands; revenue was US$26.2 billion in 2025.

massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.name: Mass Cultural Council
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.what: The public arts funding body of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, based in Boston, which makes grants to cultural organizations, schools, communities and individual artists.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.money: An annual appropriation from the Massachusetts Legislature, plus funds from the National Endowment for the Arts.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.address: 10 St. James Avenue, 3rd Floor, Boston, MA 02116-3803

mazda.name: Mazda Motor Corporation
mazda.what: A Japanese carmaker founded on 30 January 1920 as Toyo Cork Kogyo by Jujiro Matsuda, headquartered in Fuchu, Hiroshima Prefecture.
mazda.money: Sales of cars and commercial vehicles: net sales of 4,918.2 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

mbhbank.name: MBH Bank Nyrt.
mbhbank.what: A Hungarian bank formed on 1 May 2023 by merging MKB Bank, Takarékbank and Budapest Bank; Lőrinc Mészáros holds almost half the shares and the state-owned Corvinus 15%.
mbhbank.money: Interest and fees from banking in Hungary; net income was HUF 165.109 billion in 2025.

mcommemutuelle.name: M comme Mutuelle
mcommemutuelle.what: A French mutual health insurer founded in 1870 and built up through mergers of local mutuals, headquartered in Lille with agencies across northern France and Normandy.
mcommemutuelle.money: Contributions from individual members and employer clients for its health and provident (prévoyance) insurance.

merciervanlanschot.name: Mercier Van Lanschot
merciervanlanschot.what: The Belgian branch of the Dutch private bank Van Lanschot Kempen NV, trading under this name since January 2024 after Van Lanschot Belgium and Mercier Vanderlinden combined.
merciervanlanschot.money: Wealth management for clients with €10.5 billion of assets under management (third quarter 2023), run for its parent Van Lanschot Kempen.

merribekcouncil|Australia.name: Merri-bek City Council
merribekcouncil|Australia.what: The local council for the City of Merri-bek in Melbourne's inner north, created as the City of Moreland in 1994 and renamed in September 2022, with its seat in Coburg.
merribekcouncil|Australia.money: Property rates, capped by the Victorian government; rates were set to raise A$202,778,329 for 2025-26.

methanexalso.name: Methanex Corporation
methanexalso.what: A methanol producer headquartered in Vancouver, incorporated in 1992 when it split off from Ocelot, with plants in Canada, Chile, Egypt, New Zealand, Trinidad and Tobago and the US.
methanexalso.money: Sales of methanol, plus ammonia and other products; revenue was US$3.6 billion in 2025.

metrobank.name: Metropolitan Bank & Trust Company
metrobank.what: A Philippine universal bank founded in Binondo, Manila, in 1962, with George Ty as founder, now headquartered at Metrobank Center in Taguig.
metrobank.money: Its banking business; GT Capital Holdings owns 39.8% and the Ty family and related parties 12.3%, with 47.8% public (June 2026).

miamidesigndistrict.name: Miami Design District Associates
miamidesigndistrict.what: A partnership of Craig Robins's company Dacra and L Catterton Real Estate, a fund set up in 2016 by Catterton, LVMH and Groupe Arnault, that develops Miami's Design District.
miamidesigndistrict.money: The district's retail property, anchored by more than 200 luxury brands including Hermès, Dior and Cartier.
miamidesigndistrict.arts: The district holds a public art collection, including Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome and Zaha Hadid's Elastika.

michaelaudain.name: Michael Audain
michaelaudain.what: A Canadian home builder and art collector, born in 1937, chairman since 1992 and a major shareholder of Polygon Homes Ltd. in Vancouver.
michaelaudain.money: His stake in Polygon Homes; he gives mainly through the Audain Foundation, which he set up in 1997 with Yoshiko Karasawa.
michaelaudain.arts: The Audain Foundation funds the annual C$100,000 Audain Prize for the Visual Arts and gave C$2 million to Arts Umbrella in 2023.
michaelaudain.renamed: The atlas name points at the company Polygon Homes, but both museum sentences name Michael Audain as a person.

middlesbroughcouncil|UK.name: Middlesbrough Council
middlesbroughcouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the Borough of Middlesbrough in England, a unitary authority since 1996, led by a directly elected mayor.
middlesbroughcouncil|UK.money: Council tax plus a £130.96 million government funding allocation for 2026/27 covering grants and retained business rates.

ministerofheritage.name: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism
ministerofheritage.what: Oman's government ministry for heritage, antiquities, museums and tourism; Royal Decree 91/2020 of 18 August 2020 gave the Ministry of Heritage and Culture this name.
ministerofheritage.money: The state budget of the Sultanate of Oman.
ministerofheritage.address: Al Khuwair, Madinat Al-Sultan Qaboos, P.O. Box 200, P.C. 115, Muscat

ministredelaculture|France.name: Ministère de la Culture
ministredelaculture|France.what: France's culture ministry, created in 1959 by President Charles de Gaulle for André Malraux, with offices on the rue de Valois in Paris and regional offices (DRAC).
ministredelaculture|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

ministryofculture|bergen-kunsthall-norwa.name: Kultur- og likestillingsdepartementet
ministryofculture|bergen-kunsthall-norwa.short: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
ministryofculture|bergen-kunsthall-norwa.what: Norway's government ministry for culture, media, sport and equality, set up in 1982 and renamed Ministry of Culture and Equality on 1 January 2022.

ministryofculture|mus-e-mohammed-vi-d-ar.what: Morocco's government department for youth, culture and sport, based in Rabat and headed by Minister Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid.

ministryofculture|sofia-city-art-gallery.name: Министерство на културата
ministryofculture|sofia-city-art-gallery.what: Bulgaria's government ministry for culture and heritage, first set up as a separate ministry on 6 February 1954 and based in Sofia.

ministryofculture|tainan-art-museum.name: Ministry of Culture
ministryofculture|tainan-art-museum.what: Taiwan's central government ministry for culture, set up on 20 May 2012 from the Council for Cultural Affairs (1981) and based in New Taipei; Li Yuan is minister.

ministryofocw|Netherlands.name: Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap
ministryofocw|Netherlands.short: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW)
ministryofocw|Netherlands.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science, created in 1918 and based in The Hague.
ministryofocw|Netherlands.money: The Dutch state budget, with €618 million a year in 2025-2028 for culture paid through the national cultural infrastructure and six national culture funds.

mitsuifudosan.name: Mitsui Fudosan Co., Ltd.
mitsuifudosan.what: A Japanese real estate developer founded on 15 July 1941 and headquartered in Nihonbashi-Muromachi, Tokyo, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
mitsuifudosan.money: Leasing, property sales and facility operations; revenue from operations was ¥1,215.4 billion in the first half of fiscal 2026.

mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.name: Mittelbrandenburgische Sparkasse in Potsdam
mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.what: A public-law savings bank in Potsdam, opened on 1 July 1991 and owned by an association of five Brandenburg districts and the cities of Brandenburg an der Havel and Potsdam.
mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.money: Its savings bank business; in 2025 it held €14.273 billion of customer deposits and €17.304 billion in total assets.

mizrahitefahotbank.name: Bank Mizrahi-Tefahot Ltd
mizrahitefahotbank.what: Israel's third largest bank by assets, founded in 1923 by the Mizrachi movement, headquartered in Ramat Gan, with the Ofer and Wertheim groups holding about 41.41%.
mizrahitefahotbank.money: Banking in Israel, where it is the largest mortgage lender, with net profit of NIS 5.6 billion in 2025.

mllerfonden.name: A.P. Møller og Hustru Chastine Mc-Kinney Møllers Fond til almene Formaal
mllerfonden.what: A commercial foundation set up in Copenhagen in 1953 by the shipowner Arnold Peter Møller, split from a family foundation he had created in 1946.
mllerfonden.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.
mllerfonden.arts: Its purposes include Danish culture and the upkeep of buildings of cultural and historical value; it paid to restore Kastellet in Copenhagen in 1989 and 1999.

mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.name: A.P. Møller og Hustru Chastine Mc-Kinney Møllers Fond til almene Formaal
