mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.arts: Its purposes include Danish culture and the upkeep of buildings of cultural and historical value; it paid to restore Kastellet in Copenhagen in 1989 and 1999.

mondriaan.name: Mondriaan Fonds
mondriaan.what: The Dutch public fund for visual art and cultural heritage, formed in Amsterdam in 2012 by merging the Mondriaan Stichting (set up 1994) with Fonds BKVB.
mondriaan.money: The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.
mondriaan.arts: In 2024 it approved 2,257 of 4,204 applications, awarding 53,438,678 euros in total.

morrison.name: Allies and Morrison LLP
morrison.what: A London architecture and urban planning practice founded in 1984 by Bob Allies and Graham Morrison, with studios in Cambridge, Manchester, Dublin, Jeddah and Toronto.
morrison.money: Fees from architecture, urban planning and consultancy commissions, much of it repeat work for long-term clients.

mountallisonuniversity.name: Mount Allison University
mountallisonuniversity.what: A public undergraduate liberal arts university in Sackville, New Brunswick, founded in 1839 on an offer by the Sackville merchant Charles Allison.
mountallisonuniversity.money: Student fees (C$46.6 million) and government and other grants (C$31.4 million) out of C$112.4 million revenue in 2025-26.

mozabanco.name: Moza Banco
mozabanco.what: A Mozambican commercial bank that opened in Maputo in June 2008 and was placed under central bank administration in 2016.
mozabanco.money: Its banking business; Kuhanha, the Banco de Moçambique staff pension fund manager, owns 66% and Arise B.V. 30.7%.

mtropoleeuropennedelille.name: Métropole Européenne de Lille
mtropoleeuropennedelille.what: The intercommunal authority of 95 communes around Lille, Roubaix and Tourcoing, created in 1967 as an urban community and a métropole since 1 January 2015.
mtropoleeuropennedelille.money: Business taxes it levies directly, household waste tax and French state grants; its 2025 budget was €2.446 billion.

mufgbank.name: MUFG Bank, Ltd.
mufgbank.what: A Japanese commercial bank established on 15 August 1919, owned by Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and headquartered in Marunouchi, Tokyo.
mufgbank.money: Banking through 412 branches in Japan and 101 abroad, with 31,691 employees, as of 31 March 2026.

municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.name: Gemeente Den Haag
municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.what: The municipality of The Hague, seat of the Dutch government and capital of South Holland, run by an elected council and a college of mayor and aldermen.
municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.arts: Its Meerjarenbeleidsplan Kunst en Cultuur for 2025 to 2028 has a total budget of €71.7 million; the college of mayor and aldermen adopted it in September 2024.

municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.name: Gmina Miejska Kraków
municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.what: The municipal government of Kraków, a city with county rights, run by an elected 43-member City Council and the city president.
municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.money: The Kraków city budget, which pays for the city's own tasks and those delegated by the national government.
municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.renamed: The museum sentence calls MOCAK a municipal museum of the City of Kraków; its organiser is Gmina Miejska Kraków, not the Muzeum Krakowa.

mvm.name: MVM Magyar Villamos Művek Zrt.
mvm.what: Hungary's largest state-owned energy company, wholly owned by the Hungarian state, which owns the Paks nuclear power plant, its main source of electricity.
mvm.money: Energy sales, chiefly electricity, much of it from Paks; group revenue was HUF 4,534 billion in 2024, with profit of HUF 324 billion.

nacsingapore.name: National Arts Council
nacsingapore.what: Singapore's statutory board for the arts, set up on 15 October 1991 under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; based at Goodman Arts Centre.
nacsingapore.money: Singapore government funding through the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; it receives about a third of state arts and culture funding (MCCY, 2021).
nacsingapore.arts: It gives grants, scholarships, awards and platforms to arts practitioners and runs arts education programmes.
nacsingapore.address: 90 Goodman Road, Goodman Arts Centre, Singapore

nationalartscouncil|Singapore.name: National Arts Council
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.what: Singapore's statutory board for the arts, set up on 15 October 1991 under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; based at Goodman Arts Centre.
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.money: Singapore government funding through the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; it receives about a third of state arts and culture funding (MCCY, 2021).
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.arts: It gives grants, scholarships, awards and platforms to arts practitioners and runs arts education programmes.
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.address: 90 Goodman Road, Goodman Arts Centre, Singapore

nationalbank.name: National Bank of Canada
nationalbank.what: A Canadian bank formed in 1979 by the merger of Banque Canadienne Nationale and the Provincial Bank of Canada, with roots in an 1859 Quebec City bank; based in Montreal.
nationalbank.money: Banking profits from personal and commercial banking, wealth management and financial markets: revenue CA$13.98 billion and net income CA$4.02 billion in 2025.

nationalendowmentforarts.name: National Endowment for the Arts
nationalendowmentforarts.what: An independent agency of the US federal government, created by Congress in 1965 and signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson; based in Washington, D.C.
nationalendowmentforarts.money: Annual appropriations from the US Congress: $207,000,000 a year for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.

nationalgeographicsociety.name: National Geographic Society
nationalgeographicsociety.what: A US nonprofit scientific and educational organisation founded on 13 January 1888 and based in Washington, D.C.; it owns 27% of National Geographic Partners, a joint venture with Disney.
nationalgeographicsociety.money: Donations, investment income and royalties: of $340.5 million revenue in 2025, $189.7 million came from contributions and $58.5 million from investments.

nationallotteryheritage.name: The National Lottery Heritage Fund
nationallotteryheritage.what: The UK distributor of National Lottery money for heritage, set up in 1994 as the Heritage Lottery Fund and renamed in 2019; head office in London.
nationallotteryheritage.money: A share of National Lottery proceeds raised from players, plus heritage funding it distributes for the UK and devolved governments.
nationallotteryheritage.arts: Since 1994 it has awarded over £9.9 billion of National Lottery and other funding to more than 54,000 projects.
nationallotteryheritage.address: 4th Floor, Cannon Bridge House, 25 Dowgate Hill, London EC4R 2YA

nationallottery|Belgium.name: Loterie Nationale / Nationale Loterij
nationallottery|Belgium.what: Belgium's largest lottery operator, founded in 1934 as the Colonial Lottery and a public-law limited company since 2002, under the Federal Public Service Finance.
nationallottery|Belgium.money: Sales of its lottery games and Scooore sports betting; it pays a monopoly fee to the federal treasury.
nationallottery|Belgium.arts: Parliament decides which projects and organisations receive its yearly subsidies.

nationalmuseumsofkenya.name: National Museums of Kenya
nationalmuseumsofkenya.what: A Kenyan state corporation under the Museums and Heritage Act 2006 that runs the country's museums, sites and monuments; its headquarters is on Museum Hill, Nairobi.
nationalmuseumsofkenya.money: Kenya's national government, through the National Treasury, pays staff salaries; admission fees and other earned income cover operating costs.

nationaltrustforhistoric.name: National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States
nationaltrustforhistoric.what: A privately funded nonprofit founded in 1949 by congressional charter and based in Washington, D.C.; it runs historic sites and campaigns to save historic places.
nationaltrustforhistoric.money: Contributions, 66.1% of US$104.9 million revenue in the year to June 2025, plus investment income and asset sales.

ndr.name: Norddeutscher Rundfunk
ndr.what: The public broadcaster for Hamburg, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, a public-law institution operating as NDR since 1 January 1956; based in Hamburg.
ndr.money: The broadcasting fee paid by households, collected by a joint agency of ARD, ZDF and Deutschlandradio, plus limited on-air advertising.

nec.name: NEC Corporation
nec.what: A Japanese IT and electronics company, founded in Tokyo in 1899 as Nippon Electric Company, a member of the Sumitomo Group with headquarters in Minato, Tokyo.
nec.money: Sales of IT services, telecom equipment and aerospace and defence systems: revenue ¥3.42 trillion in fiscal 2025.

nepalacademyoffinearts.name: Nepal Academy of Fine Arts
nepalacademyoffinearts.what: Nepal's national academy for the visual arts, set up by the legislative parliament on 13 April 2010 out of the Nepal Academy; it sits in Sita Bhawan, Naxal, Kathmandu.
nepalacademyoffinearts.money: Funds from the Government of Nepal plus revenue the academy generates itself.
nepalacademyoffinearts.arts: It has departments for painting, traditional arts, sculpture, folk art, handicrafts and architecture, and evaluates and awards artists.

nescafe.name: Nestlé S.A.
nescafe.what: A Swiss food and drink company based in Vevey, formed in 1905 from the Anglo-Swiss Condensed Milk Company and Henri Nestlé's firm; Nescafé is its instant coffee brand.
nescafe.money: Sales of coffee, baby food, dairy, confectionery, bottled water and pet food: revenue CHF 89.49 billion in 2025.

neubauerfamily.name: Neubauer Family Foundation
neubauerfamily.what: A private family foundation in Philadelphia founded by Joseph Neubauer, former chief executive of the food services company Aramark, and his wife Jeanette Lerman-Neubauer.
neubauerfamily.money: Money from Joseph and Jeanette Neubauer, invested: dividends and asset sales brought $9.8 million in fiscal 2024, when net assets were $361 million.
neubauerfamily.arts: It supports Jewish museums in Berlin, Warsaw and Israel, and paid $20.1 million in charitable grants in fiscal 2024.

newcarlsberg.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
newcarlsberg.what: A private foundation for the arts set up by charter on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia, based in Copenhagen.
newcarlsberg.money: Dividends from Carlsberg A/S shares, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, and returns on its other investments.
newcarlsberg.arts: It donates artworks to Danish museums, commissions site-specific art (decorative projects) and gives art awards.

newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.name: New York State Council on the Arts
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

nishat.name: Nishat Group
nishat.what: A Pakistani business group based in Lahore, founded in 1951 when Mian Muhammad Yahya and his three brothers set up Nishat Mills; chaired by Mian Muhammad Mansha.
nishat.money: Profits of its textile, cement, banking (MCB Bank), insurance (Adamjee), power, hotel and car assembly businesses; Nishat Mills is the flagship company.

nordea.name: Nordea-fonden
nordea.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1989 by the savings bank Sparekassen SDS when it became a limited company, named Nordea-fonden since 2008.
nordea.money: Returns on its assets, chiefly a stake of about 4.4 percent in Nordea Bank Abp. It gives over 80 percent of yearly returns to charity.
nordea.arts: Culture is one of its four areas of support, alongside health, exercise and nature, with a grant pool for culture houses (Kulturhuspuljen).
nordea.address: Heerings Gaard, Overgaden neden Vandet 11, 1414 Copenhagen K

nordeafonden.name: Nordea-fonden
nordeafonden.what: A Danish commercial foundation with a non-profit purpose, formed in 1989 from assets of the savings bank Sparekassen SDS; named Nordea-fonden since 2008, based in Copenhagen.
nordeafonden.money: Returns on its endowment, including a stake of about 4.4% in Nordea Bank Abp, built on Sparekassen SDS savers' capital.
nordeafonden.arts: It funds projects for nature and culture across Denmark and gives grants for study abroad; it expected to give about DKK 550 million in 2022.
nordeafonden.address: Heerings Gaard, Overgaden neden Vandet 11, 1414 København K

nordlb.name: Norddeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale
nordlb.what: A German Landesbank and public-law institution, trading under that name since 1 July 1970, owned by Lower Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and the regional savings banks; based in Hanover.
nordlb.money: Banking profits from corporate, real estate and aircraft finance; Lower Saxony (€1.5 billion) and the German savings banks association (€1.2 billion) recapitalised it in 2019.
nordlb.arts: In 2012 it sold Jeff Koons's sculpture Tulips for $33.7 million and said it would use the proceeds for a foundation for contemporary art in northern Germany.

nornickel.name: MMC Norilsk Nickel
nornickel.what: A Russian mining and metals company founded in 1993, controlled by Vladimir Potanin's Interros, with mines and smelters at Norilsk in Siberia; based in Moscow.
nornickel.money: Sales of nickel, palladium, copper, platinum and other metals: revenue $13.8 billion in 2025.

north.name: Foundation North
north.what: A community trust set up in 1988 to hold the Auckland Savings Bank (ASB) for Auckland and Northland; it was named ASB Community Trust until 2015.
north.money: An endowment from the sale of ASB to the Commonwealth Bank of Australia; it stood at over a billion New Zealand dollars in 2015.

northwestelhelp.name: Northwestel Inc.
northwestelhelp.what: The incumbent phone carrier of Canada's three territories, created by CN in 1979 and owned by BCE since 1988; BCE agreed in 2024 to sell it to Sixty North Unity.
northwestelhelp.money: Telephone, internet and long-distance fees from customers in Yukon, the Northwest Territories, Nunavut and northern British Columbia and Alberta.

nortonsimon.name: Norton Simon Foundation
nortonsimon.what: The older of two Pasadena foundations of the industrialist Norton Simon, founder of Hunt's Foods; a private foundation, tax-exempt since 1954, that owns part of his art collection.
nortonsimon.money: Investment income, with no new gifts in recent years: revenue $6.4 million and net assets $194.1 million in 2024.
nortonsimon.arts: It lends its works long term to the Norton Simon Museum, which Simon took over in 1974 when it was the Pasadena Art Museum.

nortonsimonart.name: Norton Simon Art Foundation
nortonsimonart.what: One of two Pasadena foundations of the industrialist Norton Simon, founder of Hunt's Foods; a private foundation, tax-exempt since 1957, that owns part of his art collection.
nortonsimonart.money: Investment income, with no new gifts in recent years: revenue $15.7 million and net assets $425.5 million in the year to November 2024.
nortonsimonart.arts: It lends its works long term to the Norton Simon Museum; in 2014 public filings put the two foundations' art at about $5 billion.

norwegianministryofculture|Norway.name: Kultur- og likestillingsdepartementet
norwegianministryofculture|Norway.short: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
norwegianministryofculture|Norway.what: Norway's government ministry for culture, media, sport and equality, set up in 1982 and renamed Ministry of Culture and Equality on 1 January 2022.

nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.name: Nottingham City Council
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.what: The unitary local authority for the city of Nottingham, under Labour control since 1991, with main offices at Loxley House.
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.money: UK government grants, including the Revenue Support Grant, and council tax.

nottinghamtrentuniversity.name: Nottingham Trent University
nottinghamtrentuniversity.what: A public university in Nottingham with roots in the Nottingham Government School of Design of 1843, a polytechnic from 1970 and a university since 1992.
nottinghamtrentuniversity.money: Mainly tuition fees: of about £434 million income in 2023-24, £378 million came from teaching and £22 million from research.

nrwcultureministry|Germany.name: Ministerium für Kultur und Wissenschaft des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen
nrwcultureministry|Germany.what: The culture and science ministry of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia in Düsseldorf, led by Minister Ina Brandes.
nrwcultureministry|Germany.arts: In June 2026 it granted about 18 million euros to Kultur Ruhr GmbH for the Ruhrtriennale, Chorwerk Ruhr, Tanzlandschaft Ruhr and Urbane Künste Ruhr.

nswgovernment|Australia.name: NSW Government
nswgovernment|Australia.what: The state government of New South Wales, Australia, led since March 2023 by the Labor Premier Chris Minns.
nswgovernment|Australia.money: The New South Wales state budget, which funds the arts through Create NSW and its Arts and Cultural Funding Program.
nswgovernment|Australia.renamed: The museum sentences mean the NSW Government as a whole, not its Premier's Department, the agency that leads the state public service.

ntgovernment|Australia.name: Northern Territory Government
ntgovernment|Australia.what: The executive government of Australia's Northern Territory, formed in 1978 when the Commonwealth granted the territory self-government; it sits at Parliament House, Darwin.
ntgovernment|Australia.money: Commonwealth grants supply about A$7.7 billion, or 72%, of its A$10.7 billion revenue (2026-27 budget); mining and petroleum royalties are another source.

ntteast.name: NTT EAST, Inc.
ntteast.what: A regional telecom operator for eastern Japan, set up on 1 July 1999 as a wholly owned subsidiary of the NTT holding company; based in Shinjuku, Tokyo.
ntteast.money: Fees for fixed-line telephone, optical fibre and other regional telecommunications services in eastern Japan.

nycarlsberg.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
nycarlsberg.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
nycarlsberg.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

nycarlsbergfondet.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
nycarlsbergfondet.what: A Danish art foundation set up on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia Jacobsen, operating under the Carlsberg Foundation in Copenhagen.
nycarlsbergfondet.money: Mainly dividends from shares in the brewer Carlsberg A/S.
nycarlsbergfondet.arts: It funds visual art, applied art and architecture in Denmark, including gifts of works to museums and decorative commissions.

nycculturalaffairs|USA.name: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs
nycculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.name: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.what: The New York City agency that funds non-profit culture in the five boroughs, a separate city agency since 1976.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.money: New York City's budget: an operating budget of $300 million in fiscal 2026, almost entirely city money.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.arts: Its Cultural Development Fund gave $74.3 million to 1,171 organisations in fiscal 2026.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.name: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government agency for culture, made a separate city department in 1976 under a commissioner appointed by the Mayor; its forerunner office dates from 1962.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget: $300.5 million for fiscal 2026.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.arts: It funds nonprofit arts groups, zoos, botanical gardens and historical and science museums in the five boroughs, and runs Materials for the Arts.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.address: 31 Chambers Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10007

nysca.name: New York State Council on the Arts
nysca.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
nysca.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
nysca.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

oak.name: Oak Foundation
oak.what: A charitable foundation set up in 1983 by Alan M. Parker, co-founder of the duty-free retailer DFS Group, and headquartered in Geneva.
oak.money: Resources from Alan Parker's interest in the Duty Free Shoppers business; it made about 1,000 grants totalling US$383 million in 2025.
oak.arts: Its Special Interest Programme funds the Jette Parker Artists Programme for young opera singers, which is marking 25 years.

ocm.name: One Caribbean Media Limited
ocm.what: A media group formed in December 2005 from Trinidad's Caribbean Communications Network and Barbados's Nation Corporation, based in Port of Spain; the state National Investment Fund owns 23%.
ocm.money: Advertising and sales of its newspapers, television and radio, including the Trinidad Express and TV6: revenue TT$301.17 million in 2024.
ocm.arts: It has sponsored the OCM Bocas Prize for Caribbean Literature since 2011.

oct.name: Overseas Chinese Town Enterprises Co.
oct.what: A Chinese state-owned enterprise founded in 1985 in Shenzhen, wholly owned by the State Council and supervised by its State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission.
oct.money: Profits of its tourism and culture parks, property development, hotels and Konka electronics: revenue RMB 110.3 billion in 2018.

ocw.name: Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap
ocw.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science in The Hague, led in 2026 by Minister Rianne Letschert.
ocw.money: The Dutch national budget: 57 billion euros of spending set for 2026.
ocw.arts: Its 2026 budget sets 2.7 billion euros for culture and media.

ofcaixageraldedepsitos.name: Culturgest, Fundação Caixa Geral de Depósitos
ofcaixageraldedepsitos.what: A private foundation set up by Caixa Geral de Depósitos, Portugal's state-owned bank; its venue in the bank's Lisbon head office opened in October 1993.
ofcaixageraldedepsitos.money: An annual allocation from Caixa Geral de Depósitos, which also made its €3.5 million initial endowment and provides its spaces.

ogasawara.name: Ogasawara Toshiaki Memorial Foundation
ogasawara.what: A Japanese public-interest foundation set up on 12 September 1986 by Toshiaki Ogasawara, founder of the fastener maker Nifco, as a science foundation; renamed in 2020.
ogasawara.money: Nifco shares from Toshiaki Ogasawara: 2 million at its founding and 5.94 million from his estate in 2020; basic assets ¥47.61 billion (March 2026).
ogasawara.arts: It began arts grants in 2020, for contemporary art research, translation, exchange and travel; its total grants in 2025 were ¥486.52 million.
ogasawara.address: Izumi Tamachi Building 4F, Shiba 5-27-6, Minato-ku, Tokyo

ohra.name: OHRA
ohra.what: A Dutch insurance brand founded in 1925, now a trade name of NN Group companies and, for health insurance, of the CZ group; its office is in Arnhem.
ohra.money: Premiums on non-life, life and health insurance it sells directly to customers by phone and online.

okayamacity|Japan.name: Okayama City
okayamacity|Japan.what: The capital of Okayama Prefecture in western Japan, founded on 1 June 1889 and a government-designated city since 1 April 2009.
okayamacity|Japan.money: Its fiscal 2026 general budget of ¥429.9 billion: city taxes ¥143.6 billion, national and prefectural grants ¥113.5 billion, local allocation tax ¥55.8 billion.

okayamagas.name: Okayama Gas Co., Ltd.
okayamagas.what: A city gas company founded in Okayama on 29 January 1910, supplying Okayama, Kurashiki, Akaiwa, Tamano, Soja and Hayashima.
okayamagas.money: Sales of city gas, gas appliances and pipe work; non-consolidated revenue was ¥24.81 billion in 2015.

omvzukunftspartner.name: OMV Aktiengesellschaft
omvzukunftspartner.what: Austria's integrated oil and gas company, founded on 3 July 1956 as Österreichische Mineralölverwaltung; the state holding ÖBAG owns 31.5% and Abu Dhabi's ADNOC 24.9%.
omvzukunftspartner.money: Sales of oil, natural gas, fuels and petrochemicals: revenue €24.3 billion and net income €1.52 billion in 2025.

onassis.name: Alexander S. Onassis Public Benefit Foundation
onassis.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
onassis.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
onassis.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

ontarioartscouncil|Canada.name: Ontario Arts Council
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Ontario government, created by provincial law in 1963 under Premier John Robarts; based in Toronto.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.money: The Government of Ontario, through its culture ministry.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.arts: It runs more than fifty funding programmes for Ontario artists and arts organisations.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.address: 121 Bloor Street East, 7th Floor, Toronto, ON M4W 3M5

opec.name: OPEC Fund for International Development
opec.what: An intergovernmental development finance institution set up on 28 January 1976 by the member states of OPEC; based in Vienna.
opec.money: Capital contributions from its member countries, plus bonds issued on capital markets under its Strategic Framework 2030.

opensociety.name: Open Society Foundations
opensociety.what: A grantmaking network founded by investor George Soros, begun with a Budapest foundation in 1984; the Open Society Institute was set up in New York in 1993.
opensociety.money: George Soros's personal fortune: he had given over $32 billion by 2017, including an $18 billion transfer announced that year.

oprahwinfreycharitable.name: Oprah Winfrey Charitable Foundation
oprahwinfreycharitable.what: A private foundation in Los Angeles with the television host Oprah Winfrey as trustee; tax-exempt since August 2010.
oprahwinfreycharitable.money: Gifts in some years ($35.2 million in 2018, $14.3 million in 2020) and investment income; net assets were $171.1 million at the end of 2024.

optus.name: Singtel Optus Pty Limited
optus.what: Australia's second-largest telecom company, owned by Singtel of Singapore; it grew from the satellite operator AUSSAT (1981) and gained a carrier licence in 1991.
optus.money: Mobile, home internet and fixed-line fees from over 10.7 million mobile customers: revenue A$8.05 billion in fiscal 2023.

oregoncommunity.name: Oregon Community Foundation
oregoncommunity.what: A statewide community foundation founded in 1973, with headquarters in Portland and offices in Baker City, Bend, Eugene, Medford and Salem.
oregoncommunity.money: Charitable funds set up by individuals, families, businesses and organisations: an endowment of US$3.02 billion in 2024, when it made $174 million in grants.
oregoncommunity.arts: Its Creative Heights Initiative funds Oregon arts and culture projects, with $1 million invested through its 2023 round.

orf.name: Österreichischer Rundfunk
orf.what: Austria's national public broadcaster, launched on 1 August 1955 and run from the ORF-Zentrum in Vienna.
orf.money: The ORF-Beitrag, a levy set by law on every Austrian address with an adult resident, plus limited on-air advertising.

osgf.name: Open Society Georgia Foundation
osgf.what: A Tbilisi grant-making foundation in the Open Society Foundations network since 1994, registered in Georgia in 1998; from 2024 its work continues as the Civil Society Foundation.
osgf.money: Grants from the Open Society network's Foundation Open Society Institute and Foundation to Promote Open Society, plus other donors.

otpbank.name: OTP Bank Nyrt.
otpbank.what: Hungary's largest commercial bank, established as OTP Bank on 1 March 1949 with roots in the First National Savings Bank of Pest of 1839; chaired by Sándor Csányi.
otpbank.money: Banking profits from retail and corporate clients in Hungary and subsidiaries across Central and Eastern Europe and Central Asia, such as Bulgaria's DSK Bank.

paizretailfamily.name: Paiz family
paizretailfamily.what: A Guatemalan business family; in 1928 Salvador Paiz's grandfather founded what became the Almacenes Paiz chain and later Walmart Centroamérica.
paizretailfamily.money: Retail: the Almacenes Paiz stores, later part of Walmart Centroamérica; Salvador Paiz now chairs the investment company Grupo PDC.
paizretailfamily.arts: The family's Fundación Paiz runs the Bienal de Arte Paiz, held since 1978.

palmacouncil|Spain.name: Ajuntament de Palma
palmacouncil|Spain.what: The municipal government of Palma, Mallorca, a city of 438,234 people in 2024, led by mayor Jaime Martínez Llabrés of the People's Party.
palmacouncil|Spain.money: The city's municipal budget, set at €626.67 million for 2026 and approved by the council in December 2025.

partnersincludeafricanculture.name: African Culture Fund
partnersincludeafricanculture.what: A pan-African non-profit trust set up in Bamako in February 2018 by African artists and cultural actors, registered in Mali under a headquarters agreement.
partnersincludeafricanculture.money: Contributions from African artists and cultural actors, and grants from DOEN, the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the Ford Foundation and Open Society Foundations.
partnersincludeafricanculture.arts: It finances artistic projects across Africa through calls for projects and trains cultural managers through its ACF Academy.

patio.name: Fondation Simón I. Patiño
patio.what: A Swiss foundation registered in Geneva in December 1958 to help Bolivian students and professors and to support cultural, social and ecological work in Bolivia.
patio.money: A fund of US$10 million set up when the Bolivian Patiño foundation ran short of money; the Patiño wealth came from Bolivian tin mining.
patio.arts: Its statutes include topping up the resources of the Fundación Universitaria Simón I. Patiño, created in Bolivia in 1931, and supporting literary and music prizes.

patriciagurdin.name: Patricia Gurdián de Ortiz
patriciagurdin.what: An art collector from León, Nicaragua, who founded the Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián in 1996 with Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga to promote the country's cultural development.
patriciagurdin.money: Grupo Promerica, the financial group of her co-founder, whose bank Banpro also supports the foundation's Managua art centre.
patriciagurdin.renamed: The atlas files her under Banpro, but the museum sentence names her as a founder of the Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián, not as the bank.

patronatopageshowsinterceramic.name: Internacional de Cerámica, S.A.B. de C.V.
patronatopageshowsinterceramic.what: A Mexican maker of ceramic and porcelain tiles and bath and kitchen products, founded in Chihuahua in 1978 by Óscar Almeida Chabre.
patronatopageshowsinterceramic.money: Sales of floor and wall tiles from plants in Chihuahua, Guanajuato and Garland, Texas, through showrooms and franchises in Mexico and abroad.

paulgettytrust.name: J. Paul Getty Trust
paulgettytrust.what: A trust founded in 1953 by J. Paul Getty, founder of Getty Oil, that runs the Getty Museum, Research Institute, Conservation Institute and Getty Foundation in Los Angeles.
paulgettytrust.money: An endowment of US$9.4 billion (2025) built on Getty's bequest, which included nearly $660 million in Getty Oil stock received in 1982.
paulgettytrust.arts: The Getty Foundation gives grants to museums and cultural institutions worldwide.

paulhamlyn.name: Paul Hamlyn Foundation
paulhamlyn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity started by publisher Paul Hamlyn in 1987 and in its current form since 2004; based in King's Cross, London.
paulhamlyn.money: An endowment from Paul Hamlyn's publishing fortune: a £50m gift in 1987 and about £308 million from his estate in 2001.
paulhamlyn.arts: It funds children and young people, with a focus on the arts.

pellerestates.name: Andrew Peller Limited
pellerestates.what: A Canadian wine producer listed in Toronto and based in Grimsby, Ontario, whose brands include Peller Estates; in June 2026 it agreed to be bought by Fairfax Financial.
pellerestates.money: Sales of wine, ciders and spirits, including through 101 company stores in Ontario; revenue was C$393.0 million in the year to 31 March 2026.

phillips.name: Phillips
phillips.what: An auction house founded in London in 1796, with head offices in London and New York and a UK holding company, Phillips Assets Ltd.
phillips.money: Fees on auction and private sales (UK turnover £89m in 2024), under a parent, Mercury Group Trading, controlled by Leonid Fridlyand and Leonid Strunin.

pinault.name: Artémis
pinault.what: The Pinault family's holding company, founded in Paris in 1992 by François Pinault and chaired by his son François-Henri Pinault since 2003.
pinault.money: Its holdings, chiefly 42.3% of the luxury group Kering, plus Christie's, Château Latour and other wine estates, Creative Artists Agency and Ponant cruises.
pinault.arts: It backs the Pinault Collection, which opened the Bourse de Commerce in Paris in 2021.

platinumbarjeel.name: Barjeel Art Foundation
platinumbarjeel.what: A non-profit art foundation in Sharjah, set up in 2010 by the Emirati writer and collector Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi to manage and show his collection of modern Arab art.
platinumbarjeel.money: It holds the personal collection of its founder, a member of Sharjah's ruling Al Qasimi family and chairman of the brokerage Barjeel Geojit Securities.
platinumbarjeel.arts: Since 2018 it has shown its collection in a long-term exhibition at the Sharjah Art Museum under a contract with the Sharjah Museums Authority.
platinumbarjeel.address: Al Saud Head Office Building, Level 2, Block B, Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Road, Muwailih Commercial, Sharjah

plenitude.name: Eni Plenitude S.p.A. Società Benefit
plenitude.what: An Italian energy company and Società Benefit controlled by Eni, registered in Milan and active in more than 15 countries.
plenitude.money: Energy sold to over 11 million European customers and power from about 6 GW of renewables; pro forma EBITDA about €1.1 billion in 2025.

pnc.name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
pnc.what: A US bank holding company in Pittsburgh, tracing to the Pittsburgh Trust and Savings Company of 1845 and formed as PNC by a 1982 merger.
pnc.money: Interest and fees from personal, small business and corporate banking through PNC Bank; revenue was US$21.49 billion in 2023.

polishcultureministry|UK.name: Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego
polishcultureministry|UK.short: Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
polishcultureministry|UK.what: Poland's government ministry for culture and national heritage, based in the Potocki Palace in Warsaw; Marta Cienkowska has been minister since 24 July 2025.

polygonhomes.name: Polygon Homes Ltd.
polygonhomes.what: A Metro Vancouver home builder in business since 1980, chaired by its major shareholder Michael Audain.
polygonhomes.money: Sales of the homes it builds and develops, more than 35,000 to date, from masterplanned communities to high-rise towers.
polygonhomes.address: Suite 900-1333 West Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6H 4C2

portomunicipality|Portugal.name: Câmara Municipal do Porto
portomunicipality|Portugal.what: The executive body of the municipality of Porto in Portugal, led by its president, Pedro Duarte.
portomunicipality|Portugal.money: The municipal budget, 491.3 million euros for 2026, raised mainly from local taxes such as the IMI property tax and from fees.

portugueseministryofculture|Portugal.name: Ministério da Cultura, Juventude e Desporto
portugueseministryofculture|Portugal.what: Portugal's government ministry for culture, youth and sport, created in June 2025 by the XXV Constitutional Government; Margarida Balseiro Lopes is minister.

power.name: Power Corporation of Canada
power.what: A Canadian holding company founded in 1925 and based in Montreal, controlled since 1968 by a group led by Paul Desmarais.
power.money: Its financial services holdings in insurance, retirement, wealth and asset management, which have included Great-West Life, Canada Life, IGM Financial and Mackenzie.

princeclaus.name: Prince Claus Fund
princeclaus.what: A Dutch fund set up in 1996 and named after Prince Claus of the Netherlands; it gives grants and awards to artists in places where culture is under pressure.
princeclaus.money: An annual subsidy from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
princeclaus.arts: Its Principal Award is worth €100,000; since 1996 it has supported almost 2,400 projects in 144 countries.

privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese private foundation in Lisbon, created on 18 July 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, the Armenian oil magnate who settled in Portugal.
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.arts: It runs the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum and the Gulbenkian Orchestra, founded in 1962.

privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.name: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.what: A private non-profit contemporary art foundation set up in Turin on 6 April 1995 by the collector Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, its president.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.money: Mainly public and private contributions: €275,872 public and €1,812,995 private in 2024, of €2,650,394 total revenue.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.arts: It runs venues in Turin and Guarene d'Alba, a sculpture park at Guarene and the Young Curators Residency Programme.

prohelvetia.name: Pro Helvetia
prohelvetia.what: The Swiss Confederation's arts foundation, set up by the Federal Council in 1939 and made a foundation under public law in 1949; based in Zurich.
prohelvetia.money: The Swiss federal budget, set by parliament in four-year Cultural Messages: CHF 186.9 million for 2025 to 2028.
prohelvetia.arts: In 2025 it approved 2,448 of 7,235 applications and put 86.9 percent of its funds directly into art and culture.

provinceofbc|Canada.name: Government of British Columbia
provinceofbc|Canada.what: The provincial government of British Columbia, Canada, led by a Premier and Cabinet answerable to the 93-member Legislative Assembly in Victoria.
provinceofbc|Canada.money: Provincial taxes, natural resource royalties and federal transfers; revenue was forecast at C$83.3 billion for 2025-26.

provinceofmanitoba|Canada.name: Government of Manitoba
provinceofmanitoba|Canada.what: The provincial government of Manitoba, Canada: a cabinet led by the premier and drawn from the elected Legislative Assembly, seated in Winnipeg.
provinceofmanitoba|Canada.money: Provincial taxes and federal transfers: Budget 2026 projects C$26,820 million of revenue for 2026/27, including C$9,657 million from the federal government.

qatarmuseums.name: Qatar Museums
qatarmuseums.what: A Qatari government entity founded in 2005 that runs the country's museums, chaired by Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani under the Amir's patronage.
qatarmuseums.arts: It oversees the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf, the National Museum of Qatar and the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum.

qattan.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattan.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattan.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattan.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qattantodate.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattantodate.what: An independent foundation for culture and education in Palestine and the Arab world, set up in 1993 by the Palestinian businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah.
qattantodate.money: Al-Qattan family money: in 2011 the founder put a quarter of his wealth, made through Al-Hani Construction and Trading, into the Al-Qattan Charitable Trust.
qattantodate.arts: It runs the Al-Qattan Cultural Centre in Ramallah, opened in June 2018 at a cost of $21 million, and a cultural centre in Gaza.

ralesfamily.name: Mitchell P. Rales and Emily Wei Rales
ralesfamily.what: Mitchell Rales co-founded the Danaher Corporation with his brother Steven in 1984 and founded Glenstone with his wife, Emily Wei Rales, in 2006.
ralesfamily.money: Mitchell Rales's fortune from Danaher, Colfax and Fortive, estimated at 4 billion dollars in 2025.
ralesfamily.arts: Mitchell Rales is a former president of the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
ralesfamily.renamed: The atlas name points at the Danaher Corporation, while the museum sentence means a gift from the Rales family.

realdania.name: Realdania
realdania.what: A Danish member-based philanthropic association created in 2000, when Realkredit Danmark sold its mortgage business in its merger with Danske Bank, based in Copenhagen.
realdania.money: Returns on investing the capital it kept from that deal; about 195,000 members own it.
realdania.arts: It funds projects in architecture, planning and the built environment.

regionecampania.name: Regione Campania
regionecampania.what: The regional government of Campania in southern Italy, seated in Naples and led by President Roberto Fico with a 60-member Regional Council.
regionecampania.money: The regional budget, over EUR 38.5 billion for 2026, almost 70% of it for health.
regionecampania.arts: Its 2026 budget raises cinema funding to EUR 6 million and live-performance funding to EUR 17 million.

regionelazio.name: Regione Lazio
regionelazio.what: The regional government of Lazio in central Italy, seated in Rome and led by President Francesco Rocca, with a Regional Council as its legislature.
regionelazio.money: The regional budget; its 2025 economic and financial plan set the 2025 to 2027 budget at about EUR 10 billion.

regionepiemonte.name: Regione Piemonte
regionepiemonte.what: The regional government of Piedmont, an Italian region with ordinary statute created in 1948 and operating since 1970; seat in Turin.
regionepiemonte.money: The regional budget, which draws on its own taxes such as IRAP, regional surcharges and car tax.

rgionbourgognefranchecomt.name: Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.what: The regional council of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, the French region formed on 1 January 2016 from Burgundy and Franche-Comté, seated in Besançon.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.money: A EUR 1.922 billion budget in 2025, led by EUR 699 million of national VAT revenue assigned by the French state.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.arts: Its 2025 budget gives EUR 33.7 million to culture and heritage.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.address: Hôtel de Région, 4 square Castan, 25000 Besançon

rgiongrandest.name: Région Grand Est
rgiongrandest.what: The regional council of Grand Est, the French region formed in 2016 from Alsace, Champagne-Ardenne and Lorraine, seated in Strasbourg.
rgiongrandest.money: Mostly national VAT shared out by the French state (53% of French regions' operating revenue in 2024); its planned 2026 budget is EUR 4.1 billion.

rgionsud.name: Région Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
rgionsud.what: The regional council of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, the south-eastern French region also called Région Sud, seated in Marseille.
rgionsud.money: Mainly a share of national VAT assigned by the French state; councillors adopted a EUR 3.2 billion budget for 2024.
rgionsud.arts: The 2024 budget gave EUR 67 million to arts and culture.

right:cohen.name: Steven A. Cohen
right:cohen.what: An American hedge fund manager, founder of Point72 Asset Management (2014, Stamford, Connecticut) and owner of the New York Mets.
right:cohen.money: His hedge fund fortune: S.A.C. Capital Advisors from 1992, which pleaded guilty to insider trading in 2013, then Point72.
right:cohen.arts: The Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation, started in 2001, has granted US$1.5 billion to health, education, arts and culture and New York projects.
right:cohen.wrong_match: The Aldrich and NYU Tisch sentences do not name Cohen or Point72; the MOCA sentence records that he left its board.

rolex.name: Rolex SA
rolex.what: A Geneva watchmaker founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis, owned since 1960 by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
rolex.money: Sales of Rolex and Tudor wristwatches by a company wholly owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private Swiss foundation.
rolex.arts: Its Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative, set up in 2002, pairs emerging artists with established ones and gives each protégé about $41,000.

russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.name: PJSC Novatek
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.what: Russia's second-largest natural gas producer after Gazprom, founded in August 1994 by Leonid Mikhelson, who chairs its management board; headquartered in Tarko-Sale with a head office in Moscow.
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.money: Sales of natural gas and petroleum products from fields in the Yamalo-Nenets region of West Siberia: revenue $17 billion in 2025.
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.arts: Mikhelson co-founded the V-A-C Foundation for contemporary art in 2009 with Teresa Iarocci Mavica.
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.wrong_match: The museum sentence names Novatek only to describe Leonid Mikhelson; the money reaches GES-2 through his V-A-C Foundation, not from the company.

safraeach.name: Edmond J. Safra Philanthropic Foundation
safraeach.what: A private foundation set up by the banker Edmond J. Safra, who died in 1999, and led by his widow Lily Safra for more than twenty years; registered in Geneva.
safraeach.money: An endowment from Edmond J. Safra's banking fortune; he founded Republic National Bank of New York and sold his holdings to HSBC in 1999.
safraeach.arts: Its arts grants have gone to the Courtauld Institute of Art, the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra and the Grand Théâtre de Genève.

sansebastincity|Spain.name: Ayuntamiento de San Sebastián / Donostiako Udala
sansebastincity|Spain.what: The city council of San Sebastián in the Basque Country, seated since 1945 in the former casino by La Concha bay and led by mayor Jon Insausti of the PNV.
sansebastincity|Spain.money: The municipal budget, about €517 million for 2025 and the first above €500 million, approved in December 2024.

sasktel.name: Saskatchewan Telecommunications Holding Corporation
sasktel.what: A telecommunications Crown corporation owned by the Government of Saskatchewan, founded in 1908 and based in Regina.
sasktel.money: Phone, wireless and internet services, with almost C$1.4 billion of annual revenue and C$104.7 million net income for 2025-26.

serbiasministryofculture|Serbia.name: Министарство културе Републике Србије
serbiasministryofculture|Serbia.what: Serbia's government ministry for culture and media regulation, established in 1991 and based in Belgrade; Nikola Selaković has been minister since 2 May 2024.

sigridrausingtrust.name: The Sigrid Rausing Trust
sigridrausingtrust.what: A London grant-making trust for human rights, open societies and the environment, established in 1995 by Sigrid Rausing.
sigridrausingtrust.money: Funds that Sigrid Rausing, granddaughter of Tetra Pak co-founder Ruben Rausing, moved into it from her Sea Foundation in 1996.

sintmartenslatem.name: Gemeente Sint-Martens-Latem
sintmartenslatem.what: The municipality of Sint-Martens-Latem in East Flanders, Belgium, made up of Sint-Martens-Latem and Deurle, with about 8,000 inhabitants and a history as a painters' village on the Leie.
sintmartenslatem.money: Local taxes and Flemish government transfers, including the Flemish Gemeentefonds, which gives Belgian municipalities about 20% of their operating resources.
sintmartenslatem.arts: It runs the Gemeentelijk Museum Gust De Smet in Deurle and invited Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens to show its collection there in 2022.

sloveniasministryofculture|Slovenia.name: Ministrstvo za kulturo
sloveniasministryofculture|Slovenia.what: The Slovenian government ministry for culture, based in Ljubljana.
sloveniasministryofculture|Slovenia.arts: It funds artist residencies in Berlin, London, New York and Vienna; its call for 2027 offers up to €100,000.

soichirofukutakes.name: Fukutake Foundation
soichirofukutakes.what: A Japanese public interest foundation set up on 27 February 2004 on Naoshima, Kagawa; Soichiro Fukutake is honorary chairman and Hideaki Fukutake chairman.
soichirofukutakes.money: Dividends on Benesse Holdings shares, held to fund its work (7.57% reported in 2020); basic assets of ¥41,366 million in 2026.
soichirofukutakes.arts: It runs museums and gives grants for art-based regional revitalisation in the Seto Inland Sea area.

spanishministryofculture|Spain.name: Ministerio de Cultura
spanishministryofculture|Spain.what: The Government of Spain's department for heritage, national museums, archives, libraries, books and film, headed by Minister Ernest Urtasun and based in Madrid.
spanishministryofculture|Spain.money: The Spanish state budget; its annual budget is €1.15 billion for 2026.

sparebankstiftelsendnb.name: Sparebankstiftelsen DNB
sparebankstiftelsendnb.what: A Norwegian foundation set up in 2002 when Sparebanken NOR became a share company, tracing to Christiania Sparebank of 1822, based in Oslo.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.money: Dividends on its stake of about 8.9% in DNB.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.arts: It buys art shown in Norwegian museums and lends instruments to musicians from a collection begun in 2006.

sparkassebremen.name: Die Sparkasse Bremen AG
sparkassebremen.what: An independent savings bank founded by Bremen citizens in 1825, run as a stock corporation owned by the Finanzholding der Sparkasse in Bremen, whose about 750 members represent Bremen's citizens.
sparkassebremen.money: Banking income from private and business customers, with total assets of more than 15 billion euros.

srp.name: Salt River Project
srp.what: A not-for-profit Arizona utility run by the Salt River Valley Water Users' Association, formed in 1903, and the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District.
srp.money: Electricity and water bills from more than 2 million people, including more than 1.2 million electric customers in central Arizona.

stadsdeeloost.name: Gemeente Amsterdam, Stadsdeel Oost
stadsdeeloost.what: One of Amsterdam's city districts, covering areas such as Oud-Oost and the Indische Buurt, run by a three-member district board acting for the city's executive.
stadsdeeloost.money: Budgets set in the Amsterdam municipal budget, which the district board allocates to its tasks.

statenskunstfond.name: Statens Kunstfond
statenskunstfond.what: Denmark's state arts foundation, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, administered by a Ministry of Culture agency.
statenskunstfond.money: Danish state funds allocated by the culture ministry.
statenskunstfond.arts: Its 16 expert committees award grants to more than 6,400 artists and art projects a year from about 15,700 applications.

stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.name: Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kunst Baden-Württemberg
stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.what: The Baden-Württemberg state ministry for universities, research and the arts, set up in 1978 in Stuttgart; Petra Olschowski has been minister since 28 September 2022.
stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.money: The budget of the State of Baden-Württemberg; the ministry's budget was about €5.74 billion in 2021.
stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.arts: It is responsible for the state's universities, university hospitals and many research bodies, and for arts institutions of Baden-Württemberg.

stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.name: Land Baden-Württemberg
stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.what: The government of the German federal state of Baden-Württemberg, founded on 25 April 1952, with its Staatsministerium (state chancellery) in Stuttgart.
stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.money: The state budget set by the Landtag; the draft for 2025 and 2026 planned just over EUR 136 billion of spending in total.
stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.arts: Its arts funding runs through the Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts (Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kunst).

stateoflowersaxony|Germany.name: Niedersächsisches Ministerium für Wissenschaft und Kultur
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.short: Lower Saxony Ministry for Science and Culture
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.what: The science and culture ministry of the German state of Lower Saxony in Hanover, led since 8 November 2022 by Minister Falko Mohrs.
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.money: The state budget of Lower Saxony.

stavrosniarchos.name: Stavros S. Niarchos Foundation for Charity
stavrosniarchos.what: A philanthropic foundation set up in 1996 after the death of Greek shipping magnate Stavros Niarchos, with offices in Athens, New York and Monaco.
stavrosniarchos.money: An endowment from Stavros Niarchos's shipping fortune; for many years he owned the world's largest private fleet, over 80 tankers and other vessels.
stavrosniarchos.arts: Arts and culture is one of its four grant priorities; since 1996 it has committed nearly $4 billion to grantees in 138 countries.

stichtingdoen.name: Stichting DOEN
stichtingdoen.what: A Dutch foundation set up more than 30 years ago by the Postcode Loterij to fund small, innovative initiatives.
stichtingdoen.money: Lottery proceeds: EUR 24.3 million from the Postcode Loterij and EUR 7.2 million from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
stichtingdoen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and cultural projects in 2025.

swedishartscouncil|Sweden.name: Statens kulturråd
swedishartscouncil|Sweden.what: A Swedish government agency under the Ministry of Culture that distributes state cultural grants, based at Filmhuset in Stockholm.
swedishartscouncil|Sweden.money: Appropriations from the Swedish state budget, set each year in the government's regleringsbrev.

tamayo.name: Fundación Olga y Rufino Tamayo, A.C.
tamayo.what: A Mexican civil association formalised on 31 October 1989 by the painter Rufino Tamayo and his wife Olga to study and show international contemporary art.
tamayo.money: Contributions from its members; with the Board of Trustees and the Círculo Contemporáneo it is one of the benefactor circles that support the Museo Tamayo.

terraforamericanart.name: Terra Foundation for American Art
terraforamericanart.what: A private foundation for American art set up in 1978 by Daniel J. Terra, founder of Lawter Chemicals, with offices in Chicago and Paris.
terraforamericanart.money: An endowment that pays for its grants; its assets were US$582 million in 2020.
terraforamericanart.arts: It closed its Chicago museum in 2004 to give grants and lend its collection; in 2012 it gave US$7.6 million.

thompson.name: The James H.W. Thompson Foundation
thompson.what: A Thai foundation set up in 1976 by the court-appointed administrator of Jim Thompson's property, under the royal patronage of Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.
thompson.money: Jim Thompson's Bangkok house and art collection, turned over to it in 1976.
thompson.arts: It runs the Jim Thompson Art Center, artist residencies and grants for preserving Thai art and culture.

tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.name: Mori Building Co., Ltd.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.what: A Tokyo property developer founded on 2 June 1959, grown out of Mori Fudosan, which Taikichiro Mori set up in 1955.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.money: Developing, leasing and managing offices, homes, shops and hotels; the Mori family owns 95.94%.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.arts: It opened the Mori Arts Center, with an art museum, on the upper floors of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower in 2003.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 106-6155

tommeetippee.name: Mayborn Group Limited
tommeetippee.what: A baby products company in Newcastle upon Tyne, incorporated in 1946, that owns the Tommee Tippee brand; 3i agreed in 2016 to sell it to China's Shanghai Jahwa United.
tommeetippee.money: Sales of Tommee Tippee baby feeding products; 2015 sales were £130 million, about 60 percent from international markets.
tommeetippee.address: Mayborn House, Balliol Business Park, Benton Lane, Newcastle upon Tyne NE12 8EW

torontoartscouncil|Canada.name: Toronto Arts Council
torontoartscouncil|Canada.what: Toronto's city-wide public funding body for the arts, created in 1974; a charitable organization working under an arm's-length funding agreement with the City of Toronto.
torontoartscouncil|Canada.money: An annual appropriation from the City of Toronto of about C$25 million.
torontoartscouncil|Canada.address: 26 Grand Trunk Crescent, Suite 200, Toronto, ON M5J 3A9

tunisair.name: Société Tunisienne de l'Air
tunisair.what: Tunisia's national airline, formed by the government in 1948 and based near Tunis-Carthage International Airport.
tunisair.money: Ticket sales, with turnover of TND 1,627 million in 2025; the state holds 64.86% and three state funds 9.56%.

unesco.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
unesco.what: A specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1945, with 194 member states and headquarters in Paris.
unesco.money: Assessed contributions that member states must pay, plus voluntary contributions from governments, international bodies, companies and other donors.

uniqlo.name: Fast Retailing Co., Ltd.
uniqlo.what: A Japanese retail holding company incorporated in 1963 by Hitoshi Yanai, owner of Uniqlo and GU, with its head office in Yamaguchi and an office in Tokyo.
uniqlo.money: Clothing sales, chiefly Uniqlo: revenue of 3.9633 trillion yen in the year to August 2026.

uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.name: Friends of the Ixchel Museum Inc
uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.what: A US charity established in 1984 to promote the Maya textile tradition of Guatemala and the Ixchel Museum in Guatemala City; registered in Princeton, New Jersey.
uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.money: Contributions from members and donors: $45,631 of its $45,638 revenue in 2025.
uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.arts: It funds renovations, field research and publications for the Ixchel Museum.

usfincaviga.name: Finca Vigía Foundation
usfincaviga.what: A US nonprofit in Boston founded in 2002 by Jenny and Frank Phillips to restore Ernest Hemingway's house and papers at Finca Vigía, Cuba.
usfincaviga.money: Donations: contributions made up all $368,460 of its revenue in 2024.
usfincaviga.arts: It has conserved and digitized more than 10,000 Hemingway documents and built a conservation centre with archival storage at the Finca.

valeculturalinstitute.name: Instituto Cultural Vale
valeculturalinstitute.what: The cultural institute of Vale, the Brazilian mining company, created in 2020 and based in Rio de Janeiro.
valeculturalinstitute.money: Money from Vale, a global mining company headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, which reported revenue of US$38.4 billion in 2025.
valeculturalinstitute.arts: It runs the Memorial Minas Gerais Vale, Museu Vale, Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão and Casa da Cultura de Canaã dos Carajás, and the Vale Música programme.
valeculturalinstitute.address: Praia de Botafogo 186, Botafogo, Rio de Janeiro

vancleef.name: Van Cleef & Arpels
vancleef.what: A French jewellery house founded in Paris in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, owned by the luxury group Richemont since 1999.
vancleef.money: Sales of jewellery through 155 stores, as part of Richemont.

velmakimbell.name: Velma Fuller Kimbell
velmakimbell.what: Velma Fuller Kimbell (1887 to 1982), wife of the Fort Worth businessman Kay Kimbell, with whom she set up the Kimbell Art Foundation; she co-chaired its board.
velmakimbell.money: Her share of the Kimbells' community property, built on Kay Kimbell's milling, grocery and oil firms, given to the foundation after his death in 1964.
velmakimbell.renamed: The atlas name points at the Kimbell Art Foundation, but the museum sentence means Velma Kimbell's own gift of her share of the couple's property.

vgc.name: Vlaamse Gemeenschapscommissie
vgc.what: The body that represents the Flemish authorities in the Brussels-Capital Region, created by the special law of 12 January 1989 and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
vgc.money: A dotation from the Flemish government's budget, EUR 30,588,000 in 2025, plus EUR 1,116,000 a year for community infrastructure.
vgc.arts: It runs more than 20 Dutch-language public libraries, including Muntpunt, and 22 community centres in Brussels.

vriendenloterij.name: VriendenLoterij N.V.
vriendenloterij.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterij.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterij.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vsbfonds.name: VSBfonds
vsbfonds.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht named after the Verenigde Spaarbank (VSB), formed in 1983 from 19th-century Nutsspaarbanken savings banks.
vsbfonds.money: Returns on capital held by Stichting VSB Vermogensfonds, built from the VSB shares the fund owned after the bank merged into Fortis in 1990.

walmart.name: Walmart Inc.
walmart.what: A US retailer founded in 1962 by the brothers Sam and Bud Walton, running Walmart stores and Sam's Club, headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas.
walmart.money: Retail sales; total revenue was US$713.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

warholfdn.name: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts
warholfdn.what: A New York nonprofit set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which also serves as the artist's estate.
warholfdn.money: An endowment built from Warhol's assets, plus income from licensing and selling his works.
warholfdn.arts: It has given more than US$300 million in cash grants to over 1,000 arts organisations in 49 states and abroad.
warholfdn.address: 65 Bleecker Street, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10012

wesfarmersarts.name: Wesfarmers Limited
wesfarmersarts.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmersarts.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmersarts.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.
wesfarmersarts.address: Level 14, Brookfield Place Tower 2, 123 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 6000

wienerstdtische.name: Wiener Städtische Versicherung AG
wienerstdtische.what: An Austrian insurer founded in Vienna in 1824, the largest single company in the Vienna Insurance Group.
wienerstdtische.money: Insurance premiums, about EUR 3,196.2 million gross; the Wiener Städtische Versicherungsverein is the group's main shareholder.

winnipegartscouncil|Canada.name: Winnipeg Arts Council
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.what: A not-for-profit charity that the City of Winnipeg charges with distributing its arts funding and managing its Public Art Policy.
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.money: City arts funding of C$4.65 million in 2025, plus C$258,570 for five city-designated museums.

wirth.name: Hauser & Wirth AG
wirth.what: A commercial gallery for modern and contemporary art, founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.
wirth.money: Its gallery business for more than 80 artists and estates, among them the estates of Louise Bourgeois and Philip Guston.
wirth.arts: It runs art centres in Somerset, opened in 2014, and on Menorca's Illa del Rei, opened in 2021.

wolfson.name: The Wolfson Foundation
wolfson.what: A UK grant-making charity set up in 1955 by Isaac Wolfson, chairman of Great Universal Stores, with his wife and son Leonard; based in London.
wolfson.money: Its endowment, just under £1 billion in 2024, when it spent £44 million on charitable activities.

wrth.name: Würth Group
wrth.what: A family-owned German group selling fastening and assembly materials, founded by Adolf Würth in Künzelsau in 1945 and led by his son Reinhold Würth from 1954.
wrth.money: Sales through more than 400 companies in 80 countries, EUR 20.7 billion in 2025.
wrth.arts: Its Kunsthalle Würth reopened in October 2026 for its 25th anniversary.

zwirner.name: David Zwirner
zwirner.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in New York in 1993 by the German-born dealer David Zwirner, with galleries in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris and Hong Kong.
zwirner.money: Sales of works by the more than seventy artists and estates it represents, in the primary and secondary art markets.
